## Candidate 1: Global one-mode prime logarithm operator

### CONSTRUCTION

Let P be the primes and let H=l2(P), A e_p=(log p)e_p, and U_t=exp(i t A). For a test function phi define U(phi)=integral phi(t) U_t dt, so U(phi)e_p=hat(phi)(log p). Inputs are only primes and logarithms; no zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The global l2(P) space replaces local transverse Z_p^m fibers and separate leafwise cohomology sectors. There is no scale q; the diagonal generator supplies lengths log p directly. The proposed replacement for Assumption (iv) is global diagonal spectral control: one mode per prime.

### ORBITS

There are no nonstationary closed orbits: U_t is a spectral representation, not the Koopman flow of a space with periodic leaves. The intended labels are formal: p=2 has log 2 and 2 log 2; p=3 has log 3 and 2 log 3. They are eigenvalue labels, not primitive geometric orbits, and no Poincare map or Lefschetz sign exists. Gate ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR AND ARCHIMEDEAN DATA

No transverse return map produces p^{-m}, and no stationary archimedean point with exponent -2 exists. A critical-line twist or appended archimedean term would be external data, not generated by this construction.

### SPECTRUM AND TRACE CLASS

The spectrum is global and diagonal, avoiding a direct sum of full circle spectra only by removing the geometric orbit model. Formally,
Tr U(phi)=sum_p hat(phi)(log p), and the trace norm is sum_p |hat(phi)(log p)|. Gate 1 requires this to be finite for every phi in C_c-infinity((0,infinity)); the construction provides no such estimate, and it still would not be a geometric Lefschetz trace. Thus TRACE fails.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, log p, the Hilbert space l2(P), the diagonal generator, and Fourier transformation. No zeta-zero locations or RH assumptions are used.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). A global diagonal operator can list prime logarithms without creating a flow whose Lefschetz trace has prime powers. This candidate replaces the non-trace-class prime-sector object but loses the geometric data required by Gate 1.

### FAILURE CLASS

Spectral encoding is not geometric orbit realization. The next candidate must retain genuine primitive closed orbits of lengths log p while using a genuinely global, non-direct-sum trace-class mechanism and an explicit stationary archimedean point with exponent -2.

## Candidate 2: Compact prime bouquet with a common archimedean junction

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, take a circle C_p of circumference log p and identify one marked point on every circle to a single vertex v. Let X be the resulting countable bouquet with the path metric. On each open edge use unit-speed translation toward the vertex and continue through the vertex by a fixed Kirchhoff routing rule. Add v as a stationary orbit with a one-dimensional transverse linear model of exponent kappa=-2. Use the finite graph cohomology complex of the bouquet, tensored with a fixed finite-dimensional transverse fiber, and impose the Kirchhoff matching condition at v. The construction uses only the primes, their logarithms, and the exponent -2.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The common junction and its finite transverse fiber replace the separate Z_p^m local transversals. There is no single scale q. The Kirchhoff condition is intended to replace Assumption (iv): it is supposed to force globally controlled harmonic data while retaining a finite transverse sector. Unlike Candidate 1, this is a genuine geometric flow model with periodic loops.

### ORBITS

For p=2, the circle gives one primitive loop of length log 2 and its first two iterates have lengths log 2 and 2 log 2. For p=3, the corresponding lengths are log 3 and 2 log 3. If the vertex routing lets a trajectory leave one circle and enter another, concatenating the p=2 and p=3 loops produces closed paths of lengths log 2+log 3 and 2 log 2+log 3, with further arbitrary words. These are not prime powers. The Lefschetz signs of the mixed paths are products of routing signs and cannot make the paths disappear geometrically. If routing is chosen to forbid every switch, each C_p is dynamically invariant and the model reduces to the forbidden direct sum of prime sectors. Therefore ORBITS fails in both cases.

### MODULAR FACTORS

A circle return map with a transverse scalar p^-1 can produce p^-m for the p-loop iterates, but a common junction does not preserve a separate p-labelled return map along mixed words. The mixed return products carry products of local factors rather than the required single-prime sequence. If no switching is allowed, the local factors are available but the direct-sum obstruction returns.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The vertex v supplies a stationary point with transverse exponent -2 by construction. Its local geometric kernel can produce the formal factor (1-e^-2t)^-1. This is the one Gate component that the candidate explicitly supplies.

### SPECTRUM

The graph is globally connected when switching is allowed, so the spectrum is not a direct sum. When switching is forbidden, the cohomology decomposes into the direct sum over circles plus the vertex sector.

### TRACE CLASS

In the connected case, every allowed switch creates mixed periodic words. Their number grows at least exponentially in word length whenever two prime loops can be concatenated, so the periodic-orbit side is not the required prime-only trace. In the no-switch case, the prime circle blocks remain and the established trace divergence reappears. A finite-dimensional junction fiber cannot cancel an infinite positive trace contribution without changing the orbit coefficients; an infinite junction fiber would require a separate trace-class theorem and does not remove the mixed-word dichotomy.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the prime set, circle lengths log p, a common vertex, a routing/Kirchhoff rule, a finite transverse fiber, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** The candidate has genuine prime loops and an explicit archimedean point, but global coupling produces forbidden composite closed paths; prohibiting coupling reduces it to the already-failed prime direct sum.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Globalized bouquet creates forbidden mixed return paths.** In a connected recurrent geometry, two primitive loops can be concatenated into non-prime closed paths. Removing all such paths forces invariant prime components and restores the trace-class obstruction.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 3

The next candidate must provide global trace-class cohomology without a common recurrent junction or any mechanism that permits concatenated prime loops. It must preserve prime-loop geometry through a genuinely nonlocal construction rather than a connected graph routing rule.

## Candidate 3: Prime loops joined only at an asymptotic end

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, take a circle C_p of circumference log p and attach to one marked point a half-infinite corridor E_p=(0,infinity). Identify all corridor ends at a single ideal point v_infinity in the one-point compactification, but do not identify any finite corridor points. The flow translates each C_p periodically and moves along E_p toward the common ideal end; v_infinity is stationary and carries a transverse exponent kappa=-2. Use leafwise L2 cohomology with decay at the ideal end and matching only through the common asymptotic boundary value. The construction is zero-independent.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The corridors and their common end replace the separate Z_p^m transverse systems. There is no common finite scale q. Decay at infinity replaces Assumption (iv): it is intended to suppress transverse harmonic multiplicity and make the global cohomology trace class while allowing a connected ambient space.

### ORBITS

For p=2 and p=3, the circles give primitive lengths log 2 and log 3 and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. Because the corridors are directed toward the ideal end and have no return map, no trajectory can leave C_p, travel through the end, and return to C_q as a finite periodic orbit. Thus no mixed finite closed paths are created. The prime orbit list is preserved locally, but the asymptotic attachment is not a mechanism producing new recurrent Lefschetz data.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Assigning transverse return multiplier p^-1 on C_p gives the desired p^-m for the local prime iterates. The asymptotic corridors have no return map and contribute no additional modular factors. This part can be specified consistently, but it does not solve the global trace problem.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The ideal point v_infinity is stationary and is assigned transverse exponent -2. Its local stationary contribution is formally the required kernel (1-e^-2t)^-1, subject to the usual local trace construction.

### SPECTRUM

The flow is topologically connected only through the ideal end. Since no finite trajectory returns through that end, the reduced leafwise cohomology and the smeared flow decompose into the prime sectors plus the stationary end sector. The apparent connectedness is therefore asymptotic rather than recurrent.

### TRACE CLASS

For a fixed Weil-class phi, the prime-loop sectors retain the same infinitely many low-frequency contributions as independent prime circles. The asymptotic matching condition can remove boundary modes or identify a finite-dimensional subspace, but it does not alter the nonzero Fourier spectrum on infinitely many prime loops. Consequently the trace norm still contains the divergent sum of prime-sector contributions. If the end is given a return mechanism strong enough to couple those sectors, finite mixed recurrent paths reappear and violate the prime-only orbit condition. Hence the candidate fails trace class in the no-return realization, and fails the orbit condition in the returning realization.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, circle lengths log p, directed corridors, the ideal common end, decay conditions, local multipliers p^-1, and the stationary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE)** in the asymptotic no-return version; **FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE)** if the end is modified to permit return. The construction separates global topology from recurrent dynamics, but the nonrecurrent connection is invisible to the ordinary periodic trace.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Asymptotic-only connectivity is trace-invisible.** A connection through an end that no finite orbit can traverse may make the ambient space connected, but it cannot change the prime-sector trace. A recurrent connection restores mixed closed paths.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 4

The next candidate must produce a genuinely global trace-class cohomology effect without finite switching, asymptotic-only attachment, or a direct-sum decomposition. It must specify a recurrent global mechanism whose closed-orbit trace remains exactly prime-indexed.

## Candidate 4: Global diagonal quotient of prime-circle cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

Start with the prime-circle flow
\\[
X=\\bigsqcup_p C_p,\\qquad |C_p|=\\log p,
\\]
and let the leafwise cohomology model be
\\[
\\mathcal H=\\bigoplus_p L^2(C_p)\\otimes E,
\\]
where E is a fixed finite-dimensional transverse space. Choose a nonzero summable vector
\\[
w=(w_p)_p\\in\\ell^2(P),\\qquad w_p=p^{-1},
\\]
and remove the single global matched mode generated by w: define \\(\\mathcal H_4\\) as the orthogonal complement of the closed span of the corresponding rank-one vector in the prime-sector coefficient space, tensored with the circle modes. The flow preserves this subspace because the quotient acts only on the prime-sector coefficient. Add a separate stationary point with transverse exponent -2. This is a genuine global quotient rather than a new prime-to-prime flow.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The prime-sector coefficient space and its one-dimensional quotient replace the separate transverse Z_p^m data. The weight w supplies a global matching condition in place of Assumption (iv): only coefficient combinations orthogonal to w are retained. The local circles and their return multipliers are kept unchanged.

### ORBITS

The underlying flow still has one primitive orbit for each p. For p=2, the first two iterates have lengths log 2 and 2 log 2; for p=3, they have lengths log 3 and 2 log 3. No finite orbit switching is introduced, so no mixed lengths appear. The geometric orbit list and local Lefschetz signs can be retained before quotienting.

However, the quotient changes the cohomological multiplicity of every prime orbit. The global removed mode has nonzero component at every prime, so its Lefschetz contribution is distributed across all prime orbits rather than being a local acyclic cancellation. The required coefficient +1 for every prime iterate is therefore not automatically preserved.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local transverse multiplier p^-1 remains available on each unquotiented circle mode and gives p^-m for its iterates. The global quotient removes a nonlocal component, so its correction to the supertrace is not represented by a local transverse Poincare determinant. If the quotient is arranged to have zero trace effect, it cannot repair the trace divergence.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A separate stationary point with exponent -2 supplies the formal archimedean kernel. The quotient does not interact with that point, so this component is unchanged.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum remains a prime-indexed direct sum after removal of one global coefficient direction. The quotient is finite-codimensional in the prime coefficient factor and does not create recurrent cross-prime paths.

### TRACE CLASS

Let A_p(phi) denote the smeared prime-circle block for a fixed nonzero Weil-class test function. The unquotiented trace norm is the divergent sum over p of the block trace norms. Removing one rank-one global mode changes the operator by at most a rank-one or summable trace-class term on the coefficient factor. If the quotient were trace class after this removal, then adding back the removed trace-class mode would make the original prime direct sum trace class, contradicting the established divergence. Thus the quotient cannot repair ordinary trace class.

If instead the removed mode is chosen non-summably so that it could cancel the divergent prime contribution, the quotient is not a bounded Hilbert-space quotient and the construction becomes a regularized difference, forbidden by Gate 1. The trace condition therefore fails.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, prime-circle lengths, local multipliers p^-1, the explicit summable vector w_p=p^-1, the orthogonal quotient, and the stationary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** The quotient preserves prime geometry and supplies the archimedean point, but a finite-rank or summable global identification cannot remove the divergent prime-circle trace. A nonsummable identification ceases to be an ordinary Hilbert-space quotient.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Finite/global quotient cannot remove extensive prime trace.** Removing a bounded finite-dimensional or trace-class transverse direction cannot turn a non-trace-class arithmetic direct sum into a trace-class operator; an effective cancellation must itself be non-trace-class or regularized.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 5

The next candidate must replace the entire prime-circle cohomology, not merely quotient a finite or summable subspace. It must retain geometric prime orbits while making the full cohomology globally trace class through a mechanism that is not an additive correction, finite quotient, or direct-sum decomposition.

## Candidate 5: Prime-weighted Hilbert cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

Keep the disjoint prime circles C_p of circumference log p, with a local transverse return multiplier p^-1 and a stationary archimedean point of exponent -2. Replace the ordinary direct-sum Hilbert norm by
\\[
\\|(v_p)_p\\|_{\\mathrm{wt}}^2=\\sum_p p^{-2}\\|v_p\\|_{L^2(C_p)\\otimes E}^2,
\\]
where E is a fixed finite-dimensional transverse space. The flow acts by translation on each C_p and preserves the weighted norm. The weights are explicit arithmetic data and use no zeros.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The weighted prime-sector Hilbert space replaces the unweighted leafwise cohomology sum. The scale q remains replaced by the local periods log p, and the weighted harmonic norm is proposed as the analogue of Assumption (iv): it is intended to suppress large-prime transverse multiplicity without changing local orbit dynamics.

### ORBITS

The geometry has exactly one primitive orbit for each p. For p=2 the first two iterates have lengths log 2 and 2 log 2; for p=3 they have lengths log 3 and 2 log 3. The local return multipliers p^-1 give the intended p^-m factors. The archimedean stationary point is separate. Gate ORBITS passes at the geometric level.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The transverse return map on the p-sector has determinant multiplier p^-1, so its m-th iterate supplies p^-m in the negative-time normalization. The Hilbert weight p^-2 is not used as a Lefschetz factor; it only changes the norm.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary point with transverse exponent -2 is included explicitly and is intended to contribute the factor (1-e^-2t)^-1.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is still a direct sum of the full circle spectra, with only the Hilbert norm rescaled sector by sector. There is no global recurrent coupling.

### TRACE CLASS

Define
\\[
(Jv)_p=p^{-1}v_p.
\\]
Then J is a unitary map from the weighted Hilbert direct sum to the ordinary Hilbert direct sum. The weighted flow is conjugate to the unweighted flow:
\\[
J U_t^{\\mathrm{wt}} J^{-1}=U_t^{\\mathrm{unwt}},
\\qquad
J U(\\phi)^{\\mathrm{wt}} J^{-1}=U(\\phi)^{\\mathrm{unwt}}.
\\]
Trace-class membership and trace norm are invariant under unitary conjugacy. Since the unweighted prime-circle smeared operator is not trace class for the established test class, the weighted operator is not trace class either. The arithmetic weights have changed coordinates, not the operator's singular-value density.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, prime-circle periods log p, local multipliers p^-1, the weighted Hilbert norm p^-2, a finite transverse fiber, and the stationary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** The weighted norm does not create a new trace-class mechanism; it is unitarily equivalent to the original direct-sum representation. The orbit and modular data survive, but ordinary trace class does not.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Hilbert-weight reparametrization leaves trace class invariant.** Any positive sector rescaling that is implemented by an invertible unitary identification cannot change the trace-class property of the smeared flow.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 6

The next candidate must change the operator or cohomology spectrum itself, not merely the Hilbert norm. It must preserve one prime orbit and its exact Lefschetz contribution while reducing the global spectral multiplicity through a genuinely non-unitary, geometrically defined mechanism.

## Candidate 6: Constant-mode compression of every prime circle

### CONSTRUCTION

Let X be the disjoint union of circles C_p of circumference log p, with local transverse multiplier p^-1 and a separate stationary archimedean point of exponent -2. On each circle, replace the full leafwise \\(L^2(C_p)\\) cohomology by its harmonic constant subspace
\\[
H_p^0=\\operatorname{span}\\{1_{C_p}\\}.
\\]
Let
\\[
\\mathcal H_6=\\bigoplus_p H_p^0
\\]
and let the flow act by translation on the circles. Since constants are invariant, the induced cohomological flow on every H_p^0 is the identity.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The constant-mode projection is a non-unitary spectral compression, unlike Candidate 5's norm rescaling. It replaces the transverse/cohomological multiplicity by one mode per prime and is intended as the analogue of Assumption (iv): all nonconstant modes are removed by harmonic projection. The geometric prime circles and their local return maps are retained in the ambient space.

### ORBITS

The ambient geometry still has primitive loops of lengths log p. For p=2 the first two lengths are log 2 and 2 log 2; for p=3 they are log 3 and 2 log 3. But the reduced cohomology sees only constant functions, on which translation has no period-sensitive eigenvalue. Its operator trace cannot distinguish log 2 from log 3. Thus the orbit geometry and the reduced cohomological trace are no longer compatible with the required Lefschetz formula. Gate ORBITS fails as a trace-realization condition.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The ambient transverse multiplier p^-1 remains assigned to the circle return map, but the constant-mode cohomology has no nontrivial transverse spectrum from which the iterate coefficient can be recovered. The factor is therefore external to the compressed operator.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary point with exponent -2 is included and can formally supply the archimedean kernel.

### SPECTRUM

The reduced spectrum is one identity eigenmode for every prime, plus the archimedean sector. It is not a full circle spectrum, but it remains an infinite direct sum over primes.

### TRACE CLASS

For a test function phi, the compressed flow is
\\[
U_6(\\phi)|_{H_p^0}=\\left(\\int \\phi(t)\\,dt\\right)I_{H_p^0}.
\\]
Choose any nonnegative nonzero phi in C_c^\\infty((0,infty)). Then its integral is strictly positive, and
\\[
\\|U_6(\\phi)\\|_1
=\\sum_p\\left|\\int\\phi(t)\\,dt\\right|
=+\\infty.
\\]
Therefore the compressed operator is not trace class. The compression removed Fourier multiplicity but left one identical identity mode per prime; it cannot encode the distinct prime periods.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, circle periods log p, local return multipliers p^-1, harmonic projection to constants, and the stationary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** Constant-mode compression makes the sector spectrum too small: it removes the period information and still leaves infinitely many identical identity modes, whose smeared trace diverges.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Constant-mode compression loses period-sensitive trace.** Eliminating nonconstant circle modes does not create a prime-period trace; it leaves one trivial mode per prime, producing an infinite identical contribution for every nonzero positive test function.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 7

The next candidate must retain exactly one period-sensitive cohomological mode per prime without retaining the full circle spectrum, and must make the resulting global family trace class through a genuine geometric mechanism rather than norm weighting or compression to constants.

These are different distributions for general compactly supported \\phi. The selected character therefore does not realize the required Lefschetz orbit term. Thus this candidate can obtain trace class for the character family. But the trace is then a Fourier sample at the artificial frequencies \\omega_p, not the required prime-period orbital distribution. Making the winding bounded to restore a canonical minimal character returns Candidate 7 and its trace divergence.

The inputs are primes, periods log p, the explicit integer winding k_p=ceil((log p)^2), local multipliers p^-1, the character representation, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations are used.

**High winding trades frequency collapse for noncanonical spectral data.** Separating the character frequencies by increasing winding can restore summability, but no longer represents the prime periods and has no canonical geometric source in the transverse return map.

The next candidate must obtain spectral separation from a canonical geometric structure, not an externally chosen winding sequence, while preserving the distributional identity between the smeared trace and the prime orbit lengths.

## Candidate 9: Canonical transverse dilation over prime loops

For each prime p, take a prime circle C_p of circumference log p and attach the transverse half-line R_+^*. Let the return map after one circuit act by
\\[
(x,y)\\longmapsto(x+\\log p,\\;p^{-1}y)
\\]
in logarithmic coordinates along the circle and multiplicative coordinates transversely. The transverse Hilbert space is \\(L^2(\\mathbb R_+,dy/y)\\), and the return operator is the canonical dilation
\\[
(D_p f)(y)=f(py).
\\]
Include a stationary archimedean point with transverse exponent -2. The construction uses only prime dilations and no zero data.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The multiplicative transverse line replaces the compact \\(\\mathbb Z_p^m\\) transversal. The scale q is replaced by the canonical local factor p. The dilation itself replaces Assumption (iv): it is the geometric source of p^-m rather than an imposed scalar weight.

### ORBITS

There is one primitive geometric orbit for each p. For p=2 the first two iterates have lengths log 2 and 2 log 2; for p=3 they have lengths log 3 and 2 log 3. The transverse return after m iterates is y to p^-m y, so the modular factor is geometrically present. No mixed prime orbits are introduced.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The transverse Jacobian of the m-th dilation is p^-m in the multiplicative normalization. This is the strongest Gate component of the candidate: the arithmetic factor is generated by an actual return map rather than a spectral weight.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A separate stationary point with transverse exponent -2 is included. Its formal local contribution is the geometric series kernel (1-e^-2t)^-1.

Under the Mellin transform, the dilation group becomes translation:
\\[
\\mathcal M D_p^t\\mathcal M^{-1}=e^{it(\\log p)\\xi},
\\qquad \\xi\\in\\mathbb R.
\\]
Thus each prime transverse sector has continuous Mellin spectrum \\(\\xi\\in\\mathbb R\\), not a discrete period-sensitive mode.

For a compactly supported smooth test function phi, the smeared transverse operator is a Fourier multiplier with symbol

a_p(\\xi)=\\widehat\\phi((\\log p)\\xi)
\\]
up to the chosen time normalization. It is not compact, let alone trace class, on \\(L^2(\\mathbb R,d\\xi)\\): a nonzero multiplication operator on a nonatomic \\(L^2\\) space is never compact. Therefore even one prime sector fails ordinary trace class. Compressing the Mellin line to a discrete lattice would require an additional compactification or boundary condition; that changes the canonical dilation and reintroduces either the high-winding/noncanonical choice or full spectral multiplicity.

The inputs are primes, circle lengths log p, canonical multiplicative dilation, the local transverse measure, the stationary exponent -2, and Mellin transform theory. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

## Consolidation 10: Canonical multiplicative dilation is not ordinary trace class

### CLASS UNDER TEST

Consider any prime sector whose transverse model is the canonical multiplicative Haar representation
\\[
\\mathcal K=L^2(\\mathbb R_+^\\ast,dy/y),
\\qquad
(D_t f)(y)=f(e^t y),
\\]
or a finite direct sum of such sectors. Let \\phi be a nonzero element of C_c^\\infty((0,\\infty)), and define
\\[
D(\\phi)=\\int_{\\mathbb R}\\phi(t)D_t\\,dt.
\\]

### PROVED NO-GO

The Mellin transform is unitary from \\mathcal K to L^2(\\mathbb R,d\\xi), and it sends D_t to multiplication by e^{it\\xi}. Therefore
\\[
\\mathcal M D(\\phi)\\mathcal M^{-1}
=
M_{\\widehat\\phi(\\xi)}
\\]
(up to the harmless Fourier-sign convention). Since \\phi is nonzero and compactly supported, \\widehat\\phi is an entire function that is not identically zero; its nonzero set has positive Lebesgue measure. A nonzero multiplication operator on a nonatomic L^2 space is not compact: choose infinitely many orthonormal functions supported on a finite-measure subset where |\\widehat\\phi| is bounded below. Their images remain mutually orthogonal with norms bounded below, so no subsequence can converge. Hence D(\\phi) is not compact and therefore cannot be trace class.

The same conclusion holds for every finite direct sum of these sectors. In particular, the canonical transverse representation that geometrically realizes multiplicative scaling cannot satisfy Gate 1 TRACE CLASS for all nonzero Weil-class test functions.

### CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ARITHMETIC FACTOR

The dilation model is not an arbitrary failed spectrum. It is the canonical representation in which the multiplicative return y to p^-1 y is realized by the modular factor p^-m. Replacing it by a discrete lattice or finite-dimensional character requires extra boundary, compactification, or winding data. The previous candidates show the alternatives:

- constant compression loses period-sensitive trace;
- minimal characters have frequencies tending to zero;
- high winding changes the trace distribution and has no canonical Lefschetz origin;
- finite or trace-class quotients cannot remove the noncompact sector.

Thus the natural geometric source of p^-m and ordinary Hilbert trace class are incompatible within this canonical dilation class.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The theorem is forced by the mechanism, not by candidate naming. Any construction using multiplicative Haar dilation has the same Mellin multiplication representation, independently of the chosen prime labels or finite transverse multiplicity. The theorem does not rule out replacing the entire transverse representation by a new trace-class object, nor does it address non-Hilbert traces; those are outside this Gate 1 target.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The adelic replacement for Z_p^m cannot simply be the multiplicative Haar/dilation fiber if ordinary trace class is required. A successful replacement must either:

1. use a genuinely different transverse representation that still produces p^-m geometrically, or
2. change the global notion of cohomology/operator so the dilation is not represented as a nonzero multiplication operator on a nonatomic Hilbert space.

Both possibilities remain open under Gate 1; neither has been instantiated here.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**PROVED NO-GO for canonical multiplicative Haar dilation sectors; PARTIAL globally.**

## Candidate 11: p-adic finite-level transverse tower

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, use the compact p-adic transversal Z_p and the finite quotients
\\[
Z_p \\longrightarrow Z/p^nZ.
\\]
Let the proposed prime return map on the transversal be
\\[
R_p(x)=p x.
\\]
At level n, let H_{p,n}=L^2(Z/p^nZ) and let R_{p,n} be the induced map wherever defined. Form a tower under pullback along the quotient maps and take the inverse-limit Hilbert space. Attach this tower to a prime circle of length log p, and add a stationary archimedean point with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The compact p-adic transversal replaces the local Z_p^m model directly. The arithmetic scale is p itself, so the return map is intended to supply the modular factor p^-m. The finite quotient harmonic spaces are intended to replace Assumption (iv) by making each approximation finite dimensional.

### ORBITS

The base circle has primitive length log p and iterates m log p; for p=2 these are log 2 and 2 log 2, and for p=3 they are log 3 and 2 log 3. However, a flow return map must be invertible on the transverse space. Multiplication by p on Z_p is injective but not surjective, and on Z/p^nZ it is noninjective. Therefore R_p cannot be the Poincare return map of an invertible flow on the proposed transversal. The finite-level model fails the geometric orbit requirement before trace analysis.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The non-surjective map x to p x has the desired arithmetic scaling on Haar measure, but this is precisely a noninvertible endomorphism rather than a transverse return map of a flow. Replacing it by an invertible extension, such as a solenoid or bilateral p-adic dilation, restores an infinite two-sided spectrum and leaves the finite-level trace-class mechanism.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary point with transverse exponent -2 is included explicitly, so the local archimedean component is present.

### SPECTRUM

Each finite quotient has finite-dimensional spectrum, but the inverse limit contains infinitely many new locally constant characters. The resulting Koopman/transfer representation is not a finite direct sum. Without a finite-level cutoff, the character tower is infinite and no uniform trace-class estimate follows from finite-dimensionality of each approximation.

### TRACE CLASS

At any fixed n, a finite quotient produces a finite matrix and hence a trace-class smeared operator. But the number of characters grows like p^n. Passing to the inverse limit restores infinitely many character modes. A cutoff-independent ordinary trace would require summability of the full character tower; no such summability is supplied by the Haar representation. If one keeps only a fixed finite level, the system omits arbitrarily fine transverse dynamics and the claimed p-adic return is not the inverse-limit object. Thus finite-level trace class does not survive as a verified Gate-1 property.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, Z_p, finite quotient rings Z/p^nZ, multiplication by p, locally constant functions, inverse limits, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** Multiplication by p is not an invertible return map, while finite-level trace class disappears in the inverse limit unless a cutoff is retained.

### FAILURE CLASS

**p-adic finite-level scaling is noninvertible or loses trace control in the inverse limit.** Arithmetic compactness at each finite quotient does not provide an invertible flow return or a cutoff-independent trace-class cohomology.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 12

The next candidate must use an invertible p-adic/adelic extension from the start and prove a uniform trace-class estimate in the inverse limit, rather than relying on finite quotients. It must also preserve the exact prime orbit and modular factor.

## Candidate 12: Invertible p-adic solenoid dilation

### CONSTRUCTION

Let
\\[
\\mathbb S_p=\\varprojlim_n \\mathbb R/p^n\\mathbb Z
\\]
be the p-adic solenoid, with Haar probability measure. Multiplication by p extends to an invertible automorphism \\(R_p\\) of the solenoid because the inverse acts on the inverse-limit coordinates by shifting them. Attach \\(\\mathbb S_p\\) transversely to a prime orbit circle of length log p, let one return apply R_p, and include a stationary archimedean point with exponent -2. Use the Haar \\(L^2(\\mathbb S_p)\\) representation. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The solenoid replaces the noninvertible Z_p tower while retaining compactness and an invertible arithmetic return. The automorphism R_p replaces the scale q and the p-adic Jacobian mechanism. The Haar-character decomposition is intended to replace Assumption (iv) with a canonical global spectral decomposition.

### ORBITS

The base orbit for p=2 has primitive length log 2 and iterates 2 log 2; for p=3 the corresponding lengths are log 3 and 2 log 3. The transverse return is invertible, so the basic geometric orbit is admissible. However, the solenoid automorphism has many character modes; the Lefschetz contribution is not reduced to a finite local harmonic sector without an additional trace prescription.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The return automorphism is the invertible extension of p-adic multiplication and carries the arithmetic p-scaling. Any modular factor obtained from its Haar action is encoded in the automorphism, not inserted as a scalar. This repairs Candidate 11's noninvertibility at the geometric level.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary point with transverse exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The characters of the compact solenoid form a countable discrete group. The Koopman operator permutes these characters under the dual action of R_p. The resulting representation contains infinitely many character orbits; it is not a finite-dimensional harmonic sector. Nontrivial character orbits either have infinite shift chains or finite cycles, depending on the dual action.

### TRACE CLASS

At finite character truncation, the smeared operator is finite rank, but the truncation is a cutoff. In the full Haar \\(L^2\\) representation, infinitely many character modes remain. For any nonzero smearing whose spectral multiplier is nonzero on infinitely many character orbits, the operator has infinitely many singular values bounded away from zero along those modes, or has a noncompact bilateral-shift component. Hence it is not trace class. Suppressing the modes by a finite-level projection restores Candidate 11's cutoff dependence; adding a smoothing operator changes the canonical Haar representation and requires a new noncanonical choice.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the prime, the compact solenoid, Haar measure, the invertible p-adic scaling automorphism, the prime orbit length log p, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** The solenoid repairs invertibility but not ordinary trace class: finite-level trace class is a cutoff, while the full invertible Haar representation has an infinite character spectrum.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Invertible solenoid dilation has continuous/discrete infinite Haar spectrum.** Making p-adic scaling invertible preserves the full infinite character representation; compactness of the transversal does not imply trace-class smeared dynamics.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 13

The next candidate must replace the full Haar representation by a canonically finite or summably smoothed cohomology while retaining invertible p-adic scaling, and must prove that the smoothing is intrinsic rather than a cutoff or an added regularization.

## Candidate 13: Heat-smoothed solenoid cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, take the compact p-adic solenoid S_p with its Haar measure and invertible multiplication-by-p automorphism R_p. Choose the standard translation-invariant Laplacian Delta_p on the compact character group and define the heat-smoothed cohomology operator
\\[
K_{p,\\tau}=e^{-\\tau\\Delta_p},\\qquad \\tau>0.
\\]
Use the range/graph Hilbert space determined by K_{p,\\tau} as the transverse cohomology, with the prime orbit circle of length log p and local return R_p. Add a stationary archimedean point of exponent -2. The heat parameter is fixed canonically by the unit Haar normalization, not chosen from zeros.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The solenoid replaces Z_p^m and supplies an invertible arithmetic return. The heat operator is proposed as the replacement for Assumption (iv): it damps high transverse characters intrinsically and is trace class on the compact transversal for each fixed p. The local prime period and return map are retained.

### ORBITS

The base prime orbits remain: p=2 has lengths log 2 and 2 log 2; p=3 has lengths log 3 and 2 log 3. The transverse automorphism is invertible. But the heat-smoothed cohomology is not preserved by the return unless K_{p,\\tau} commutes with R_p. If it is not preserved, it is not a well-defined flow-invariant cohomology. If it is forced to be invariant, the trace contribution is changed by the heat multiplier on each character and no longer equals the unweighted Lefschetz contribution for every iterate.

### MODULAR FACTORS

R_p supplies the arithmetic scaling and its intended p^-m factor. The heat operator adds a character-dependent factor e^(-tau lambda_chi) to the return trace. This changes the local iterate coefficient from the required pure p^-m to a sum weighted by heat eigenvalues, unless the heat factor is identically one.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The solenoid character spectrum is countably infinite. Heat smoothing makes the character multiplier summable at a fixed tau, but the return automorphism permutes characters and generally does not commute with the fixed Laplacian. A dilation-invariant Laplacian would have to assign equal heat weights along every R_p-character orbit; for infinite character orbits this prevents decay along the orbit and destroys trace class.

### TRACE CLASS

There are two cases.

1. If Delta_p and R_p do not commute, the heat-smoothed subspace is not invariant under the flow, so no flow cohomology operator A_j(phi) is defined on it without inserting a projection. The inserted projection is an external regularization and changes the trace formula.

2. If they commute, the heat multiplier is constant on every character orbit of R_p. On any infinite orbit, a nonzero constant multiplier is repeated infinitely many times, so the resulting operator is not trace class. Setting the multiplier to zero on all infinite orbits removes the arithmetic sector; retaining only finite orbits is a noncanonical spectral truncation.

Thus intrinsic heat smoothing cannot simultaneously be flow-invariant, trace class, and coefficient-preserving.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, compact p-adic solenoids, Haar measure, invertible multiplication-by-p, the standard Laplacian, a fixed heat parameter, prime periods log p, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** Noncommuting heat smoothing is not an invariant cohomology; commuting heat smoothing is constant along infinite character orbits and cannot be trace class without deleting or truncating the arithmetic sector.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Intrinsic heat smoothing is not flow-compatible.** A smoothing operator can be trace class, but the canonical arithmetic return either fails to preserve it or forces its eigenweights to repeat along infinite character orbits.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 14

The next candidate must find a flow-invariant summable structure on the invertible p-adic spectrum without weighting every infinite character orbit by a repeated nonzero constant. It must preserve the pure p^-m Lefschetz coefficient, not replace it by heat-weighted character sums.

## Candidate 14: Invertible weighted character shift

### CONSTRUCTION

Let the dual character set of the p-adic solenoid contain a bilateral orbit indexed by n in Z under the dual action of multiplication by p. On the Hilbert space l2(Z) for this orbit, define a weighted bilateral shift
\\[
(W_p e_n)=a_{p,n}e_{n+1}.
\\]
Choose positive weights with forward decay, for example \\(a_{p,n}=2^{-|n|}\\) after a symmetric normalization, and couple the shift to a prime orbit circle of length log p. Include local arithmetic return p^-1 and the stationary archimedean exponent -2. The weights are intended to make smeared powers summable while retaining an invertible global action.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The bilateral character orbit replaces the Haar character representation of the solenoid. The weighted shift is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv): it is meant to suppress high character multiplicity intrinsically. The p-adic return remains invertible only if W_p has a bounded inverse.

### ORBITS

The base circles retain primitive lengths log 2 and log 3 and their first iterates. The transverse character dynamics is invertible only when every a_{p,n} is nonzero and both W_p and W_p^{-1} are bounded. No mixed prime orbits are introduced.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local p-adic return is intended to supply p^-m. The shift weights add additional products of a_{p,n} to the iterated trace, so the pure p^-m coefficient is preserved only if the weights cancel in the alternating Lefschetz supertrace. No such cancellation is present in the one-sector construction.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

Each infinite character orbit produces a bilateral weighted-shift spectrum. The construction is not a finite-level cutoff, but it has infinite multiplicity along each orbit.

### TRACE CLASS

If W_p is boundedly invertible, there is a constant c_p>0 such that
\\[
|a_{p,n}|\\ge c_p
\\]
for all n; otherwise the inverse is unbounded. Thus the shift cannot have weights decaying to zero in both directions. Any smeared operator containing a nonzero contribution from infinitely many basis vectors has singular values bounded below along an infinite subsequence and is not trace class. If the weights are allowed to decay to zero, W_p ceases to be invertible and cannot be a flow return map. If one adds a compact smoothing factor, Candidate 13's flow-compatibility problem returns and the pure p^-m coefficient is altered.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, solenoid dual orbits, an explicit weighted bilateral shift, local p-adic scaling, prime periods log p, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** Bounded invertibility prevents the two-sided decay needed for trace class; allowing decay destroys the invertible flow return.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Invertible weighted shift cannot decay in both directions.** A genuinely invertible bilateral arithmetic action has no intrinsic two-sided summability mechanism from scalar orbit weights.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 15

The next candidate must avoid scalar weighted shifts and find a different invariant summability mechanism—such as finite-dimensional cohomological cancellation that preserves the prime Lefschetz coefficient—while remaining invertible and cutoff-free.

## Candidate 15: Conductor-graded adelic cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

Take the finite adeles A_f with compact slice \\widehat{\\mathbb Z} and prime orbit circles C_p of length log p. For each integer N>=1 define the finite-dimensional space
\\[
V_N=C(\\mathbb A_f/N\\widehat{\\mathbb Z}),
\\]
identified with locally constant functions of conductor dividing N. Define the proposed transverse cohomology as the Hilbert completion
\\[
\\mathcal H_{\\mathrm{cond}}=\\widehat{\\bigoplus}_{N\\ge1}V_N
\\]
with a summable spectral grading chosen so that the dimensions have the required O(T log T) counting. Let Q_{>0}^* act by adelic multiplication and let the prime return at p use multiplication by p on A_f. Add the stationary archimedean boundary stratum with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

A_f replaces Z_p^m simultaneously for all primes. The local arithmetic multiplier p^-1 comes from additive finite-adelic Haar scaling, not from the unit factors. The conductor grading is proposed as the replacement for Assumption (iv): it makes H^1 infinite-dimensional but spectrally compact through finite-dimensional V_N pieces.

### ORBITS

The intended prime circles have primitive lengths log 2 and log 3 and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3, each with multiplicity one and sign +1 at the base geometry. The adelic return is supposed to act on the transverse graded modes. But multiplication by q in Q_{>0}^* sends functions of conductor N to functions whose conductor is generally qN or q^-1N. Therefore the finite V_N are not preserved by the full return group. Restricting to a positive-prime semigroup loses inverse-time flow; closing under inverses produces an infinite orbit of conductor grades. Gate ORBITS/flow compatibility fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

On the additive finite adeles, d(qx)=|q|_f dx and for q=p^m the local scaling supplies p^-m in the chosen normalization. This part is arithmetically correct. On the unit factors away from p there is no such factor, consistent with the addendum.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The archimedean stationary point is placed in the boundary compactification stratum, with transverse exponent -2. It is not part of the finite-adelic transversal.

### SPECTRUM

At each fixed conductor N, V_N is finite-dimensional. The full Q_{>0}^* orbit of a mode is not finite: inverse prime multiplications generate unbounded conductor denominators. Consequently a flow-invariant completion contains infinitely many translated conductor pieces. A spectral weight that decays along this orbit is not invariant under the invertible return; an invariant weight repeats along the orbit.

### TRACE CLASS

Finite conductor truncations give finite-rank smeared operators, but truncation is forbidden. In the invariant completion, every nonzero mode generates an infinite orbit under Q_{>0}^*. If the return acts by bounded invertible permutations on these mode spaces, the corresponding singular values cannot decay to zero along the full orbit without making the inverse unbounded. Therefore the globally invariant operator is not trace class unless the mode is deleted. Deleting all nontrivial conductor modes leaves only the trivial mode and cannot encode the adelic modular factor or the required prime orbit coefficients.

### INPUTS

The inputs are A_f, \\widehat Z, finite conductor quotients, Q_{>0}^* multiplication, Haar scaling, prime orbit lengths, and the archimedean boundary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** The finite-dimensional conductor grading is not preserved by the full invertible return group; its invariant closure has infinite conductor orbits and no cutoff-free trace-class estimate.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Conductor grading is not invariant under the full return group.** Finite adelic spectral compactness is incompatible with the inverse-prime action required by a two-sided arithmetic flow unless a cutoff or noninvertible restriction is introduced.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 16

The next candidate must use a Q_{>0}^*-invariant spectral grading from the beginning, with infinite mode orbits controlled by a canonical summability mechanism that does not weight an invertible orbit by decaying scalars. It must retain additive Haar scaling and the boundary archimedean point.

## Candidate 16: Quotient by full adelic return orbits

### CONSTRUCTION

Let A_f be the finite adeles and let G=Q_{>0}^* act by multiplication. Start with locally constant compactly supported functions on A_f and impose the orbit relation
\\[
f\\sim f\\circ g,\\qquad g\\in G.
\\]
Define the proposed transverse cohomology as the completion of the coinvariant space under the quotient seminorm, with prime orbit circles of length log p and additive Haar scaling. Add the stationary archimedean boundary point with exponent -2. The construction is zero-independent.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

A_f replaces Z_p^m globally. The full G-action replaces the single scale q and is intended to preserve all inverse-prime operations. The coinvariant quotient replaces Assumption (iv): all translates of one adelic mode are identified, so the infinite conductor orbit is collapsed rather than weighted.

### ORBITS

The prime circles retain formal primitive lengths log 2 and log 3 and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. But the quotient identifies transverse states under all rational scaling. The return action of every prime becomes the identity on coinvariants. Consequently the quotient has no nontrivial transverse return data from which to distinguish the prime orbit contributions or their modular factors. The orbit geometry and reduced cohomology no longer produce the same Lefschetz trace. Gate ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Before quotienting, additive Haar scaling gives p^-m. After imposing f equivalent to f composed with p, the p-action is trivial on the quotient; the modular operator is lost or becomes an external cocycle not represented on cohomology.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The coinvariant quotient is not naturally a Hilbert space. The orbit relation is nonproper and has dense/nonclosed ranges in natural \\(L^2(A_f)\\) realizations. Completing by a quotient seminorm either collapses all non-invariant spectral modes or produces a non-Hausdorff pre-Hilbert space before completion. A Hausdorff quotient retaining the G-action has not been constructed.

### TRACE CLASS

If the quotient collapses every G-orbit, the prime return action is the identity on the surviving classes. A nonzero positive test function then contributes the same scalar to infinitely many surviving prime classes unless all but finitely many classes are removed, which is a cutoff or deletion of arithmetic data. If one instead retains a Hilbert representation of the G-action, the infinite orbit directions return and the same non-trace-class/shift obstruction applies. Thus neither quotient branch gives ordinary trace class with the required trace formula.

### INPUTS

## Candidate 17: Arithmetic regular representation with word-length confinement

### CONSTRUCTION

Let G=Q_{>0}^* and identify it with the free abelian group on the primes. Use the regular Hilbert space \\(\\ell^2(G)\\), with left translations \\(L_q\\). Let
\\[
\\ell(q)=\\sum_p |v_p(q)|
\\]
be the arithmetic word length and define the diagonal confining operator
\\[
D e_q=(1+\\ell(q))e_q.
\\]
Use the cohomological space as a compact-resolvent graph/Sobolev completion for D, with the prime return represented by L_p. Attach a prime orbit circle of length log p and the archimedean boundary point of exponent -2.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The full arithmetic group G replaces the separate p-adic transversals and implements all inverse primes simultaneously. The word-length operator D replaces Assumption (iv): it gives finite-dimensional sublevel spaces and a discrete spectrum. The local p-adic modular factor is intended to come from the additive adelic realization behind the group labels.

### ORBITS

Formal prime circles have lengths log 2 and log 3, with iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3, and no mixed geometric loops in the base. But powers of the global return L_p act by translation on G and produce infinite label orbits, not finite transverse return data. The regular representation therefore does not furnish a finite Lefschetz determinant for the prime orbit. Gate ORBITS fails at the cohomological realization level.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The group label p records additive adelic scaling, but the left translation L_p itself is unitary and has no p^-m Jacobian on counting measure. Adding the adelic Haar Jacobian as a scalar weight changes the regular representation and loses unitarity/invertibility unless a different non-Hilbert measure is used. Thus the intended modular factor is not generated by the stated Hilbert return.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The representation is global, not a direct sum of prime circles. D has compact resolvent because each word-length ball in the free abelian group on countably many primes is nevertheless infinite unless one also bounds the allowed prime support. If one bounds support, the action of all inverse primes leaves the domain. If one uses a support-penalizing length that makes balls finite, the length is no longer invariant under left translation.

### TRACE CLASS

A confining D can make functions of D trace class only after choosing a nontranslation-invariant potential. The prime returns L_p do not commute with D:
\\[
[D,L_p]\
e0.
\\]
If the smeared flow is built from L_p alone, it is a unitary translation with no compactness. If it is built from a D-dependent heat/confining factor, the resulting trace is no longer the pure prime Lefschetz trace and contains potential-dependent weights. Thus no flow-invariant, trace-class cohomology is obtained.

### INPUTS

The inputs are Q_{>0}^*, prime valuations, counting measure, regular translations, arithmetic word length, prime periods log p, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS).** Translation-invariant arithmetic regular representation has no compact spectral mechanism; a confining operator breaks translation invariance and changes the trace formula.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Group-invariant confining operator cannot have compact resolvent.** A faithful regular representation of the full arithmetic return group has infinite translation orbits; a confining potential can be compact only by breaking the return symmetry.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 18

The next candidate must obtain spectral compactness from an invariant of the full arithmetic group, not from word length or a noncommuting potential, while still generating the additive Haar factor p^-m and the exact prime Lefschetz trace.

## Candidate 18: Idele-class quotient with invariant harmonic analysis

### CONSTRUCTION

Let
\\[
C_{\\mathbb Q}=\\mathbb A_{\\mathbb Q}^\\*/\\mathbb Q^\\*
\\]
be the idele class group with its Haar measure. Use the modulus map
\\[
|\\cdot|:C_{\\mathbb Q}\\to\\mathbb R_+^\\*
\\]
and let the flow act by translation in the modulus coordinate. Use the regular representation on \\(L^2(C_{\\mathbb Q})\\), with the finite-idele component supplying additive prime scaling and a separate boundary point for the archimedean exponent -2. Prime orbit circles of length log p are attached as geometric suspension data. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The global idele class group replaces the collection of local Z_p^m transversals and incorporates all inverse primes in one quotient. The modulus character replaces the single scale q. Invariant Haar harmonic analysis replaces Assumption (iv), with the hope that the quotient by Q^* removes redundant arithmetic directions while retaining a manageable global spectrum.

### ORBITS

The attached formal prime suspensions have lengths log 2 and log 3 and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. But the regular idele-class flow itself has no discrete family of isolated prime closed orbits corresponding one-to-one to p; its modulus component is a noncompact translation. The prime circles are added as separate geometric data rather than derived from the quotient. Thus the orbit realization is not obtained from the invariant harmonic object.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The finite-idele Haar scaling records the p-adic factors, while the modulus character records the product formula. However, on the quotient by Q^*, rational scaling has been identified, so the modular cocycle is not a separate transverse return determinant for an isolated prime orbit. It remains an adelic character datum rather than a Lefschetz return map.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A boundary compactification point with transverse exponent -2 is added explicitly. It is not an interior point of the idele-class Haar flow.

### SPECTRUM

The idele class group has a noncompact modulus factor isomorphic to R under logarithm. Its regular representation has continuous Fourier spectrum. The compact idelic quotient contributes discrete characters, but tensoring with the modulus representation retains the continuous component.

### TRACE CLASS

For a nonzero compactly supported test function phi in the modulus time, the smeared translation operator on L^2(R) is multiplication by \\widehat\\phi(\\xi), hence is noncompact by the same nonatomic multiplier argument as Consolidation 10. Adding the compact idelic factor cannot repair this; it only adds multiplicity. Compactifying or discretizing the modulus direction changes the modulus trace and loses the exact prime-period distribution. Therefore the invariant global quotient does not satisfy ordinary trace class.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the ideles, Q^*, the idele class group, Haar measure, the modulus map, finite-idele scaling, formal prime suspensions, and the boundary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS).** The invariant idele-class object has continuous modulus spectrum and does not itself produce isolated prime closed orbits. Adding prime suspensions externally returns the earlier globalization problem.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Idele-class harmonic analysis retains a noncompact scaling spectrum.** Quotienting by rational scaling creates a canonical global object but does not remove the continuous real-modulus direction required for the arithmetic flow.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 19

The next candidate must compactify or spectrally confine the modulus direction without changing the exact prime-period trace, or derive isolated prime closed orbits intrinsically from the global quotient rather than appending them.

## Candidate 19: Bohr compactification of logarithmic modulus

### CONSTRUCTION

Let bR be the Bohr compactification of the additive logarithmic time group R. The original modulus translation embeds densely in bR, and Haar measure on bR gives a canonical compactification without choosing a period. Use the Koopman representation on L^2(bR), attach prime closed-orbit suspensions with primitive lengths log p, and include the archimedean boundary point with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The compact group bR replaces the noncompact modulus direction of the idele-class model. Its Haar character decomposition replaces Assumption (iv) by a compact-group harmonic decomposition. The prime periods are retained as translations by log p, while the finite-adelic scaling remains the source of p^-m.

### ORBITS

The translation by log 2 and log 3 on bR is well-defined, but it is not periodic: because log 2 and log 3 are nonzero and no chosen compact period identifies their integer multiples with zero, each translation has dense orbit in the relevant Bohr closure. Thus bR itself does not yield primitive closed orbits of lengths log 2 or log 3. Adding separate prime suspensions makes the orbit data external, not intrinsic.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The finite-adelic component can still encode additive Haar scaling p^-m. The Bohr compactification changes only the modulus-time representation and does not itself create a transverse return determinant.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with transverse exponent -2 is included explicitly, but it is an added compactification stratum rather than a point forced by the Bohr flow.

### SPECTRUM

The Pontryagin dual of bR is R equipped with the discrete topology. Consequently
\\[
L^2(b\\mathbb R)\\cong \\ell^2(\\mathbb R_{\\mathrm{disc}}),
\\]
with an uncountable orthonormal character basis. Translation by t acts diagonally with eigenvalues e^{i\\xi t}. This is compact as a group space but has an uncountable spectral multiplicity.

### TRACE CLASS

For a nonzero compactly supported smooth test function phi, the smeared translation is diagonal with eigenvalues \\widehat\\phi(\\xi) indexed by every \\xi in R. Since \\widehat\\phi is continuous and nonzero somewhere, there is an interval on which its absolute value is bounded below. That interval contains uncountably many distinct \\xi, so the diagonal operator is not even a compact operator on \\ell^2(R_disc), and hence not trace class. Restricting to a countable subgroup or character lattice is an additional noncanonical spectral cutoff and changes the modulus trace.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the additive logarithmic group R, its Bohr compactification, Haar measure, prime translation parameters log p, finite-adelic scaling, formal prime suspensions, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE).** The Bohr compactification supplies canonical compactness but loses periodic prime orbits and has an uncountable character spectrum preventing ordinary trace class.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Bohr compactification has too-large dual spectrum.** Compactifying a noncompact arithmetic flow without choosing a period replaces continuous spectrum by an uncountable discrete dual, which is still incompatible with ordinary trace class.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 20

The next pass must be a consolidation. It must compare the three canonical modulus treatments—real line, idele-class modulus, and Bohr compactification—and formulate a no-go theorem for compactifications that preserve the full logarithmic translation group while retaining ordinary trace class.



## Consolidation 20: Modulus compactification versus ordinary trace class

### CLASS UNDER TEST

Compare the three canonical ways tested for the global logarithmic/modulus direction:

1. the real translation line L^2(R);
2. the idele-class quotient, whose modulus factor still contains L^2(R);
3. the Bohr compactification bR of R with Haar representation.

Each is required to retain the full additive logarithmic translation group and to support a cutoff-free ordinary trace for every nonzero phi in C_c^\\infty((0,infty)).

### PROVED NO-GO: REAL MODULUS

For the translation group on L^2(R), Fourier transform turns the smeared operator into multiplication by \\widehat\\phi(\\xi). For nonzero compactly supported phi, \\widehat\\phi is nonzero on a positive-measure set. A nonzero multiplication operator on nonatomic L^2(R) is not compact, hence not trace class. Therefore the real modulus representation cannot satisfy Gate 1 TRACE.

### PROVED NO-GO: IDELE-CLASS MODULUS FACTOR

The modulus map on the idele class group has a noncompact R factor. The regular representation contains the real translation representation as a tensor/direct factor. Tensoring with the remaining idelic representation cannot make the noncompact multiplier compact; it only adds multiplicity. Therefore any idele-class construction retaining the full modulus regular representation fails ordinary trace class.

### PROVED NO-GO: BOHR COMPACTIFICATION

For bR, Pontryagin duality gives
\\[
L^2(bR)\\cong\\ell^2(R_{\\mathrm{disc}}).
\\]
The smeared translation is diagonal with eigenvalues \\widehat\\phi(\\xi), indexed by every real \\xi. Since \\widehat\\phi is nonzero on an interval for a suitable nonzero phi, uncountably many diagonal entries are bounded below. The operator is not compact and hence not trace class. Restricting to a smaller character set is a spectral cutoff or a new noncanonical representation, not the full Bohr flow.

### COMPARISON AND LIMIT

The real line fails by nonatomic continuous spectrum. The idele-class quotient fails because its modulus factor retains that real spectrum. The Bohr compactification fails by replacing it with an uncountable discrete dual. Compactness of the underlying group does not imply trace-class smearing.

A compact quotient with a single period would avoid these conclusions only by imposing an external period. Since the numbers log p are Q-linearly independent, no single compact period realizes all prime lengths. Thus the three canonical modulus mechanisms exhaust the natural compactification choices tested here, but this is not a theorem about every possible global construction.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The result is forced for the real regular representation, the idele-class regular representation with its modulus factor, and the Bohr compactification. It is not forced by candidate naming. The global open class is a different, non-regular representation that both preserves all logarithmic prime translations and has an intrinsically summable spectrum.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The modulus direction cannot be made trace class by:

- leaving it as the real line;
- passing to the idele class group;
- compactifying canonically by bR;
- or imposing one period.

A successful adelic replacement must therefore be neither the ordinary modulus regular representation nor a canonical compactification with the full character spectrum. It must provide a new global representation in which prime translations remain geometrically meaningful while the spectral measure is intrinsically summable.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**PROVED NO-GO for the real, idele-modulus, and Bohr-compactification classes; PARTIAL globally.**

## Candidate 21: Discrete oscillator representation of logarithmic time

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \\(\\mathcal H=\\ell^2(\\mathbb N_0)\\) with basis e_n and define
\\[
A e_n=n e_n,\\qquad U_t=e^{itA}.
\\]
This is a single global representation of logarithmic time with discrete spectrum and compact-resolvent generator. For every prime p, the operator \\(U_{\\log p}\\) is a well-defined global return operator; no separate prime sector is introduced. Add formal prime suspension circles of lengths log p and a stationary boundary point with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The oscillator space replaces all separate Z_p^m fibers by one global compact-resolvent cohomology. The integer spectrum replaces the scale q and the proposed Assumption (iv) is the number operator's discrete spectral growth. The prime return is represented by a translation in the same global space rather than by separate fibers.

### ORBITS

The global representation has no primitive closed geometric orbits corresponding to individual primes. The operators U_log2 and U_log3 are merely two elements of one continuous-time representation; their periods are not log 2 and log 3. Attaching prime circles externally restores the lengths but makes the orbit geometry separate from the cohomological trace. Thus Gate ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

No transverse return map produces p^-m. One could append p^-m to a formal prime term, but that would not arise from the oscillator representation.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is added explicitly, but it is not generated by the oscillator flow.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is global and discrete. For \\phi in C_c^\\infty((0,\\infty)),
\\[
U(\\phi)e_n=\\widehat\\phi(n)e_n.
\\]
Because \\widehat\\phi is rapidly decreasing on integers, U(\\phi) is trace class for every such \\phi. This is genuine progress on spectral compactness, but not on the orbit identity.

### TRACE CLASS AND TRACE FORMULA

The ordinary trace is
\\[
\\operatorname{Tr}U(\\phi)=\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\widehat\\phi(n),
\\]
which is finite. The required Gate trace is instead
\\[
\\sum_p\\log p\\sum_{m\\ge1}\\phi(m\\log p)
+\\int_0^\\infty\\frac{\\phi(t)}{1-e^{-2t}}\\,dt.
\\]
These are different distributions in \\phi. Equality for all test functions would require the oscillator spectral distribution \\(\\sum_n\\delta_n\\) to equal the prime-period distribution, which is false: the former is supported on integer frequencies, while the latter is supported on the multiplicative set \\(\\{m\\log p\\}\\), and those supports are not equal. Thus trace class is achieved but the required trace formula is not.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the integer spectrum, continuous translation, the prime labels log p, formal prime suspensions, and the boundary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, TRACE FORMULA).** This is a valid global trace-class representation, but its trace distribution is the wrong one and prime geometry is appended rather than generated.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Discrete oscillator spectrum gives the wrong orbit distribution.** Compact resolvent alone is insufficient: the spectral trace must equal the exact prime-period distribution, not merely be summable.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 22

The next candidate must construct a globally discrete/summable representation whose spectral trace distribution is exactly supported at the prime iterates \\(m\\log p\\), while generating the modular factors geometrically rather than appending them.

## Candidate 22: Diagonal spectrum at all prime iterates

### CONSTRUCTION

Let
\\[
\\Lambda=\\{m\\log p:p\\ \\text{prime},\\ m\\ge1\\}
\\]
with one basis vector e_{p,m} for each pair, and define
\\[
A e_{p,m}=m\\log p\\,e_{p,m},\\qquad U_t=e^{itA}.
\\]
Use the global Hilbert space \\(\\ell^2(\\Lambda)\\), include the formal prime orbit circles of lengths log p, and add the archimedean boundary point with exponent -2. The construction is zero-independent and directly places the desired prime-iterate support into the spectrum.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The entire adelic transverse structure is replaced by one global diagonal spectral space indexed by prime iterates. Assumption (iv) is replaced by the asserted one-mode-per-iterate grading. The prime lengths are no longer generated by local circle spectra; they are inserted as eigenvalues.

### ORBITS

The formal base data have one primitive orbit for p=2 of length log 2 and iterates 2 log 2, and one primitive orbit for p=3 of length log 3 and iterate 2 log 3, each with intended sign +1. But these orbit data are external to the diagonal representation. The spectral basis is indexed by iterates rather than arising from a primitive closed orbit and its Lefschetz powers. Gate ORBITS is not geometrically realized.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The diagonal eigenvalues do not produce p^-m. Appending p^-m to the basis labels is not a transverse return determinant. A scalar multiplicity/weight would be required in the trace, which is not ordinary Hilbert trace.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is added explicitly, but the diagonal spectrum does not generate it.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is global and discrete, but its counting function is too dense: the number of pairs with m log p <= T grows on the scale of e^T rather than the polynomial/logarithmic density compatible with a rapidly decaying Fourier multiplier. Thus even placing the support correctly does not automatically give trace class.

### TRACE FORMULA

For any trace-class diagonal operator, the coefficient of an isolated eigenvalue in the ordinary trace is its algebraic multiplicity, an integer. The required prime-orbit distribution has coefficient log p at every m log p. Since log p is not an integer for any prime p, no ordinary unweighted Hilbert trace of this diagonal spectrum can equal
\\[
\\sum_p\\log p\\sum_{m\\ge1}\\phi(m\\log p)
\\]
for all test functions. Assigning noninteger weights is a weighted trace or a non-Hilbert functional, not the Gate 1 ordinary trace.

Even if one duplicates eigenvalues to approximate log p, the coefficient remains an integer and exact equality fails. The dense eigenvalue counting also obstructs trace class for general compactly supported smooth tests unless additional smoothing is inserted, which changes the trace distribution.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, integers m, eigenvalues m log p, formal prime suspensions, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE FORMULA, TRACE).** The spectral support can be written down, but ordinary Hilbert trace coefficients cannot equal the logarithmic prime weights, and the raw diagonal spectrum is too dense for unconditional trace class.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Ordinary spectral multiplicity cannot equal logarithmic orbit weight.** Exact logarithmic coefficients require a Lefschetz/geometric mechanism or a weighted trace; they cannot be assigned as noninteger multiplicities in an ordinary Hilbert trace.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 23

The next candidate must generate the \\(\\log p\\) coefficient geometrically through a genuine orbit/Lefschetz index rather than assigning it as a spectral weight, while keeping a globally trace-class cohomology.
