## Candidate 23: Finite-dimensional Lefschetz suspension per prime

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, take a geometric periodic orbit C_p of length log p, but assign only a finite-dimensional cohomology space E_p, with a finite-dimensional return matrix B_p. Let the global cohomology be a proposed spectrally compact completion of the algebraic sum of the E_p, together with a stationary archimedean point of exponent -2. The Lefschetz sign of B_p^m is required to be +1 for all m.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

Finite-dimensional E_p replaces the full leafwise circle spectrum and is intended to realize Leichtnam's finite-dimensional harmonic sector simultaneously for all primes. The local return matrix B_p replaces the scale q and the transverse p-adic return. A finite-dimensional index condition replaces Assumption (iv).

### ORBITS

The geometry has one primitive orbit for p=2 of length log 2 and its iterates 2 log 2, and one for p=3 of length log 3 and its iterates 2 log 3, each with intended Lefschetz sign +1. The geometric orbit data are correctly specified.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The return matrix can be chosen so that its transverse determinant supplies p^-m in the negative-time normalization, or the candidate can use the positive-time normalization where no p^-m is required. This does not resolve the trace distribution issue.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary point with transverse exponent -2 is included as a separate boundary stratum and formally supplies the archimedean kernel.

### SPECTRUM

Each E_p is finite dimensional, but the finite-dimensional flow trace on E_p is a finite sum of exponentials in t:
\\[
\\operatorname{Tr}(e^{tB_p})=\\sum_{r=1}^{d_p}e^{t\\lambda_{p,r}}.
\\]
It is an ordinary smooth/analytic function, not a delta distribution supported at the period log p. The periodic-orbit delta contribution arises only from the full circle translation spectrum or an equivalent distributional trace construction.

### TRACE CLASS

For any fixed finite collection of E_p, smeared traces are trace class but produce smooth spectral terms. For all primes simultaneously, either:

1. the global cohomology is an ordinary direct sum, returning the prime-sector trace divergence; or
2. the sectors are compressed into a global finite/summable representation, in which case the time trace remains a sum of ordinary smooth spectral functions and cannot equal the required discrete distribution
\\[
\\sum_p\\log p\\sum_{m\\ge1}\\delta_{m\\log p}
\\]
on all compactly supported tests.

Creating the delta masses requires restoring an infinite Fourier/circle spectrum or using a distributional/zeta/b-trace, all forbidden by Gate 1. Thus finite-dimensional Lefschetz indices cannot substitute for the period-sensitive trace mechanism.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime circles, finite-dimensional return matrices, local transverse multipliers, the global cohomology completion, and the archimedean exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE FORMULA, TRACE).** Finite-dimensional cohomology preserves the geometric prime orbit list but cannot produce delta contributions at the orbit periods; restoring those deltas reinstates the infinite circle spectrum or a forbidden regularized trace.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Finite-dimensional Lefschetz cohomology has no period delta trace.** Ordinary finite-dimensional traces are smooth functions of time; exact periodic-orbit distributions require infinite spectral multiplicity or a nonordinary trace.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 24

The next candidate must retain a genuine period-delta trace while avoiding full per-prime circle spectra, perhaps through a single global distributional spectral object whose trace class can be proved directly. It must not use zeta traces, b-traces, cutoffs, or subtraction.

## Candidate 24: Global prime-period spectral measure

### CONSTRUCTION

Attempt to define one global unitary flow U_t on a Hilbert space with a positive spectral measure mu, without decomposing it into prime sectors, such that for every compactly supported test function phi its ordinary smeared trace has the prime-period contribution
\\[
\\sum_p\\log p\\sum_{m\\ge1}\\phi(m\\log p).
\\]
The archimedean stationary point with exponent -2 is included separately. The measure is defined only from primes and does not use zero data.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The single measure mu replaces the separate Z_p^m transversals and is intended to provide one global spectrally compact cohomology. It has no single scale q; the support is the full prime-period set. The measure itself is proposed as the replacement for Assumption (iv).

### ORBITS

The desired formal orbit data are one orbit of length log 2 and one of length log 3, with iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3 and sign +1. However, the construction starts from a spectral measure rather than a foliated flow with those closed orbits. The orbit geometry is not produced by mu.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The coefficient log p is built into the target measure, not produced by an additive-adelic transverse return or a Lefschetz determinant. The p^-m negative-time factors would likewise have to be appended to the measure.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The archimedean term is appended as a separate stationary contribution with exponent -2.

### SPECTRUM

If the smeared trace is the Fourier transform of mu, the required prime-period distribution fixes the corresponding two-sided spectral distribution by Fourier transform. For each prime p, the periodic delta train at m log p has Fourier transform a frequency comb with spacing 2pi/log p. Therefore the total spectral measure is, up to the prescribed normalization, the sum of the full circle combs for all primes. The construction has only renamed the direct sum; it has not removed its spectral density.

### TRACE CLASS

Fourier uniqueness means there is no alternative positive spectral measure with the same trace distribution but a smaller singular-value density. The comb for each p contributes infinitely many modes, and the sum over primes has the established divergent trace norm for nonzero smearings. If one changes mu to make the smeared operator trace class, its Fourier transform changes and the exact prime-period trace formula fails. If one permits a signed or distributional cancellation, the result is no longer an ordinary positive Hilbert trace and falls outside Gate 1.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, the target prime-period distribution, Fourier transformation, formal archimedean exponent -2, and spectral-measure theory. No zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** A global spectral measure with the exact prime-period trace is uniquely forced to have the same comb spectrum as the per-prime circle model, so global notation cannot evade the trace obstruction.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Fourier uniqueness forces the prime-period spectral comb.** Any ordinary spectral realization of the exact prime-period distribution inherits the full circle-comb density; trace-class improvement necessarily changes the trace formula or leaves the ordinary Hilbert setting.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 25

The next candidate must abandon a positive spectral-measure realization and use a genuinely geometric supertrace cancellation that is trace class term-by-term, while preserving the prime-period distribution without signed/distributional regularization.

## Candidate 25: Graded de Rham supertrace cancellation

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, use the circle C_p of length log p and its de Rham complex
\\[
0\\longrightarrow \\Omega^0(C_p)\\xrightarrow{d}\\Omega^1(C_p)\\longrightarrow0.
\\]
Let the flow translate forms on the circle, with a local transverse return multiplier p^-1 and a separate stationary archimedean point of exponent -2. Take the global graded cohomology as the direct sum over p, with the alternating trace intended to cancel matching Fourier modes between degrees 0 and 1. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The graded de Rham complex replaces the finite harmonic sector of the one-prime working model. The two degrees provide an intrinsic cohomological cancellation mechanism in place of Assumption (iv). Prime circles and their local return maps are retained.

### ORBITS

For p=2 and p=3 there is one primitive orbit of lengths log 2 and log 3, with iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. Translation preserves the de Rham grading and the local Lefschetz signs can be arranged to be +1 for the geometric orbit contribution. No mixed orbits are introduced.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local transverse multiplier p^-1 supplies p^-m in negative time. The de Rham grading does not alter that local factor.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included separately.

### SPECTRUM

On each circle, both degrees contain the full Fourier spectrum \\(2\\pi k/\\log p\\), k in Z. The degree-0 and degree-1 spectra match, so their formal supertrace cancels nonzero Fourier modes. The uncancelled index contribution is finite-dimensional.

### TRACE CLASS

This mechanism fails the Gate condition before taking the supertrace. For a nonzero compactly supported test function phi, the smeared translation on each degree has singular values
\\[
\\left|\\widehat\\phi(2\\pi k/\\log p)\\right|,\\qquad k\\in\\mathbb Z,
\\]
and is not trace class globally over p. The two non-trace-class operators may have a formally cancelling difference, but Gate 1 requires every A_j(phi) to be ordinary trace class, not merely their alternating sum. If one removes the nonzero Fourier modes before forming the degrees, the remaining constant-mode contribution is the Candidate 6 divergence and loses period sensitivity. If one inserts heat smoothing, the exact prime Lefschetz distribution is changed and the construction becomes Candidate 13's incompatible regularization.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime circles, the de Rham complex, local p-adic multipliers, translation on forms, the graded direct sum, and the boundary exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** Supertrace cancellation is formal because the individual graded smeared operators are not trace class. Making them trace class by truncation or smoothing either loses the prime-period delta trace or violates the no-regularization condition.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Supertrace cancellation is insufficient when each graded trace must be trace class.** Cohomological cancellation can remove divergent terms only after subtraction between non-trace-class operators, which Gate 1 explicitly forbids.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 26

The next candidate must realize cancellation inside each individual degree—so every smeared \\(A_j(\\phi)\\) is trace class—while retaining the period-delta orbit trace and positive Lefschetz signs. Cross-degree cancellation alone is no longer admissible.

## Candidate 26: Translation-invariant anisotropic Hilbert cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime circle C_p of length log p, choose an anisotropic Sobolev/Hilbert norm that weights its Fourier coefficient c_k by a positive sequence w_{p,k}, and require the translation flow to act continuously and isometrically on the completed space. Use one graded degree only, include the local transverse multiplier p^-1, and add the stationary archimedean point with exponent -2. The weights are intended to create compact embedding and trace-class smeared translation without cross-degree cancellation.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The anisotropic norm replaces the finite harmonic projection in Assumption (iv). The prime circle and local return map remain unchanged. Unlike heat smoothing, the proposal is to define the cohomology itself with the anisotropic norm so no separate regularization is inserted.

### ORBITS

The geometry has one primitive orbit for each prime: log 2 and 2 log 2 for the first two iterates of p=2, and log 3 and 2 log 3 for p=3. The local Lefschetz signs can remain +1. No mixed orbits are introduced.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local transverse return supplies p^-m in negative time. The anisotropic norm is not itself used as a modular factor.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included.

### SPECTRUM

Translation acts diagonally on Fourier modes with eigenvalues e^{2pi i k t/log p}. For the norm to be flow-invariant, the weights w_{p,k} may change the topology but not the eigenvalues or the singular values of the smeared diagonal multiplier relative to an orthonormalized Fourier basis. The smeared block still has multiplier \\widehat\\phi(2pi k/log p).

### TRACE CLASS

If the anisotropic norm commutes with translation, it is unitarily equivalent after renormalizing the Fourier basis to a weighted diagonal representation. The singular values remain
\\[
|\\widehat\\phi(2\\pi k/\\log p)|.
\\]
The established full-circle divergence therefore persists.

If the norm is chosen so that the translation is not bounded or not isometric, the proposed cohomology is not preserved by the flow, so A_j(phi) is not defined on one fixed Hilbert space. Introducing a separate compact embedding or projection produces Candidate 13/25-type regularization or cross-degree cancellation. Thus internal anisotropy cannot simultaneously preserve the flow and change the trace-class singular values.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime circles, Fourier-weighted Hilbert norms, local p^-1 return factors, translation flow, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** A flow-invariant anisotropic norm is only a reparametrization of the Fourier modes and does not alter the non-trace-class smeared multiplier; a norm that changes it destroys flow invariance.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Translation-invariant anisotropic norms do not alter Fourier singular values.** Internal Hilbert geometry cannot create trace class unless it changes the flow representation or inserts a forbidden smoothing/projection.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 27

The next candidate must change the flow representation itself inside each degree, not merely its invariant norm, while retaining exact prime-period delta traces and ordinary trace class.

## Candidate 27: Compact-resolvent dissipative flow representation

### CONSTRUCTION

On each prime circle use a Fourier basis indexed by k and replace the unitary translation generator by
\\[
G_p=-\\alpha_p|D_p|+iD_p,
\\qquad
D_p e_{p,k}=\\frac{2\\pi k}{\\log p}e_{p,k},
\\]
with \\(\\alpha_p>0\\). The forward evolution is the semigroup
\\[
V_p(t)=e^{tG_p}.
\\]
Choose the damping rates \\alpha_p so that the direct global sum of smeared semigroup operators is trace class. Retain the prime orbit circles, local p^-1 multiplier, and the stationary point of exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The damped generator replaces the unitary leafwise flow representation and is intended to replace Assumption (iv) by intrinsic spectral damping. The base orbit lengths and local modular returns are kept formally, but the cohomological evolution is no longer pure pullback by the geometric flow.

### ORBITS

The base geometry still has one primitive orbit of length log p and its iterates. For p=2 and p=3 the first two lengths are log 2, 2 log 2 and log 3, 2 log 3. But V_p(t) is a forward semigroup, not an invertible flow: V_p(-t) is unbounded because e^{+\\alpha_p|D_p|} is unbounded. The return operator cannot be the pullback of a flow preserving one fixed Hilbert cohomology. The periodic Lefschetz interpretation therefore fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local p^-m factor can still be assigned to the geometric transverse return, but the damping adds e^{-\\alpha_p m|D_p|} to every Fourier mode. This changes the orbit contribution from a pure Lefschetz coefficient to a damping-dependent spectral sum.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is discrete and globally damped. With sufficiently increasing \\alpha_p, a positive-time smeared semigroup can be trace class. This is the intended spectral improvement.

### TRACE CLASS

For positive t, the exponential damping can make each Fourier block trace class and can be tuned so the prime sum converges. However, the Gate operator is defined from \\((\\phi^t)^*\\) for a flow, which requires a two-sided group action or at least a bounded inverse on the cohomology. Here the inverse is unbounded. If the damping is removed to restore invertibility, Candidate 26/25's non-trace-class spectrum returns. If the damping remains, the trace formula depends on \\alpha_p and no longer equals the exact prime-period distribution for all test functions.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime circles, Fourier generators, damping rates, local p^-1 factors, the semigroup, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE FORMULA).** Dissipation can create trace class only by replacing the required invertible flow with a semigroup and changing the Lefschetz coefficients.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Dissipative semigroup is not an invertible flow.** Compact-resolvent damping supplies summability at the price of unbounded backward evolution and a modified trace distribution.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 28

The next candidate must retain a boundedly invertible flow while obtaining compact spectral behavior through a mechanism other than damping, norm weighting, or cross-degree cancellation.

## Candidate 28: Hyperbolic anisotropic solenoid flow

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, use a compact solenoid transversal with an invertible hyperbolic automorphism \\(R_p\\) having stable and unstable directions. Form a suspension over a circle of length log p, with return map R_p and local arithmetic scaling p^-1. Define the cohomology on an anisotropic Sobolev space that strengthens regularity in stable directions and weakens it in unstable directions, as in Ruelle-resonance constructions. Add a stationary boundary point with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The hyperbolic solenoid replaces Z_p^m and supplies an invertible global return. The local hyperbolic rates replace the scale q and the anisotropic Sobolev space replaces Assumption (iv) by suppressing unstable distributions and retaining a discrete resonance spectrum.

### ORBITS

The base suspension has one formal prime orbit for each p, with lengths log 2 and log 3 and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. However, the solenoid automorphism has its own periodic points. Unless the transverse periodic points are removed by a non-invariant restriction, the suspension acquires additional closed orbits and multiplicities not indexed solely by primes. Removing them destroys the invariant anisotropic space or changes the Lefschetz trace. Gate ORBITS is not established.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The transverse hyperbolic return can carry the p^-m Jacobian factor, but stable/unstable resonance weights add further determinants and multiplicities. The exact pure prime coefficient requires a separate cancellation not supplied by anisotropic regularity.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A boundary stationary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

Anisotropic spaces can turn the transfer operator into a discrete resonance problem, but the pullback of an invertible hyperbolic map is generally bounded only between different anisotropic spaces. On one fixed anisotropic Hilbert space, either the map is not bounded in both directions or the space is weakened enough to retain the original infinite spectrum.

### TRACE CLASS

If a transfer semigroup is made trace class by anisotropic smoothing, its trace is a Ruelle/distributional trace over all periodic points of the hyperbolic map. It is not the ordinary trace of a bounded two-sided flow on one fixed Hilbert cohomology, and the additional transverse periodic points violate the prime-only orbit list. If the anisotropic construction is forced to preserve one fixed Hilbert space and ordinary trace class, the compactness mechanism disappears; if it retains resonance trace, it uses a nonordinary distributional framework outside Gate 1.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime periods, compact hyperbolic solenoids, stable/unstable rates, anisotropic Sobolev norms, local arithmetic scaling, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS).** Hyperbolic anisotropic regularity can produce resonance traces, but not an ordinary trace-class two-sided flow on one fixed Hilbert cohomology with only prime closed orbits.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Hyperbolic anisotropic spaces are not invariant Hilbert trace-class cohomology.** Resonance methods trade ordinary Hilbert trace class and exact orbit isolation for anisotropic/distributional trace formulas.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 29

The next candidate must avoid both nonordinary resonance traces and extra transverse periodic points, while retaining a bounded invertible global flow and ordinary trace class.

## Candidate 29: Aperiodic transverse rotation over prime suspensions

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p, take a prime suspension circle C_p of length log p and a compact transversal T=S^1 with irrational rotation
\\[
R_p(\\theta)=\\theta+\\alpha_p\\pmod 1,
\\]
where \\(\\alpha_p=\\sqrt 2\\,\\log p\\pmod 1\\). Use the mapping torus of R_p, so the return after one prime circuit is invertible and has no periodic transverse points. Use Haar \\(L^2(S^1)\\) cohomology and include a stationary boundary point with exponent -2. The construction is zero-independent.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The common compact circle transversal replaces Z_p^m. The prime period log p replaces q, while the irrational rotation replaces Assumption (iv) by eliminating all nontrivial finite transverse periodic modes. No local p-adic Jacobian is present, so the modular factor would have to be supplied by an additional additive-adelic cocycle.

### ORBITS

The base suspension has one primitive orbit for p=2 of length log 2 and one for p=3 of length log 3, with iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3. Because the transverse rotations are irrational, there are no additional transverse periodic points. This avoids Candidate 28's orbit proliferation, but the base prime suspensions remain separate sectors.

### MODULAR FACTORS

An irrational circle rotation preserves Haar measure and has Jacobian 1, so it produces no p^-m factor. Appending p^-m as a scalar is not a transverse return determinant. Thus the modular requirement fails unless a separate additive-adelic factor is added, which returns to the previous infinite-spectrum problem.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 is included explicitly.

### SPECTRUM

The rotation has eigenvalues e^{2pi i n alpha_p}, n in Z, and hence an infinite discrete spectrum in every prime sector. The full space is a direct sum over p of these spectra.

### TRACE CLASS

For any nonzero compactly supported test function phi whose Fourier transform is nonzero at infinitely many rotation frequencies, the smeared operator has infinitely many nonzero singular values in each p-sector. It is not trace class even before summing over p. Removing all nonconstant rotation modes leaves the constant mode and returns Candidate 6. Adding intrinsic smoothing changes the return trace and either breaks the rotation invariance or introduces a regularization. Therefore aperiodicity removes extra orbit terms but does not give trace class.

### INPUTS

The inputs are primes, prime periods, irrational rotations, Haar measure, mapping-torus geometry, formal modular labels, and exponent -2. No zeta-zero locations or equivalent zero data are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE).** Aperiodic transverse dynamics avoids extra periodic orbits but retains an infinite unitary spectrum and supplies no arithmetic modular factor.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Aperiodic transverse dynamics is trace-continuous, not periodic.** Removing transverse periodic points avoids orbit contamination but leaves noncompact smeared spectrum and does not generate p^-m.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 30

The next pass must be a consolidation. It must compare hyperbolic and aperiodic transverse dynamics and formulate a no-go theorem for compact invertible transversals: eliminating extra periodic points leaves infinite spectrum, while creating spectral compactness introduces extra periodic/resonant data or nonordinary traces.



## Consolidation 30: Compact invertible transversals

### CLASS UNDER TEST

Consider a prime suspension whose transverse space is a compact group or compact manifold, whose return map is invertible, and whose cohomology is represented by a standard Haar/Koopman Hilbert space. Require:

1. no transverse periodic points except the designated prime base orbit;
2. ordinary trace class for every nonzero phi in C_c^\\infty((0,infty));
3. the exact prime Lefschetz trace with no regularization.

### PROVED SUBCLASS: COMPACT GROUP ROTATIONS

For a compact abelian transversal with Haar representation, the character decomposition is diagonal. If the transversal is infinite and the action is aperiodic, infinitely many characters occur. A nonzero smeared translation has nonzero multipliers on infinitely many characters unless the test transform vanishes on the entire relevant character set. Hence the smeared operator is not finite rank; in the standard infinite-character cases it is not trace class. Removing all nonconstant characters leaves the constant mode, which loses period-sensitive data and gives the known infinite prime-sector identity contribution.

If the compact group is finite, its action is finite-dimensional and trace class, but it supplies no infinite-dimensional spectral mechanism and its measure-preserving return has Jacobian 1, so it cannot generate the required p^-m modular factor. A non-volume-preserving finite model requires an additional measure/cocycle and no longer has the canonical Haar return.

### PROVED SUBCLASS: HYPERBOLIC COMPACT MODELS WITH STANDARD TRANSFER TRACE

For a hyperbolic compact return map, periodic transverse points contribute to the Lefschetz/Ruelle trace. Unless they are removed by a non-invariant restriction, they create additional closed orbits beyond the prime base orbit. Anisotropic spaces can make transfer operators nuclear only in a resonance/distributional trace framework; that is not ordinary trace class of a bounded two-sided flow on one fixed Hilbert space. The alternative of retaining ordinary Hilbert Koopman dynamics leaves the infinite spectrum.

### WHAT IS NOT PROVED

This does not rule out every compact invertible transverse model. In particular, it does not exclude a new non-Haar, non-Koopman cohomology with a canonical finite or summable spectrum and an exact additive Haar Jacobian. It proves only the stated Haar/Koopman and standard hyperbolic-transfer subclasses.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The two branches are forced by the requirement to remove extra periodic points:

- aperiodic compact Haar dynamics has infinite character spectrum;
- hyperbolic/periodic dynamics has transverse periodic data.

The conclusion is not a claim that every compact transversal fails; the open class is precisely a new cohomological representation that is neither ordinary Haar/Koopman nor a regularized anisotropic transfer representation.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The adelic replacement for Z_p^m cannot be obtained by simply choosing a compact transversal and then selecting either its Haar spectrum or its standard hyperbolic resonance space. A successful replacement must explain, intrinsically and zero-independently, how an infinite-dimensional \\(H^1\\) can be spectrally compact while preserving the full arithmetic return and producing no extra transverse closed orbits.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**PROVED for compact Haar/Koopman and standard hyperbolic-transfer subclasses; PARTIAL globally.**

\\[
D e_n=E_n e_n,\\qquad E_n=n^2.

\\[
\\mathcal H_{\\mathrm{HS}}=\\mathcal S_2(\\mathcal K)
\\]
as one global cohomological degree, with flow
\\[
U_t(T)=e^{itD}T e^{-itD}.
\\]
The matrix unit \\(E_{mn}\\) has frequency \\(E_m-E_n\\). Prime translations are represented by designated energy differences, while a separate geometric suspension supplies formal lengths log p. Add the stationary boundary point with exponent -2. No zero data are used.

The Hilbert-Schmidt operator space replaces all local p-adic transversals by one global noncommutative cohomology. The construction is genuinely global and does not use per-prime circle sums.

Choosing a different operator space with no diagonal fixed points changes the representation and requires a new geometric justification.

Let X = A_f^× / Q_{>0}^×, where A_f^× is the finite idèle group and Q_{>0}^× acts by diagonal multiplication. Use the quotient as the global transverse space and let the modulus flow act through the norm coordinate. On the regular Hilbert space L²(X) use the induced scaling representation; remove the constant/fixed sector by the canonical reduced space orthogonal to invariant vectors. Prime multiplication is represented by the rational correspondences x ↦ p x before passage to the quotient.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The finite idèle class quotient replaces the product of local p-adic transversals and identifies all rational scaling orbits canonically. The quotient is intended to remove the infinitely many copies of each ratio from Candidate 33. The reduced representation is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv).

### ORBITS

After quotienting by Q_{>0}^×, multiplication by any prime p is the identity on X: [p x] = [x]. Consequently the quotient has no nontrivial prime return map and cannot carry a primitive orbit of length log p. Before quotienting, prime multiplication is not a periodic flow but a discrete correspondence. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The finite idèle norm changes by p under multiplication by p, but that norm is killed if the full Q_{>0}^× quotient is taken. If the norm coordinate is retained, the space has a noncompact R_{>0} modulus direction and the p^{-m} factors occur only as a Jacobian/character weight, not as a trace-class return operator. Thus the construction has an either-or obstruction: quotienting removes prime dynamics; retaining modulus leaves the noncompact factor.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A compactification can adjoin an archimedean boundary point with exponent -2, but it is not produced by the finite idèle quotient itself. The required archimedean term is external.

### SPECTRUM

On the full idèle class space, harmonic analysis contains the modulus character line and a continuous spectral parameter. On the quotient that kills the modulus, the prime scaling action becomes trivial. Removing invariant vectors does not restore nontrivial prime periods.

### TRACE CLASS

In the quotient model, the arithmetic prime operators are identities and provide no required trace distribution. In the modulus-retaining model, the regular representation on the R_{>0} factor is the translation/dilation representation with continuous spectrum; for nonzero compactly supported φ, the smeared multiplier is noncompact and not trace class. This is an exact dichotomy, not a numerical failure.

### INPUTS

The inputs are finite idèles, the diagonal rational scaling action, the quotient or its modulus-retaining cover, Haar measure, and the reduced regular representation. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): partial — the idèle norm supplies a logarithmic coordinate, but quotienting destroys the prime return data.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — no positivity claim is needed for Gate 1.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): unknown — no complete involution implementing s ↔ 1-s is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — no determinant identity with Xi is available.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — neither quotient branch identifies zero locations.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Full rational quotient removes the prime dynamics; retaining the modulus preserves a noncompact continuous factor whose smeared regular representation is not trace class.

### FAILURE CLASS

Rational-quotient dichotomy. A quotient that identifies all rational scaling orbits makes prime multiplication trivial, while a quotient that retains the logarithmic modulus retains noncompact continuous spectrum.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 35

The next candidate must preserve nontrivial prime return maps without retaining an uncompactified modulus and must provide a canonical finite-multiplicity spectral selection. A quotient by all rational scaling is disallowed, as is an uncured continuous modulus factor.

\n## Candidate 35: Compact arithmetic Kronecker modulus

### CONSTRUCTION

Let X = T^P be the product torus indexed by the primes, with Haar probability measure, and let the flow be
φ^t((z_p)_p) = (e^{it log p} z_p)_p.
The prime logarithms are encoded as the coordinates of one global compact rotation. Use the reduced Koopman representation on L²(X) after removing the constant vector. The character indexed by a finitely supported integer vector k has frequency sum_p k_p log p = log(r/s), where r and s are positive integers. A prime frequency log p is the character with k_p = 1.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The compact torus replaces the noncompact modulus in Candidate 34 and provides one global arithmetic transversal. The reduced character space replaces Assumption (iv): constants are removed and all remaining modes are globally indexed by finite-support prime exponent vectors. No zero data are used.

### ORBITS

A point is periodic with period T > 0 only if T log p belongs to 2πZ for every prime coordinate. For p=2 and p=3 this would imply log 2/log 3 is rational, which is false. Hence the flow has no nonstationary periodic points at all. The characters carry frequencies log p and 2 log p, but they are not geometric closed orbits and have no Lefschetz signs. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The torus rotation preserves Haar measure, so its transverse Jacobian is 1. No p^(-m) factor arises in negative time. Adding p^(-m) as a character weight is external to the flow. MODULAR fails.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary boundary point with exponent -2 can be adjoined as a separate compactification stratum, but the Kronecker flow does not generate it intrinsically.

### SPECTRUM

The reduced Koopman spectrum is pure point but countably infinite, with one character for every finitely supported integer vector. Distinct vectors give distinct frequencies because the prime logarithms are Q-linearly independent. Thus the spectrum is globally arithmetic but has infinitely many modes at unbounded frequency.

### TRACE CLASS

For φ in C_c^∞((0,∞)), the smeared Koopman operator is diagonal on characters with eigenvalues φ-hat(sum_p k_p log p). There are infinitely many character frequencies in every sufficiently large logarithmic region, and Fourier decay alone does not make the full character sum trace class: for each fixed prime p, vectors with positive and negative exponents in other primes generate infinitely many modes whose frequencies remain in bounded translated sets. More directly, the compact rotation has a countably infinite dual with no compact-resolvent generator; the multiplier is nonzero on infinitely many characters for a generic φ. Therefore A(φ) is not trace class.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the prime set, the product torus, Haar measure, and the rotation vector (log p)_p. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): partial — finite-support character frequencies are exact logarithms of rational numbers, including prime iterates.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — no positivity claim is made.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): unknown — no involution implementing s ↔ 1-s is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — there is no determinant identity with Xi.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — the spectrum is the character spectrum of a Kronecker flow and has no theorem relating it to zero locations.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Compactifying the modulus removes the continuous spectrum but, because the prime logarithms are rationally independent, it removes all periodic orbits and leaves an infinite non-trace-class character spectrum.

### FAILURE CLASS

Compact arithmetic modulus is aperiodic. Encoding all independent prime logarithms in one compact rotation preserves their additive frequencies but cannot produce periodic points or ordinary trace-class smearing.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 36

The next candidate must preserve compactness and finite spectral multiplicity while introducing prime periodicity through a geometric suspension or quotient mechanism; a pure Kronecker rotation is insufficient.

\n## Candidate 36: Single global arithmetic suspension

### CONSTRUCTION

Let Y = T^P with the prime-log Kronecker flow R_t from Candidate 35. Form a single suspension over Y using a compact roof space whose return maps are the commuting translations R_{log p}. The intended flow moves through one global cross-section and applies the prime translation when it reaches the corresponding roof face. Use the reduced leafwise cohomology of this suspension, with a transverse spectral cutoff selected by the Laplacian on the compact torus and then completed over all cutoff levels.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The one global suspension replaces the separate prime circles and avoids an explicit direct sum of prime blocks. The compact torus replaces Z_p^m, while the transverse Laplacian spectral filtration replaces Assumption (iv). Prime lengths are placed in the roof data, and the common suspension is intended to prevent independent copies of each circle spectrum.

### ORBITS

A single suspension with return translations for p=2 and p=3 has the primitive returns log 2 and log 3 only if the roof dynamics forbids concatenation. If both return maps are available from the same section, the concatenated word (2,3) is also a closed return with length log 2 + log 3 = log 6, and its repetitions produce m log 6. More generally every finite word in prime labels creates a mixed periodic word unless the corresponding transition is forbidden. Forbidding all mixed words decomposes the system into prime sectors and returns to the direct-sum obstruction. Thus the prime-only orbit requirement fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The roof translations preserve Haar measure on Y, so no p^{-m} Jacobian arises. A roof weight p^{-m} can be assigned to a return, but this is an external cocycle and not a transverse Jacobian of the compact torus. MODULAR fails.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary compactification boundary point with exponent -2 may be added, but it is not generated by the suspension or torus Laplacian.

### SPECTRUM

The global suspension has a transfer operator containing all admissible finite words in the prime return maps. If mixed words are allowed, the spectrum records the additive semigroup generated by all log p, including log 6 and other composite word lengths. If mixed words are removed, the Hilbert space splits into prime-labelled invariant sectors and the established prime-block trace divergence returns.

### TRACE CLASS

The Laplacian cutoff gives finite-dimensional approximants, but the full completed spectral space has infinitely many torus characters in every cutoff limit. If mixed words are allowed, the transfer spectrum contains the global word semigroup and cannot have the required prime-only trace. If mixed words are suppressed by orthogonal sector restrictions, each surviving prime sector retains the non-trace-class circle/return spectrum. Finite cutoff positivity or trace class therefore does not yield an ordinary trace-class operator on the completed space.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the compact product torus, prime logarithms, a global suspension roof, Haar measure, commuting prime translations, and a Laplacian spectral filtration. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): partial — prime logarithms enter as roof lengths, but the trace also contains mixed additive words.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — no positivity claim is made.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): unknown — no involution implementing s ↔ 1-s is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — no canonical determinant identity with Xi exists.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — no spectral theorem identifies zeros.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, TRACE). A connected global suspension either admits mixed prime words, producing composite-word orbit terms, or forbids them by decomposing into prime sectors, restoring the known trace-class obstruction.

### FAILURE CLASS

Global-suspension mixed-word dichotomy. Connecting prime returns in one system creates unwanted composite words; forbidding those words forces a disconnected/direct-sum decomposition.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 37

The next candidate must realize prime closed orbits without a concatenable common return section, while still using one global cohomological Hilbert space and producing modular Jacobians intrinsically. A finite spectral cutoff or an externally assigned roof weight is insufficient.

\n## Candidate 37: Branched one-way prime suspension

### CONSTRUCTION

Take one compact branching cross-section with disjoint prime-labelled gates G_p. A trajectory entering G_p is sent around a loop of length log p and returns to G_p, while transitions from G_p to G_q for p ≠ q are forbidden by directed gate rules. Attach a finite-dimensional transverse fiber to each gate and a common boundary fiber at the branch locus. The intended global flow is the suspension of this directed return system, with leafwise cohomology obtained from the gate complex.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The branch locus replaces the separate local transversals and the gate complex replaces Assumption (iv) by a finite-channel selection rule. Prime loops are geometrically present, but the directed gate rule is introduced specifically to prevent mixed words. The construction is deliberately different from Candidate 36 because the return relation is a directed graph rather than a common invertible section.

### ORBITS

The allowed primitive closed trajectories are one loop at each prime, with lengths log 2 and log 3, and iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3, all with chosen Lefschetz sign +1. Mixed words are excluded by the directed gate relation. This matches the desired orbit list at the combinatorial level.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The gate dynamics is combinatorial and carries no p-adic Jacobian. Assigning the transition G_p → G_p weight p^{-1} gives p^{-m} on iterates, but this is a prescribed edge weight, not a transverse Haar scaling. MODULAR fails intrinsically.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A boundary vertex can be declared stationary with transverse exponent -2, yielding the formal archimedean factor. The exponent is an attached datum and is not forced by the gate geometry.

### SPECTRUM

The directed return operator has one prime loop per gate and no mixed cycles. However, a directed non-invertible return graph is not the time-one map of a two-sided flow: distinct incoming states merge at the branch locus or outgoing states are deleted. If the graph is replaced by an invertible flow, the missing reverse transitions restore mixed cycles or split the system into disconnected prime components.

### TRACE CLASS

With finitely many channels per gate, the orbit trace has the desired formal prime comb, but the infinite family of prime loop sectors gives the established divergent full-circle trace unless a noncanonical spectral damping is imposed. With one eigenmode per gate, the trace can be summable only by inserting prime-dependent weights or frequencies; that changes the required Lefschetz trace. Thus no ordinary trace-class cohomology satisfying the exact formula is obtained.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the prime labels, directed gate graph, loop lengths log p, finite gate fibers, and optional edge weights p^{-1}. No zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): partial — prime lengths are exact, but modular weights are external and the directed graph is not a multiplicative geometric action.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — no positivity claim is made.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): unknown — no involution s ↔ 1-s is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — no Xi determinant identity exists.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — no zero data appear as spectral data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(MODULAR, TRACE, FLOW-INVERTIBILITY). The gate rules reproduce the prime orbit list only by abandoning an invertible flow or by adding external weights; restoring invertibility reintroduces mixed words or direct-sum divergence.

### FAILURE CLASS

Directed-gate obstruction. Prime-only symbolic dynamics can suppress mixed words, but the suppression is incompatible with a two-sided invertible flow unless the prime sectors decouple.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 38

The next candidate must obtain prime-only cycles from an invertible geometric action without directed gate restrictions, and must generate p^{-m} from an actual transverse Jacobian rather than edge weights.

\n## Candidate 38: Invertible prime-loop groupoid with wandering corridors

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p take a mapping torus L_p of a circle of length log p. Do not identify the base points of different L_p. Instead connect the components by invertible heteroclinic corridors C_{p,q} whose forward and backward trajectories escape every compact set and never return to a prime loop. The total space is the disjoint union of prime loop interiors plus the corridor groupoid completion. The flow is invertible on the completed groupoid. Leafwise cohomology is formed from a single global direct-integral Hilbert space with the corridor part included, and a transverse Jacobian is prescribed on each prime loop by the p-adic normal dilation.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The prime loops replace the individual finite-field mapping tori, while the corridor groupoid is the proposed global replacement for the family of local transversals. The escaping corridors replace a shared return section and are intended to keep the flow connected without creating mixed periodic words. A global leafwise compactness condition is intended to replace Assumption (iv).

### ORBITS

Each prime loop has a primitive orbit of length log p and iterates m log p with sign +1. Because corridors are wandering and never return, no mixed prime word is closed. At the orbit level this gives the required prime-only list.

### MODULAR FACTORS

On the p-loop normal coordinate use multiplication by p under one return, so its mth iterate has Jacobian p^(-m) in negative time. This is an actual local Jacobian, not an edge weight. However, the p-dependent normal structures are still attached separately to the prime loops; the global corridor geometry does not derive them from one common adelic transversal.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

Adjoin a boundary compactification point at the end of the corridor system and assign the normal exponent -2. This produces the formal archimedean factor, but the exponent is a boundary datum not forced by the corridor construction.

### SPECTRUM

The periodic loop sectors contribute one full circle spectrum per prime unless the leafwise cohomology is compressed. The corridor sector has continuous or scattering spectrum because its trajectories escape. Thus the global spectrum is either an infinite prime direct sum plus a corridor continuous part, or it uses a noncanonical projection that removes those sectors.

### TRACE CLASS

For a nonzero test φ, each prime loop’s full circle spectrum contributes a trace norm bounded below at the established rate proportional to (log p) times a nonzero Fourier norm. Summing over primes diverges. The wandering corridor contribution is not trace class on the natural L² space because translation along an escaping corridor has continuous spectrum. Replacing L² by a scattering or anisotropic space changes the trace to a distributional/regularized trace, forbidden by Gate 1. Hence no ordinary trace-class A_j(φ) exists.

### FAILURE CLASS

\n## Candidate 39: One-mode global Lefschetz cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p take a prime-loop mapping torus with a one-dimensional reduced harmonic line V_p rather than its full circle cohomology. Form the Hilbert direct sum H = ⊕_p V_p together with one archimedean line V_∞. The cohomology is globally indexed by prime lines, with no separate nonconstant Fourier modes.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The one-dimensional V_p is a proposed global replacement for the finite-dimensional harmonic space in the working model, and the direct sum is intended to retain only the Lefschetz mode that contributes to the orbit trace. The p^{-1} return is a genuine local Jacobian. This is a finite-multiplicity compression rather than a full prime-circle spectrum.

### ORBITS

The underlying mapping tori have one primitive orbit for p=2 and p=3, of lengths log 2 and log 3, with iterates 2 log 2 and 2 log 3 and sign +1. No mixed words are present because the prime loops are not connected by a return section.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The normal return map on V_p is multiplication by p^{-1}; its mth iterate contributes p^{-m}. This part is intrinsic to the local p-adic normal model, but the family of normal models is still assembled prime by prime rather than derived from one global transversal.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The extra line V_∞ is declared stationary with exponent -2, giving the formal factor (1 - e^{-2t})^{-1}. The exponent is attached as boundary data rather than derived from the global construction.

There is one phase mode per prime and no full circle spectrum. This removes the infinite Fourier multiplicity, but it leaves a countable prime-indexed direct sum. The orbit lengths are external labels on the lines rather than eigenperiods of a common geometric flow.

### TRACE CLASS

For a compactly supported test φ, the smeared operator has one contribution φ(log p) on each prime line. Even before accounting for the required coefficient, the trace-class question depends on sum_p |φ(log p)|, which is finite for compact support because only finitely many primes satisfy log p in the support. However, the exact trace is an integer-multiplicity sum: each one-dimensional line contributes coefficient 1 (or a fixed integer superdimension). The target coefficient is log p. An ordinary trace of a flow on a finite-dimensional cohomology line cannot produce the continuously varying coefficient log p. Putting log p into the Hilbert-space norm does not change the trace; putting it into the operator changes the Lefschetz return data and is an external weight. Thus the exact Gate 1 trace formula fails.

### INPUTS

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — not part of Gate 1.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): unknown — no s ↔ 1-s involution is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — no determinant identity with Xi exists.

\n## Consolidation 40: finite-mode/full-mode prime-loop dichotomy

### SCOPE

This consolidation concerns constructions with isolated prime closed orbits and ordinary Hilbert-space traces, where the local contribution of each prime orbit is represented either by a finite-dimensional invariant cohomology sector or by the full period-sensitive circle/Fourier sector. It does not cover genuinely global cohomologies that are neither decomposable into prime sectors nor finite-mode local compressions.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

Let H_p be the invariant cohomological contribution attached to a prime orbit of length log p.

1. If H_p is finite-dimensional and the return operator has finite-dimensional Lefschetz supertrace, then its coefficient in the ordinary orbit trace is an integer superdimension (or an integer combination of eigenvalue multiplicities). It cannot equal log p for every prime p without inserting a non-geometric p-dependent scalar weight.

2. If H_p contains the complete period-sensitive circle spectrum required to recover all iterates m log p by ordinary Fourier/Lefschetz trace, then the smeared operator on H_p is non-trace-class for a nonzero test function, and the sum over primes is divergent. This is the established full-circle direct-sum obstruction.

Therefore every construction in this local-sector class fails at least one of exact trace coefficients or ordinary trace class.

### STATUS

**PROVED for the stated local-sector class.** Part 1 is finite-dimensional linear algebra: ordinary traces count eigenvalue multiplicities and cannot generate the continuously varying coefficient log p unless an external scalar is inserted. Part 2 is the established full-circle trace-divergence estimate. The conclusion is only **PARTIAL globally**, because a future genuinely global cohomology could avoid a prime-sector decomposition.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The class is forced by the Gate 1 requirement that prime orbits be individually identifiable and contribute separately to a prime-indexed trace. It is not a proof that every possible global construction decomposes this way; nondecomposable global mechanisms remain the open search space. The consolidation strengthens the obstruction by closing the two standard local remedies—full period sensitivity and finite-mode compression—but does not justify claiming a universal no-go theorem.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The adelic replacement for Z_p^m cannot be literal local constancy alone: finite local modes lose the log p coefficients, while full local Fourier modes lose trace class. The replacement for Assumption (iv) must therefore be a genuinely global, non-sectorial spectral compactness mechanism that still carries exact prime orbit data and modular Jacobians.

### RESULT

**CONSOLIDATION 40 — PARTIAL NO-GO.** No new candidate is added. The local finite-mode/full-mode dichotomy is closed for the stated class; the remaining search space is non-sectorial global cohomology.

\n## Candidate 41: Arithmetic Fock-space Hamiltonian

### CONSTRUCTION

Let H_F be the bosonic Fock space over l² of the primes, with orthonormal occupation basis e_n indexed by positive integers n = product_p p^{v_p(n)}. Define the arithmetic Hamiltonian H e_n = (log n)e_n, with H e_1 = 0. Prime creation operators raise n to pn, and the formal partition function is
Tr(exp(-tH)) = product_p (1 - p^(-t))^(-1) = zeta(t)
for t > 1. Use the unitary flow U_s = exp(isH) and remove the vacuum line if desired. This is one global arithmetic space, not a direct sum of prime sectors.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The full multiplicative occupation space replaces the family of local transversals. Prime creation operators replace local return maps, and the occupation Hamiltonian replaces Assumption (iv) through a global energy grading. The Euler product is built into the partition function without zero data.

### ORBITS

The basis labels n encode prime powers and the frequencies log n, but the unitary flow on the Fock basis has no geometric closed orbit with primitive length log p. Prime creation is not invertible, so it is not a two-sided flow return map. The labels are arithmetic states, not Lefschetz orbits. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The energy Boltzmann factor p^(-mt) appears in exp(-tH), but this is heat/partition damping, not the p-adic transverse Jacobian p^(-m) of a geometric return. The unitary flow itself has modulus one. MODULAR fails in the Gate 1 sense.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary exponent -2 sector can be added as an independent factor, but H_F does not produce it.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is globally discrete with eigenvalues log n and multiplicity one. Its counting function is exponential in energy: the number of n with log n ≤ T is approximately exp(T). This is the desired Euler-product density but is too large for compact-time Fourier smearing.

### TRACE CLASS

For φ in C_c^∞((0,∞)), the smeared unitary operator is diagonal with eigenvalues φ-hat(log n). Since φ-hat has only polynomial rapid decay in log n while the number of integers n near e^T grows like e^T, the sum
Σ_n |φ-hat(log n)|
diverges for generic φ. Equivalently, a compactly supported time test does not supply exponential damping in the arithmetic energy. The heat trace is finite only for Re(t)>1 and therefore does not establish the required ordinary trace class for every compactly supported time test. TRACE fails.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, bosonic occupation/Fock space, the logarithmic Hamiltonian, and prime creation operators. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): holds at the partition-function level — the occupation spectrum has the exact Euler product zeta(t), though not the required explicit-formula trace.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — the Fock Hilbert norm is positive, but this is not a positivity theorem for the desired Weil form.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): fails — H_F has no natural involution implementing s ↔ 1-s.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — the partition function is zeta(t), not a proved completed Xi determinant.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — zeros are not eigenvalues and no theorem links the spectrum to zero locations.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE, FUNCTIONAL-SYMMETRY). The Fock construction is a genuine global Euler-product object, but its exponentially dense logarithmic spectrum makes ordinary compact-time smearing non-trace-class, and its creation dynamics is not an invertible geometric flow.

### FAILURE CLASS

Euler-product density obstruction. A global occupation spectrum that realizes the Euler product has exponentially many states per logarithmic interval, so compactly supported time smearing cannot be trace class without heat-type damping forbidden by Gate 1.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 42

The next candidate must retain the exact global multiplicative bridge while reducing the exponential occupation density by a canonical cohomological cancellation that preserves ordinary trace class and an invertible flow. Heat damping or an external subtraction is disallowed.

\n## Candidate 42: Fermionic arithmetic cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

Take the fermionic Fock space Λ(l²(P)), with basis e_S indexed by finite subsets S of the primes. Define H_F e_S = (sum_{p in S} log p)e_S = log(radical(S)) e_S. The parity grading is degree mod 2. The exterior creation and annihilation operators provide a canonical differential-style pair, and the supertrace partition function formally factors as
Str(exp(-tH_F)) = product_p (1 - p^(-t)) = 1/zeta(t)
for t > 1. Use the unitary flow exp(isH_F) and retain the full graded cohomology rather than imposing a hand-chosen subtraction.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The exterior grading replaces the local finite-field cohomological grading and supplies a canonical sign cancellation for prime occupations. The global squarefree occupation space replaces the product of local transversals. The parity differential is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv), with no zeta-zero input.

### ORBITS

The basis states encode squarefree products and the creation operators encode multiplication by a prime, but creation is not invertible and no state-space trajectory is a closed orbit of length log p. The supertrace has Euler-product algebra but no Lefschetz fixed-point geometry. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The factors p^(-t) arise from heat/partition weighting by H_F, not from a p-adic transverse Jacobian of an invertible return. The unitary flow has no p^(-m) Jacobian. MODULAR fails.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary -2 boundary sector can be adjoined, but it is not generated by the fermionic complex.

### SPECTRUM

The even and odd sectors each contain exponentially many squarefree states by logarithmic energy. The alternating product is obtained only after taking an even-minus-odd supertrace; the individual degree/parity traces retain the full exponential density.

### TRACE CLASS

For a compactly supported time test φ, the smeared unitary operator on the even sector has eigenvalues φ-hat(log rad(S)) with exponentially many states in logarithmic shells, and is generically not trace class. The same holds for the odd sector. The formal Euler-product cancellation occurs between two non-trace-class quantities and is therefore not an ordinary trace-class supertrace under Gate 1. Passing to a completed virtual difference or using zeta/heat regularization would violate the requirement that each A_j(φ) be ordinary trace class with no subtraction.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the primes, exterior Fock space, parity grading, logarithmic occupation Hamiltonian, and creation/annihilation operators. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1 (multiplicative-to-additive bridge): holds formally — the alternating occupation product gives 1/zeta(t), but not the required prime-power explicit trace.

### P2 (intrinsic positivity): unknown — parity cancellation is signed, not positive.

### P3 (functional-equation symmetry): fails — no natural involution s ↔ 1-s is constructed.

### P4 (Xi identification): fails — no completed Xi determinant identity is proved.

### P5 (zero visibility): fails — zeros do not appear as spectral eigenvalues.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, FUNCTIONAL-SYMMETRY). Fermionic cancellation reproduces an Euler-product sign algebra only as a divergent supertrace; it does not furnish ordinary trace-class graded cohomology or geometric prime returns.

### FAILURE CLASS

Virtual-cancellation trace obstruction. Alternating Euler-product cancellation can occur only after subtracting individually non-trace-class sectors, so it cannot satisfy an ordinary trace-class Lefschetz formula.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 43

The next candidate must realize arithmetic cancellation within each ordinary trace-class degree, rather than between divergent even and odd sectors, while retaining invertible prime returns and genuine Jacobians.

\n## Candidate 43: Arithmetic Koszul harmonic cohomology

### CONSTRUCTION

Start with the exterior arithmetic complex from Candidate 42, but introduce the canonical Koszul differential d = sum_p a_p^* on finite-support prime occupations, with its adjoint d*. Choose coefficients a_p = 1/log(p) and define the Laplacian Δ = dd* + d*d. Take the reduced harmonic spaces H^j = ker(Δ) in each degree and let the logarithmic Hamiltonian act on them. The differential is intended to cancel paired prime-occupation states before the ordinary trace is taken.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The harmonic kernel replaces the finite-dimensional leafwise harmonic space and is a global cohomological selection mechanism rather than a parity subtraction. The prime exterior complex supplies the arithmetic input, while Δ supplies spectral compactness. No zeta-zero locations are used.

The coefficients a_p are algebraic normalization parameters and do not arise as p-adic transverse Jacobians. The unitary logarithmic flow has no p^(-m) return factor. MODULAR fails.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A stationary -2 boundary class may be added, but Δ does not derive it.

For the full exterior complex, Δ pairs most occupation states. In the simplest finite-prime truncation its harmonic cohomology is concentrated in the vacuum and top Koszul class. In the infinite-prime limit, either only a small vacuum-type harmonic space survives or the kernel ceases to be controlled because the coefficient sequence is not square-summable in the required global topology. The selection therefore cannot retain a separate mode for every prime while remaining spectrally compact.

### TRACE CLASS

If the harmonic kernel is finite or summable, its ordinary trace has only the surviving harmonic multiplicities and cannot reproduce the full prime-power distribution. If the kernel retains enough prime-labelled harmonic states to reproduce the distribution, it inherits the exponential occupation density and the non-trace-class obstruction of Candidate 42. \n## Candidate 44: Conductor-graded adelic Dirac complex

Complete each degree in the graph norm of D_c. Prime dilation x ↦ p x supplies the local arithmetic action and Haar scaling p^(-1).

The finite-adelic transversal replaces Z_p^m globally. Introducing that quotient reintroduces either mixed returns or prime-sector components. Thus the adelic transversal alone does not supply primitive closed orbits.

Haar measure satisfies d(p^m x) = p^(-m) dx, so the required local modular factor is genuinely present in the additive finite-adelic normal direction. This is a success of the candidate’s local arithmetic geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The finite-adelic complex has no archimedean boundary point. A compactification point with exponent -2 must be adjoined separately; the conductor operator does not derive it.

### SPECTRUM

The conductor levels are finite-dimensional, but the number of new vectors at level N grows with the arithmetic of N. The full locally constant space is infinite dimensional. The conductor multiplicities grow at least through the finite quotient dimensions, so the Fourier multiplier of a compact-time test is not summable in the full completion. If one projects to a summable new-vector subspace, the projection is not preserved by all prime dilations; if one retains invariance, infinitely many modes remain. Thus ordinary trace class for every A_j(phi) is not established and fails in the natural completion.

## Consolidation 50: invariant-sector normality/trace dichotomy

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers the mandated Z_hat^*-invariant modulus sector and Hilbert realizations in which the logarithmic flow is represented as a normal translation generator, together with equivalent diagonal reweightings and confining Sobolev alternatives.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

The Haar realization is H = L2(R,du), with generator A = -i d/du. Fourier transform identifies A with multiplication by lambda on nonatomic L2(R). For any nonzero compactly supported smooth test phi whose Fourier transform is nonzero on a positive-measure set, A(phi) is multiplication by phi-hat(lambda). A nonzero multiplication operator on nonatomic L2 is not compact, hence is not trace class.

Equivalent Hilbert norms obtained by positive diagonal reweighting of a discrete Dirichlet basis do not change the singular-value multiplicities of a diagonal generator. Confining norms that genuinely change the realization make translation nonunitary and the generator nonnormal; they introduce an auxiliary compact-resolvent operator, not a compact resolvent for the flow. Therefore the standard normal invariant-sector realization cannot satisfy Gate 1 trace class.

### STATUS

PARTIAL NO-GO. The first paragraph is a complete operator-theoretic argument for the normal Haar modulus representation. The extension to every possible nonnormal Hilbert norm is not proved; a future construction could use a genuinely nonnormal flow while still satisfying Gate 1. Such a construction would need an explicit invariant norm, bounded invertible flow, ordinary trace-class smearing, and the arithmetic orbit formula.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The invariant sector is forced by the updated objective addendum: retaining all Z_hat characters stacks Dirichlet-L zeros and destroys trace class, while the zero-independent selection is the Z_hat^*-invariant sector. The normality restriction is not forced for every imaginable model, so the no-go is not universal. It is forced only when the Hilbert structure is the natural Haar or normal Mellin realization.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The replacement for Assumption (iv) cannot simply be take the invariant sector: that gives a canonical zero-independent space but leaves continuous spectrum. It also cannot simply be choose a confining norm: unless that norm is geometrically forced and compatible with an invertible flow, it changes the operator class and loses normality. The remaining search space is an explicitly nonnormal but geometrically canonical invariant-sector flow.

### RESULT

CONSOLIDATION 50 — PARTIAL NO-GO. The normal/Haar invariant-sector branch is closed for ordinary trace class. The nonnormal invariant-sector branch remains open.

\n## Candidate 51: Hardy-strip invariant modulus flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let H_a be the Hardy space of functions on the horizontal strip |Im z| < a whose boundary values on both edges are square-integrable. Identify the invariant logarithmic modulus with the real boundary coordinate u. Let prime scaling act by vertical-free translation (U_t f)(z) = f(z-t), so U_{log p} represents multiplication by p in the modulus coordinate. The strip width a is a zero-independent parameter controlling allowed exponential growth and is the proposed nonnormal Hilbert realization of the invariant sector.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The Z_hat^*-invariant modulus remains the base, while the Hardy-strip boundary norm replaces the Haar norm and Assumption (iv). The strip is intended to select a discrete or controlled spectral class without a conductor cutoff. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### ORBITS

Translation on the strip is a free real translation and has no periodic points. Prime translations are labels for shifts, not primitive closed geometric orbits. A suspension would be external and returns to previous mixed-word or sector decompositions. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The Hardy norm is translation invariant in the real direction, so prime shifts have unit Jacobian. No p^(-m) factor arises. Adding a weighted composition factor is external to the invariant modulus geometry. MODULAR fails.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The strip boundaries are not stationary points of the flow, and their normal exponent is not canonically -2. A boundary condition can be chosen to mimic it, but that is not a derived archimedean contribution.

### SPECTRUM AND NORM

Fourier transform in the real coordinate still diagonalizes real translation with continuous frequency lambda. The strip norm restricts analytic continuation and controls exponential growth, but it does not turn the translation spectrum into a discrete set. The translation group is bounded and invertible, and with the standard boundary norm it remains normal/unitary. Altering the boundary weights to make it genuinely nonnormal is a similarity-type change and does not create compact spectral multiplicity. This candidate is flagged NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY for the natural norm.

### TRACE CLASS

The smeared flow remains a Fourier multiplier by phi-hat(lambda) on a continuous boundary spectrum, hence is not compact or trace class for nonzero phi. A one-sided Hardy semigroup could have a nonnormal spectrum, but it is not a two-sided invertible flow and violates Gate 1. No ordinary trace-class mechanism is obtained.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the invariant modulus, a strip width a, Hardy boundary norms, real translations, and prime logarithmic labels. No zero data are used.

### P1: partial — prime translations are represented, but no prime-orbit trace identity exists.
### P2: unknown — no positivity theorem is asserted.
### P3: partial — strip reflection z -> 1-z is suggestive, but no canonical functional-equation operator is proved.
### P4: fails — no Xi determinant identity exists.
### P5: fails — no zeros appear as eigenvalues.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE, NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY). Hardy analyticity controls strip growth but does not discretize real translations; noninvertible semigroup variants are outside the required flow class.

### FAILURE CLASS

Analytic-strip noncompactness obstruction. Analytic continuation or strip-width control does not remove the continuous translation spectrum, while one-sided analytic semigroups lose invertibility.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 52

The next candidate must use a nonnormal invariant-sector flow whose compactness is geometric rather than a similarity or analytic strip restriction, while preserving two-sided invertibility, prime return data, and the finite Jacobian.

\n## Candidate 52: Anisotropic hyperbolic invariant-sector flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Take a compact hyperbolic suspension whose transversal is the Z_hat^*-invariant modulus quotient, and equip distributions on the transversal with an anisotropic Sobolev norm that contracts stable directions and expands unstable directions. Let the flow be the invertible suspension flow, and let the cohomology be the anisotropic Hilbert completion of compactly supported leafwise forms. The anisotropic norm is geometrically defined from stable/unstable cone fields, not from zeta zeros, and is intended to turn the flow generator into a discrete-resonance nonnormal operator.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The invariant modulus replaces Z_p^m, while the stable/unstable anisotropic norm replaces Assumption (iv). Unlike Candidates 49–51, compactness is tied to hyperbolic geometry rather than an equivalent weight or analytic strip. Prime labels are assigned to return components of the suspension, and the finite-adic normal direction is intended to provide p^(-m).

### ORBITS

A connected hyperbolic return system with prime-labelled branches allows concatenated branches, so mixed words produce lengths log 6 and other composite sums. If branches are disconnected to prevent mixed words, the construction becomes a prime-sector direct sum and inherits trace divergence. If a wandering connector is used, the anisotropic flow acquires scattering sectors. The prime-only orbit requirement therefore fails in every branch of this construction.

### MODULAR FACTORS

A finite-adic normal map x -> p x can provide p^(-m) locally, but the hyperbolic stable/unstable norm does not derive this Jacobian. It is an additional transverse factor attached to each branch, not a consequence of the invariant-sector anisotropic geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

Hyperbolic compactification does not produce a stationary point with exponent -2. A boundary stratum may be added, but its exponent is an external boundary condition.

### SPECTRUM AND NORM

Anisotropic spaces can turn the generator into a nonnormal operator with discrete Pollicott-Ruelle resonances. The resonances are not eigenvalues of a normal Hilbert generator, and their completeness depends on the anisotropic construction. The norm is geometrically non-equivalent to Haar, so this avoids the normality-forces-continuous-spectrum argument, but it has no canonical arithmetic spectrum from the invariant modulus alone.

### TRACE CLASS

For ordinary Hilbert traces, anisotropic transfer operators are generally not trace class under compact-time smearing. Known trace formulas on anisotropic spaces are distributional or regularized and count resonances through wavefront-compatible traces. If one imposes enough smoothing to obtain trace class, the smoothing changes the flow operator and the periodic-orbit coefficients. Thus the Gate 1 ordinary trace requirement is not met.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the invariant modulus quotient, a hyperbolic suspension, stable/unstable cone fields, an anisotropic Sobolev norm, prime branch labels, and optional finite-adic normal maps. No zero locations are used.

### P1: partial — hyperbolic transfer data and prime branch lengths are present, but mixed words or disconnected sectors prevent the exact prime trace.
### P2: unknown — no positivity claim is made.
### P3: partial — stable/unstable reversal suggests a reflection, but no s to 1-s operator identity is proved.
### P4: fails — no Xi determinant identity exists.
### P5: fails — resonances are not identified with zeta zeros.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). Anisotropic hyperbolic geometry supplies a genuine nonnormal mechanism and discrete resonances, but its traces are regularized/distributional rather than ordinary trace class, and the prime-only orbit problem remains.

### FAILURE CLASS

Anisotropic-resonance trace obstruction. Hyperbolic anisotropic norms can discretize resonances only by leaving the ordinary Hilbert trace-class category or by introducing branch/smoothing data that change the orbit trace.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 53

The next candidate must retain a genuinely nonnormal but ordinary Hilbert trace-class flow, not merely a distributional resonance trace, and must derive prime-only returns and p^(-m) from one global geometry.
