\n## Candidate 55: Compact arithmetic graph differential

### CONSTRUCTION

Let G be a compact metric graph with one oriented loop of length log p for each prime p, coupled at a single global vertex by non-self-adjoint matching conditions. Let A be the first-order differential operator d/dx on edge interiors with the chosen nonnormal vertex conditions, and let U_t be the two-sided evolution generated by A on the graph Sobolev space. Attach finite-adic normal fibers to edges, with return map x -> p x on the p-edge. The nonnormal vertex conditions are intended to couple all prime edges into one global cohomology without a direct-sum decomposition.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The graph edges replace prime mapping tori and the common vertex replaces the global adelic transversal. Nonnormal vertex matching replaces Assumption (iv), while finite-adic edge fibers provide the proposed p^(-m) Jacobians. This is not boundedly similar to the uncoupled edge operator in general.

### ORBITS

Each edge has a primitive loop of length log p, but a common vertex allows a trajectory to leave the p-edge and enter the q-edge. Mixed closed paths of lengths log p + log q, including log 6, are therefore present unless matching conditions forbid transitions. If transitions are forbidden, the graph decouples into prime edges and returns to the full prime-sector trace obstruction. ORBITS fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The finite-adic edge fibers can produce p^(-m) locally, but the nonnormal vertex matching does not derive those factors. They are edgewise attached data, not a Jacobian of the global graph vertex. MODULAR fails globally.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The graph has no canonical stationary boundary point with exponent -2. Adding a boundary vertex and a chosen normal condition is external.

### SPECTRUM AND NORM

For a finite prime truncation, A has compact resolvent and a discrete nonnormal spectrum. For all primes, the graph has infinitely many edges with lengths log p accumulating in the geometric counting sense; compact resolvent and a single common Sobolev norm are not automatic. Strong matching that couples infinitely many edges must be controlled to define a closed generator. Weak matching leaves prime-sector blocks.

### TRACE CLASS

Finite graph truncations permit trace-class functions of A, but their periodic-orbit traces contain mixed graph words or have coefficients determined by vertex scattering, not the required prime-only log p sum. In the infinite graph, either the trace norm diverges over the prime edges, or coupling is strong enough to require a renormalized/scattering trace. Neither is the Gate 1 ordinary trace. A compact resolvent of each finite truncation does not yield a trace-class infinite-prime limit.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the prime-length metric graph, nonnormal vertex matching, finite-adic edge fibers, and a global Sobolev graph norm. No zeta-zero locations are used.

### P1: partial — prime lengths occur geometrically, but global matching adds mixed words or decouples.

### P3: partial — edge reversal can suggest a reflection, but no s to 1-s operator symmetry is proved.
### P4: fails — no Xi determinant identity exists.
### P5: fails — no zero locations are spectral data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). Nonnormal compact graph operators can have discrete spectra, but global coupling produces mixed prime words; decoupling restores divergence, and finite truncation does not supply an ordinary infinite-prime trace.

### FAILURE CLASS

Compact-graph coupling obstruction. Nonnormal global coupling turns prime loops into mixed graph words; preserving prime-only loops leaves an infinite edge direct sum whose trace diverges.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 56

The next candidate must produce a single global compact-resolvent flow without graph-edge prime sectors or concatenable vertices, while deriving prime periods and p^(-m) from one invariant adelic mechanism.

Each branch has a primitive return of length log p and iterates m log p. If the branch image returns to the common section and all branches can be composed, mixed words produce lengths log p + log q. \n## Consolidation 60: branch-Jacobian/degreewise-smoothing no-go

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers countable prime-branch transfer systems and their degreewise finite-adic heat regularizations, under Gate 1 requirements that the p-adic Jacobian be p^(-m), each degreewise smeared operator be ordinary trace class, and every prime Lefschetz sign remain +1.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

For a branch system whose first-iterate contribution in one ordinary cohomological degree contains the natural finite-adic Jacobian p^(-1) for every prime p, the absolute trace mass contains the divergent sum sum_p p^(-1). A degreewise positive heat or compactness factor c_p can make the sum finite only if c_p is summable against p^(-1), but then the orbit coefficient becomes c_p log p rather than log p. If c_p is trace-neutral so that the exact coefficient remains log p, it does not cure the divergence. Cancellation between degrees is not permitted because Gate 1 requires each A_j(phi) to be trace class and the prime Lefschetz signs are all positive.

Connected branch systems also produce mixed words, while disconnected branch systems reduce to the known prime-sector alternatives. Thus this mechanism cannot simultaneously provide exact positive prime coefficients and ordinary trace class.

### STATUS

PARTIAL NO-GO. The summability conflict is proved for the stated branch and degreewise-factor class. The argument does not cover a nonlocal global operator whose trace coefficient is not the sum of independent prime Jacobian masses, so it is not a universal no-go.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The class is forced by the working model mechanism for p^(-m): an additive p-adic normal Jacobian. Degreewise smoothing is the natural attempt to preserve that mechanism while repairing trace class. The conclusion is not forced for a global adelic cohomology in which prime contributions are coupled before taking the trace.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The finite-adelic replacement for Z_p^m can supply the correct Jacobian, but local branchwise trace class is incompatible with the positive prime coefficient unless a new global coupling changes the trace measure itself. The remaining search space is a genuinely nonlocal adelic cohomology, not a prime-indexed heat or branch sum.

### RESULT

CONSOLIDATION 60 — PARTIAL NO-GO. The local branch and degreewise-heat mechanisms are closed under the stated assumptions. A nonlocal global trace mechanism remains open.

On a compact quotient the Hecke operators may have discrete joint spectral data, but the global correspondence algebra has not been shown to have a generator whose flow spectrum is exactly the prime logarithmic data. Composite Hecke products are unavoidable. No zero data are used or identified.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

A compact quotient does not by itself make Hecke correspondences trace class: the correspondence kernels are generally distributional along graphs, and their trace is a fixed-point distribution rather than an ordinary Hilbert-space trace. Smoothing the kernels makes an operator trace class but changes the exact correspondence coefficients. If the trace is taken in the natural adelic invariant norm, the finite-prime first-order mass again contains sum_p p^(-1) at the boundary. A nonnormal correspondence norm could alter this, but the required trace formula would then need a new trace theorem. The natural invariant correspondence norm remains on the normal branch; flag NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are an adelic quotient, normalized Hecke correspondences, logarithmic prime roofs, and a proposed global correspondence trace. No zeros or zero locations are supplied. The quotient and correspondence geometry are not constructed for Spec Z in a form satisfying the required flow axioms.

### P3: unknown — no operator implementing s to 1-s is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — Hecke correspondence labels are inputs and are not proved to be primitive closed-orbit spectral data of a Deninger flow.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, ARCHIMEDEAN). The global Hecke algebra can encode prime multiplication formally, but its natural trace is a distributional fixed-point trace, not an ordinary trace-class operator trace. Smoothing changes the exact coefficients. Composite correspondences and the missing infinite-place derivation remain unresolved.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A global adelic correspondence trace does not automatically become an ordinary trace-class flow trace: the unsmoothed correspondence kernel is supported on a graph and has distributional fixed-point trace, while every smoothing strong enough to make it trace class changes the exact prime orbit coefficient or leaves the prime harmonic divergence. Thus global nonlocality alone does not bridge correspondence traces to Gate 1 ordinary trace class.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 65

The next candidate must construct an actual foliated flow whose global trace is ordinary trace class without smoothing away the exact prime coefficients. It must derive, rather than append, both the finite-adic Jacobian and the archimedean distribution, and it must make primitive-prime extraction invariant under the flow.

## Candidate 65: Adelic scaling mapping-torus groupoid

### CONSTRUCTION

Let Y be a proposed compact quotient of the finite ideles together with the real logarithmic modulus, and let sigma^t be the global scaling action. Form the mapping-torus groupoid Y semidirect product R generated by sigma^t. Give a primitive return labelled p a roof length log p and assign the p-adic transverse Jacobian p^(-m). Define a global Ruelle-type transfer operator L_s on the groupoid convolution Hilbert space by
\[
(L_s f)(y)=\int K_s(y,z)f(z)\,d\mu(z),
\]
with K_s assembled from the global scaling correspondence rather than independent prime kernels. The candidate trace is the ordinary operator trace of L_s and its iterates. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This attempts to make the arithmetic scaling into an actual flow and to obtain prime terms from closed groupoid trajectories. It avoids a direct restricted tensor product and avoids prescribing a spectral measure. The global quotient is intended to couple finite and infinite places before taking traces.

### ORBITS

The scaling action on the full idelic modulus has continuous logarithmic motion. A rational prime multiplier is a discrete correspondence, but it is not automatically a periodic point of the same one-parameter scaling flow. If the quotient identifies the p-scaling with a return, then products of returns give composite periods log(pq). If only primitive returns are retained, the primitive-return subset is not closed under the groupoid convolution. No bijection between all primitive closed flow orbits and rational primes is proved.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The finite-idele action can carry the local Jacobian p^(-m), and the global product formula couples it to the real modulus. This provides a plausible geometric source for the modular factor. However, the product formula also cancels the total adelic modulus, so retaining exactly the finite p^(-m) contribution requires a boundary or relative transverse measure not defined by the mapping torus.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The real modulus is present, but its invariant Haar measure gives a flat logarithmic coordinate. The kernel (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and the pole exponent -2 do not follow from the mapping-torus construction. Adding an archimedean transfer kernel supplies them as external data.

### SPECTRUM

The groupoid generator on the logarithmic modulus has continuous spectrum under the natural invariant Haar representation. Compactifying the modulus can make the spectrum discrete, but then scaling returns become winding numbers and the prime labels are no longer individual primitive closed orbits. A smoothed transfer operator can have discrete spectrum but introduces a noncanonical smoothing scale.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Under the natural invariant Haar norm on the modulus sector, the generator is normal with continuous nonatomic spectrum and groupoid convolution operators are not trace class without smoothing. Compactification or confining weights changes the flow and its return lengths. An anisotropic norm can create resonances, but then the trace is a distributional resonance trace rather than an ordinary Hilbert trace unless a new trace-class theorem is supplied. Flag NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY for the natural invariant sector.

### INPUTS

The inputs are a proposed compact adelic quotient, global scaling action, groupoid convolution kernel, finite-idele Jacobian, and roof lengths log p. No zeros are used. The required quotient and transverse measure are not constructed.

### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s action is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — prime labels are correspondences or winding data, not proved primitive closed-orbit spectral data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). The mapping-torus construction supplies a genuine global flow candidate and a geometric source for p-adic scaling, but primes are not periodic orbits of the same flow. The natural invariant representation has continuous spectrum and no ordinary trace-class transfer operator, while compactification or smoothing changes the arithmetic return structure.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A global adelic scaling flow cannot simultaneously retain a continuous logarithmic modulus, identify individual prime multipliers as primitive closed orbits, and have an ordinary trace-class transfer operator: continuous modulus gives non-atomic normal spectrum, while compactifying or confining it changes prime returns into composite winding data or introduces noncanonical weights.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 66

The next candidate must retain individual prime periodic orbits while eliminating the continuous modulus trace obstruction through an intrinsic compact transverse geometry. It must derive the archimedean kernel from that same compact geometry and keep the finite-idele Jacobian uncancelled without an externally chosen boundary measure.

## Candidate 66: Profinite compact transverse suspension

### CONSTRUCTION

Let K be the compact profinite group product over primes of Z_p, with normalized Haar measure, and let a prime-labelled return relation R_p translate the p-coordinate by one unit while leaving the other coordinates fixed. Form a suspension over the compact transversal K by assigning the return roof log p to R_p. The finite-place Radon-Nikodym factor is prescribed as p^(-m) on the mth return. Define the global transfer operator from the sum of the R_p correspondence operators, but keep the transversal compact and the Haar norm fixed. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces the continuous idelic modulus by a compact profinite transversal. It is designed to preserve finite-adic structure and provide a genuine compact norm, while avoiding the noncompact logarithmic coordinate and the unrestricted restricted tensor product.

### ORBITS

A translation on a compact profinite group by a nonzero element has no periodic point when the translation has infinite order. The proposed p-coordinate translation has infinite order in Z_p, so its orbit is recurrent but not closed. Replacing translation by a finite cyclic quotient creates periodic points, but their periods are determined by the chosen quotient and cannot equal log p canonically for all primes. Adding a roof with log p does not turn a nonperiodic transverse orbit into a closed flow orbit. Prime orbit bijection therefore fails.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The p-adic Haar measure is invariant under translation, so its Radon-Nikodym derivative is 1, not p^(-m). To obtain p^(-m), one must use multiplication by p or a non-Haar weighted measure. Multiplication by p is not invertible on Z_p and sends the compact space into a proper subset; a weighted quasi-invariant measure requires an external choice and is not the normalized profinite Haar geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The compact profinite transversal contains no infinite-place coordinate. A real suspension roof can insert log p, but it does not derive the kernel (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2. Those remain external.

### SPECTRUM

The Haar translation operators are unitary with pure point characters on each finite quotient but a profinite limiting character spectrum. The infinite-order translation has no prime-periodic orbit spectrum. Multiplication-by-p branches are nonunitary and noninvertible, with spectrum accumulating at zero; no canonical flow generator with the required roof data is obtained.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

On the compact Haar space, individual translations are bounded but not trace class: their kernels are delta distributions and their spectral multiplicities do not decay. Smoothing the translations gives trace-class operators only by adding a kernel whose Fourier coefficients decay; this changes the exact return coefficient and does not create closed prime orbits. The natural invariant Haar norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the compact profinite group, Haar measure, prime-labelled translations or multiplications, roofs log p, and prescribed p^(-m) weights. No zeros are used. The choice of prime-labelled relations and weights is not derived from a single foliated system.

### P1: partial — profinite coordinates encode finite-adic multiplicativity, but the Haar action has no derived p^(-m) Jacobian.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — infinite-order profinite returns are not closed, and finite quotients are arbitrary inputs.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). Compactness removes the continuous modulus but also removes the required prime periodic orbits and finite-adic Jacobian. Haar translations have unit Jacobian and are not trace class; multiplication gives the desired scaling only at the cost of noninvertibility. The archimedean distribution is absent.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Compact profinite Haar geometry cannot simultaneously provide invertible prime returns, nontrivial p^(-m) Jacobians, and primitive closed orbits: Haar translations are invertible with Jacobian 1 and no finite-order prime cycles, while multiplication by p has the desired scaling but is noninvertible and has no suspension flow with primitive prime period.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 67

The next candidate must use a compact transverse geometry with a genuinely quasi-invariant, invertible prime action whose Radon-Nikodym derivative is p^(-m), and must derive primitive prime closed orbits and the archimedean kernel from the same action.

## Candidate 67: Compact quasi-invariant modular suspension

### CONSTRUCTION

Let X be a compact transverse space with a finite positive measure mu, and let R_p:X to X be an invertible nonsingular transformation for each prime. Require the Radon-Nikodym derivative of R_p^m to be the constant p^(-m), so that a suspension over R_p with roof log p has the desired finite-adic modular factor. Couple all R_p inside one global suspension flow and use the finite measure norm on L2(X,mu). No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This directly addresses Candidate 66 by retaining compactness, invertibility, and quasi-invariance instead of using Haar translations or noninvertible multiplication. It makes the modular requirement an explicit axiom of the candidate, allowing a short exact consistency test before any trace construction.

### ORBITS

The transformations are required to be invertible, but the construction does not produce prime-periodic points. Adding periodic points by hand gives a finite cycle structure unrelated to the constant modular derivative. Products of R_p again produce composite return words unless the prime relations are disconnected or projected.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The required constant derivative is impossible on a finite measure space. By the change-of-variables identity,
\[
\mu(X)=\mu(R_p^{-1}X)=\int_X \frac{d\mu\circ R_p^{-1}}{d\mu}\,d\mu.
\]
If the derivative is the constant p^(-1), the right side is p^(-1)mu(X), which contradicts 0<mu(X)<infinity for every p>1. The same contradiction applies to every m>0. Thus compact finite-measure geometry cannot supply the required constant p^(-m) modular factor for an invertible action.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

No infinite-place coordinate or archimedean distribution is derived. Adding a real suspension roof supplies lengths but not the factor (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2.

### SPECTRUM

Since the required transformations cannot exist under the stated finite-measure assumptions, no flow generator or transfer spectrum is defined. If the finite measure is replaced by an infinite measure, the contradiction disappears but the compact trace-class argument and ordinary invariant Hilbert norm are lost.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The finite-measure L2 norm would be the natural invariant norm, but the modular axiom is inconsistent before trace class is considered. Passing to an infinite measure or a weighted non-invariant norm can permit constant cocycles, but the resulting action is outside the compact finite-measure class and returns to the noncompact continuous-spectrum obstruction. Flag NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY for the finite Haar branch.

### INPUTS

The inputs are compactness, finite positive transverse measure, invertible nonsingular prime transformations, constant p^(-m) cocycles, and roofs log p. No zeros are used. The contradiction is purely measure-theoretic.

### P1: fails — the required finite-adic modular bridge is inconsistent with invertibility on a compact finite-measure transverse space.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — no prime closed-orbit system exists once the modular axiom is removed.

### VERDICT

FAIL(MODULAR, ORBITS, ARCHIMEDEAN). The modular requirement itself contradicts finite-measure compact invertible dynamics. Relaxing finite measure or invertibility returns to previously recorded noncompact or noninvertible classes.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

There is a complete measure-theoretic no-go for the stated class: no invertible nonsingular transformation of a finite positive-measure compact space can have constant Radon-Nikodym derivative c not equal to 1. Therefore an exact constant p^(-m) Jacobian cannot coexist with compact finite-measure transverse geometry.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 68

The next candidate must use an infinite transverse measure, a nonconstant modular cocycle, or a relative measure with boundary terms. It must prove that this relaxation still gives ordinary trace-class operators, primitive prime closed orbits, and the archimedean kernel without repeating the continuous-spectrum obstruction.

## Candidate 69: Noncommutative modular crossed product

### CONSTRUCTION

Let K be the compact finite-adelic solenoid and let Q_+ act by rational scaling on its measurable completion. Form the crossed-product von Neumann algebra
\[
\mathcal A=L^\infty(K)\rtimes Q_+,
\]
with modular operator Delta implementing the Radon-Nikodym cocycle of rational scaling. A prime generator p is represented by the group element [p], with modular eigenvalue p^(-1), and the mth power has p^(-m). Add the real logarithmic flow generated by the dual action, assigning roof log p to [p]. The candidate trace is the canonical semifinite trace on the crossed product, restricted to a proposed trace-class ideal. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces ordinary commutative transverse dynamics by a noncommutative measured groupoid. The modular operator can retain p^(-m) while the underlying compact base avoids the finite-measure constant-Jacobian contradiction. The construction is genuinely global because rational scaling is represented inside one crossed product.

### ORBITS

The crossed-product generators [p] are algebraic group elements, not primitive closed orbits of a classical foliated flow. The product [p][q]=[pq] is intrinsic, so composite words are present. A trace of [p] would need a fixed-point or groupoid isotropy interpretation, but rational scaling has no canonical prime-specific closed orbit set on the compact solenoid.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The modular operator records the exact rational scaling cocycle, so p^(-m) appears naturally in the noncommutative representation. This is a formal success. It is a modular eigenvalue of the crossed product, not a transverse Jacobian of a classical invertible finite-measure map.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The dual real flow supplies a logarithmic parameter, but the archimedean distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole exponent -2 do not follow from the crossed-product relations. They would require a separate real-place weight or modular spectral density.

### SPECTRUM

The modular spectrum can contain the discrete multiplicative subgroup generated by the primes, and the dual action has a continuous real parameter. The combined spectrum is therefore mixed discrete-continuous. No theorem identifies a classical flow spectrum with prime periodic orbits, and no target spectral determinant is defined.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The canonical crossed-product trace is generally semifinite, not a finite ordinary Hilbert-space trace. The modular eigenvectors associated with p have infinitely repeated groupoid translates, so the corresponding spectral projections are not finite rank. Restricting to a finite trace ideal or applying heat smoothing can produce trace-class pieces, but the prime trace then depends on the ideal or smoothing and is not the exact universal coefficient. The natural Plancherel norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the compact solenoid, rational scaling action, crossed-product algebra, modular operator, dual logarithmic flow, and formal roofs log p. No zero locations are used. The classical foliation, primitive closed orbits, and archimedean density are not constructed.

### P1: partial — the crossed product gives a genuine multiplicative-to-additive modular representation, but no ordinary Gate 1 trace formula.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — modular eigenvalues are algebraic/groupoid data, not verified prime closed-orbit spectral data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). The noncommutative crossed product naturally carries the p^(-m) modular spectrum, but its canonical trace is semifinite and its prime generators are not classical closed orbits. Any trace-class restriction or smoothing is auxiliary, and the archimedean factor is absent.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Replacing a classical transverse system by a crossed-product modular algebra converts the trace problem into a semifinite multiplicity problem: exact prime modular eigenvalues occur with infinite groupoid multiplicity, so ordinary trace class fails. A finite trace ideal removes the multiplicity only by introducing a noncanonical cutoff that changes the prime trace coefficients.

The next pass is a consolidation. It must state a rigorous cumulative no-go theorem for the nonlocal global classes tested since Candidate 60, or exhibit a genuinely new mechanism not covered by local smoothing, restricted products, affine suspensions, compact profinite actions, or crossed-product modular algebras.

## Consolidation 70: Global nonlocal assembly no-go

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers Candidates 60 through 69 and the following Gate 1 classes: degreewise smoothing of prime branches, restricted tensor products, global relative Euler determinants, spectral-shift measures, adelic Hecke correspondences, adelic mapping tori, compact profinite suspensions, infinite-measure affine suspensions, and modular crossed products. The claim is restricted to the hypotheses stated for those classes. It is not a universal no-go for every possible arithmetic dynamical system.

### CUMULATIVE NO-GO THEOREM

Suppose a proposed Gate 1 construction satisfies all of the following:

1. Its exact first prime contribution is the positive coefficient log p together with the finite-place factor p^(-1), with no damping factor.
2. Its global assembly is obtained either by summing local prime sectors, multiplying independent local factors, taking an ordinary relative determinant, using a finite-variation spectral-shift measure, taking a trace of a smoothed correspondence kernel, or taking a canonical trace on a modular crossed product.
3. Its transverse norm is one of the natural invariant Haar, restricted-product vacuum, finite-measure compact, sigma-finite affine, or Plancherel norms.
4. Its primitive prime labels are required to arise from the same flow rather than being inserted as an external spectral measure.

Then the construction cannot satisfy Gate 1 in full.

### PROOF BY CLASS

For local sectors and restricted products, ordinary trace class requires summability of the first-order local defects. Exact p^(-1) defects force the divergent prime harmonic sum sum_p p^(-1). Damping makes the trace finite only by changing the exact coefficient.

For relative determinants and finite-variation spectral-shift measures, the same divergence appears in the first-order logarithmic determinant or total variation. Analytic continuation or determinant regularization is not an ordinary trace-class determinant under Gate 1.

For correspondence kernels, unsmoothed Hecke or groupoid kernels have distributional fixed-point traces. Smoothing makes them trace class but changes the exact orbit coefficient or introduces an auxiliary cutoff.

For compact profinite or finite-measure transverse actions, Haar translations have unit Jacobian and infinite-order prime translations have no periodic points. An invertible finite-measure transformation cannot have constant Radon-Nikodym derivative p^(-1), because integrating the derivative forces it to equal 1.

For infinite-measure affine suspensions, p^(-1) can occur as a partial p-adic branch Jacobian, but the shared logarithmic coordinate has continuous non-atomic spectrum, the branch is not an invertible flow return, and ordinary trace class fails without smoothing or confinement.

For modular crossed products, the exact modular eigenvalues occur with infinite groupoid multiplicity and the canonical trace is semifinite. Restricting to a finite trace ideal changes the normalization and is not canonical.

### STATUS

PARTIAL NO-GO THEOREM. The theorem closes the listed assembly classes under their stated norms and exact-coefficient assumptions. It does not exclude a new global mechanism whose trace is neither an ordinary local/relative determinant nor a finite-variation spectral shift, and whose prime orbit measure is generated geometrically without independent local defects.

### REMAINING OPEN CLASS

The remaining search space is a genuinely new global object with all of these properties simultaneously:

- a non-additive but ordinary trace invariant;
- no independently trace-summable local deviations;
- no regularization or smoothing that changes log p;
- an actual invertible flow with primitive prime closed orbits;
- a derived finite-adic modular cocycle;
- a discrete trace-class transverse spectrum;
- a derived archimedean factor.

### RESULT

CONSOLIDATION 70 — PARTIAL NO-GO. Candidates 60–69 establish a common trace/orbit/modular obstruction for the listed global assembly mechanisms. The search is not saturated because the remaining class is not covered by the theorem.

## Candidate 71: Integer-spectrum plethystic determinant

### CONSTRUCTION

Let H be l2(N greater than or equal to 2) with diagonal operator A_s e_n=n^(-s)e_n for Re(s)>1. Its ordinary Fredholm determinant exists because A_s is trace class in that half-plane:
\[
D(s)=\det(I-A_s)=\prod_{n\ge2}(1-n^{-s}).
\]
Define the global arithmetic invariant by applying the intrinsic plethystic logarithm and Möbius transform to the integer-indexed determinant:
\[
\mathcal P(s)=\sum_{r\ge1}\frac{\mu(r)}{r}\log D(rs),
\]
whenever the series converges. The intended effect is to remove composite integer indexing and recover an Euler-product logarithm from one global integer spectrum. The object uses no zero data.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This is neither a direct prime-sector sum nor a restricted tensor product. All integers occur in one diagonal spectrum, and prime information is extracted by an algebraic Möbius transform applied after the determinant. It therefore tests whether non-additive global arithmetic cancellation can avoid the local p^(-1) trace obstruction.

### ORBITS

The diagonal integer spectrum has no underlying foliated space, flow, or primitive closed orbit. The labels n are spectral inputs, not return periods. Möbius inversion is an algebraic projection and does not create prime orbits or an invariant primitive-return subset.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The eigenvalues n^(-s) contain prime powers through integer factorization, but no finite-adic transverse Jacobian is present. The p^(-m) coefficients arise only after the Möbius transform of the determinant expansion, not from a geometric modular action.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

No real-place operator or archimedean distribution is present. The pole and factor (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) cannot be derived from the integer diagonal determinant.

### SPECTRUM

The spectrum is discrete and explicitly known in the half-plane Re(s)>1. It is exponentially dense in the logarithmic coordinate because the eigenvalue locations are log n. The plethystic transform changes the scalar invariant, not the spectrum of a single operator. No flow generator or prime spectrum is identified.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For Re(s)>1, A_s is trace class because sum_n n^(-Re(s)) converges. At the boundary where the first prime term is p^(-1), the corresponding integer trace sum also diverges. The Möbius transform can cancel composite terms in the scalar determinant after the trace-class region, but it does not make A_s trace class at the boundary and does not define an ordinary trace-class operator there. Analytic continuation of the transformed scalar is not an ordinary Fredholm determinant. The diagonal norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the integer-indexed diagonal spectrum and Möbius inversion. No zero locations are used. The arithmetic factorization is built into the labels n rather than derived from a flow.

### P1: partial — the global determinant plus Möbius transform can encode the Euler-product algebra in its convergence region, but no geometric trace bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — prime information is extracted algebraically from integer spectral labels, not realized as primitive closed-orbit data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). The integer determinant gives a genuinely global arithmetic encoding, but Möbius cancellation occurs only after taking a scalar determinant and does not repair the boundary trace-class failure. No flow, finite-adic Jacobian, or archimedean factor is produced.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Post-trace Möbius or plethystic cancellation cannot substitute for an operator-level trace-class mechanism: a scalar arithmetic transform may cancel composite terms after the determinant is formed, but the underlying integer operator still has divergent boundary trace and has no prime-orbit geometry. Therefore global algebraic cancellation does not create a Gate 1 operator.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 72

The next candidate must realize arithmetic cancellation before the ordinary trace is taken, while retaining an actual flow with primitive prime orbits and deriving the archimedean term. A scalar Möbius transform or determinant regularization is insufficient.

## Candidate 72: Pre-trace graded prime-cycle blocks

### CONSTRUCTION

For every prime p, take a finite graded block B_p with two or more internal states and a cycle operator whose pth roof contribution is generated by an off-diagonal closed path. Assemble the blocks into one direct-sum Hilbert space, but define the arithmetic trace through the graded block trace before summing over p. Choose the internal signs so that divergent diagonal masses cancel inside each block while the cyclic word contributes +log p times p^(-1). The blocks are finite-dimensional, and no zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This moves cancellation before the global trace, unlike Candidate 71. It also avoids a post-trace Möbius transform and attempts to produce positive prime coefficients from finite internal cycles rather than from independent scalar eigenvalues.

### ORBITS

Each block has a formal p-cycle, but the direct-sum assembly gives one disconnected prime sector per p. If the blocks are coupled into one flow, mixed composite cycles appear. If they remain disconnected, the construction is exactly a prime-sector sum with no global adelic geometry.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The p^(-1) factor can be attached to the cyclic block weight, but it is an internal scalar normalization rather than a derived transverse Jacobian. A genuine modular Jacobian would require an underlying p-adic return map, which the finite block does not provide.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

No infinite-place block or archimedean kernel is derived. Adding one more graded block supplies a chosen factor but does not explain (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2.

### SPECTRUM

Each finite block has a discrete spectrum and finite rank. The infinite direct sum has repeated prime-sector spectra. Coupling blocks creates composite cycle spectra and destroys the independent finite-block decomposition. No common flow generator or canonical global spectral object is identified.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Internal graded cancellation can make the algebraic supertrace of one block finite, but ordinary trace class is a norm condition on the full operator, not merely cancellation of diagonal traces. The trace norm of a block carrying a nonzero p^(-1) cycle contribution is bounded below by a constant multiple of p^(-1). Therefore the direct sum has trace norm at least a constant multiple of sum_p p^(-1), which diverges. Coupling blocks does not reduce this lower bound without changing the cycle coefficients. A graded supertrace would be a different invariant from the required ordinary trace. The block norm is normal on each finite component and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

The inputs are finite graded prime blocks, internal cycle matrices, roof lengths log p, and assigned p^(-1) weights. No zeros are used. The prime labels and modular weights are not derived from a single global foliation.

For a direct sum of finite prime-cycle blocks, any nonzero positive ordinary trace contribution of size at least c p^(-1) forces the global trace norm to dominate c sum_p p^(-1), even if the algebraic graded trace cancels internally. ## Candidate 73: Long-cycle nonnormal transfer operator

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p choose a finite cyclic block of length L_p greater than or equal to 2, with a weighted cyclic shift C_p whose edge weights are all p^(-1/L_p). Then
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(C_p^{L_p})=p^{-1},
\]
so the prime modular weight appears only in a power of the operator, not as a diagonal entry. Assign the block a roof length log p per full cycle and assemble the blocks into one global transfer operator C by direct sum, with an optional off-diagonal coupling between blocks. The operator is intentionally nonnormal. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This attacks the trace-norm obstruction at the operator level. The exact p^(-1) factor is a product around a cycle, so it is not placed directly on a prime diagonal and is not canceled by a post-trace scalar transform.

### ORBITS

Each block has a formal primitive cyclic orbit associated with p. A direct sum gives disconnected prime sectors. Coupling blocks creates mixed cycles whose periods are sums of prime roofs and therefore includes composite words. The construction has no single connected foliated space from which the blocks arise.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The product of edge weights around the p-cycle is exactly p^(-1), so the modular factor is algebraically present. It is not derived from a p-adic transverse Jacobian; it is assigned to the cycle edges.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

No infinite-place action or archimedean distribution is derived. An additional continuous block or weight would be external.

### SPECTRUM

Each cyclic block has eigenvalues p^(-1/L_p) times the L_p-th roots of unity. The global spectrum is discrete blockwise but has no canonical compact-resolvent ordering when the blocks are assembled. Off-diagonal coupling destroys the independent cycle spectrum and produces mixed eigenvalues.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For each block, the trace norm of the weighted cyclic shift is
\[
\|C_p\|_1=L_p p^{-1/L_p}.
\]
Since L_p is at least 2, this is at least 2p^(-1/2), and the sum over primes diverges. Thus the direct sum C is not trace class. Making the edge weights more unequal does not avoid the obstruction: the product of the L_p edge weights is p^(-1), while the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives a lower bound on the sum of their absolute values, and hence on the block trace norm, of order L_p p^(-1/L_p). Coupling blocks cannot reduce the trace norm lower bound for the orthogonal prime-cycle subspaces without changing the cycle products. The block is nonnormal, so NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY does not apply, but ordinary trace class still fails.

### INPUTS

The inputs are finite cyclic prime blocks, nonnormal weighted shifts, cycle products p^(-1), and roofs log p. No zeros are used. The cyclic geometry and weights are assigned rather than derived from an adelic foliation.

### P1: partial — the cycle product produces p^(-1) before taking the trace, but no global arithmetic-to-additive geometric bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — prime cycles are explicitly represented, but as disconnected finite blocks rather than primitive orbits of one constructed flow.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Moving p^(-1) into long nonnormal cycles does not make the global operator trace class: every prime block has trace norm at least 2p^(-1/2), whose sum diverges. Coupling creates mixed cycles, while the modular and archimedean structures remain assigned.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

For a finite cyclic block whose ordinary power trace carries a positive cycle product p^(-1), the trace norm of the underlying weighted shift is bounded below by L_p p^(-1/L_p), hence at least a constant multiple of p^(-1/2) for L_p at least 2. Therefore hiding the arithmetic weight in nonnormal cycle products makes ordinary trace class strictly worse than diagonal placement.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 74

The next candidate must produce prime contributions through powers of a trace-class operator without assigning one separate finite block per prime. It must avoid the cycle trace-norm lower bound, generate a connected flow, and derive rather than prescribe modular and archimedean factors.

## Candidate 74: Shared-hub prime-cycle graph

### CONSTRUCTION

Let Gamma be one connected countable directed graph with a common hub h and, for each prime p, a return path from h through vertices v_{p,1},...,v_{p,L_p-1} back to h. Put weighted edges on the paths so that the product around the p-cycle is p^(-1), and let T be the weighted adjacency operator on l2 of the vertices. The paths share h, so this is not a direct sum of prime blocks. Assign the total roof of the p-path to log p. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This tests whether a single connected combinatorial object can avoid both the direct-sum trace-norm divergence and the disconnected-sector failure. Shared hub coupling is explicit, and prime cycles are intended to be primitive returns in one graph.

### ORBITS

The graph contains the intended prime cycles, but sharing the hub creates concatenated closed walks: a p-path followed by a q-path is a closed word with length log p + log q. These are composite mixed returns and contribute to traces of powers unless an invariant primitive-cycle subtraction is introduced. Such a subtraction is not generated by the graph dynamics.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The p^(-1) factors are products of assigned edge weights, not Radon-Nikodym derivatives of an adelic transverse action. A common hub does not supply the finite-adic modular geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

No infinite-place coordinate or kernel is present. The graph roof lengths are discrete labels and do not derive (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole term.

### SPECTRUM

The shared hub makes T a nonnormal weighted adjacency operator. If the edge weights are chosen small enough for T to be bounded, the spectrum is governed by the hub return equation and mixes all prime paths; it is not the independent prime list. If the weights are chosen to suppress mixed words, the hub effectively decouples and the construction returns to Candidate 73.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For a trace-class weighted adjacency operator, the sum of absolute singular values of all hub-to-path and path-to-hub edges must be finite. Every prime cycle has product p^(-1). By the product-versus-sum inequality along a path, at least one of its edge magnitudes is at least p^(-1/L_p), and the path contributes a nonzero amount to the trace norm. If the paths are disjoint away from h, these contributions add and the trace norm diverges for the same reason as Candidate 73. Sharing only h does not change the orthogonal path components. If substantial path overlap is introduced to avoid addition, distinct primes share return words, so their traces are no longer separately identifiable and the primitive prime coefficients are altered. NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY does not apply because T is deliberately nonnormal.

### INPUTS

The inputs are one connected graph, a shared hub, prime-labelled paths, assigned cycle products p^(-1), and roofs log p. No zeros are used. The graph and weights are not derived from a global adelic foliation.

### P1: partial — one connected graph gives an additive path model for selected prime words, but no exact arithmetic-to-additive bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — prime cycles are represented in one connected graph, but mixed concatenations destroy primitive-prime trace separation.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). A shared hub creates one connected graph but inevitably creates mixed prime words. Keeping paths distinct reproduces the divergent trace-norm lower bound; overlapping them changes the prime coefficients. The modular and archimedean structures remain assigned.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Connectivity by a common return hub has a sharp dichotomy: if prime paths remain distinguishable, their trace-norm costs add and inherit the p^(-1/L_p) lower bound; if paths overlap enough to avoid that cost, mixed words or shared cycles make the individual prime trace coefficients non-identifiable. Thus hub coupling cannot simultaneously provide connectedness, exact primitive-prime traces, and ordinary trace class in this graph class.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 75

The next candidate must couple prime cycles without concatenable shared return states, or prove an intrinsic trace functional that removes mixed words while remaining ordinary trace class. It must also derive modular and archimedean data rather than assign edge weights and roof labels.

## Candidate 75: Nonbacktracking primitive-cycle determinant

### CONSTRUCTION

Let E be a directed edge set with a single global nonbacktracking transition operator B on l2(E). Build prime-labelled closed edge paths of total roof log p, and define the weighted transition so that the product around the primitive p-path is p^(-1). Use the Ihara-type identity
\[
-\log\det(I-B_s)=\sum_{r\ge1}\frac{1}{r}\operatorname{Tr}(B_s^r),
\]
with the nonbacktracking rule intended to remove immediate reversals. Primitive cycles are then extracted intrinsically by the Euler product for the graph zeta function, not by a post-trace Möbius transform. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This directly targets Candidate 74: it allows one connected transition system but uses nonbacktracking dynamics to control unwanted concatenations. It is a genuine operator construction rather than a scalar spectral ansatz.

### ORBITS

A connected graph with a common return state still has concatenated nonbacktracking cycles whenever the terminal edge of one prime path can be followed by the initial edge of another. Preventing those transitions requires a memory state or forbidden-transition rule that separates prime paths. The separated transition components then reproduce disconnected prime sectors. Thus nonbacktracking removes immediate reversals but not arbitrary prime concatenations.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The cycle weights can be chosen so that each primitive p-cycle has product p^(-1), but the weights are assigned to edges. No finite-adic transverse action or Radon-Nikodym derivation is supplied.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The graph roof lengths give discrete logarithmic periods only. They do not derive the archimedean distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1), the pole exponent -2, or a real-place flow measure.

### SPECTRUM

For a finite graph, B is finite-dimensional and its primitive-cycle determinant is well defined. For infinitely many prime paths, either the edge transition operator has infinitely many distinguishable branches or the prime paths share memory states. The first case creates a divergent trace norm at the exact p^(-1) weights; the second case creates mixed cycles and loses prime separation.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The ordinary Fredholm determinant requires B_s to be trace class or an appropriate nuclear transfer operator. For distinguishable prime paths, the cycle-product lower bound from Candidate 73 applies to the singular values of the path blocks, and the trace norm dominates a divergent prime sum. A nonbacktracking restriction changes the set of words but not the norm cost of each retained primitive cycle. If the operator is defined only through a graph zeta continuation after the trace-class domain, that is a regularized determinant rather than an ordinary trace-class determinant at the Gate 1 boundary. The natural edge-space norm is normal only in the decoupled branch; a nonnormal memory implementation avoids that label but not the trace-norm bound.

### INPUTS

The inputs are a global directed graph, nonbacktracking transition rule, prime-labelled paths, edge weights with products p^(-1), and roofs log p. No zeros are used. The graph and modular weights are not derived from an adelic foliation.

### P1: partial — graph zeta algebra gives an intrinsic primitive-cycle expansion in its nuclear domain, but no exact arithmetic-to-additive geometric bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — primitive cycle extraction is intrinsic for the graph zeta, but the prime cycles are still inserted graph paths and not derived from Spec Z.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Nonbacktracking removes immediate reversals but not concatenation between distinct prime paths. Separating those paths restores the trace-norm divergence, while coupling them creates composite words. The determinant is ordinary only in a convergence domain and becomes regularized at the arithmetic boundary.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Nonbacktracking dynamics is insufficient for prime isolation: any connected transition system that permits successive distinct prime returns contains composite closed words, while forbidding those transitions decomposes the system into prime sectors. The primitive-cycle determinant does not remove this connectedness dichotomy or the trace-norm cost of the retained prime cycles.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 76

The next candidate must isolate prime primitive returns without disconnected sectors, using a mechanism stronger than local nonbacktracking memory. It must remain an ordinary trace-class operator at the exact arithmetic boundary and derive the modular and archimedean factors geometrically.

## Candidate 76: Reset-gated prime renewal flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let a directed renewal graph contain one reset state r and, for each prime p, a finite cyclic path P_p with roof log p and edge-product p^(-1). After completing P_p, the transition returns to r only through a gate that sends the trajectory into a nonrecurrent transient state; no transition from r is allowed directly into a different prime path during the same recurrent return. Define the transfer operator on the graph path space with the reset gate built into the transition rule. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This is a stronger anti-concatenation mechanism than nonbacktracking: the reset gate explicitly prevents a p-return followed by a q-return from becoming one closed word. The graph is topologically connected through the reset and transient states, but the recurrent prime paths are separated dynamically.

### ORBITS

The construction has one primitive recurrent cycle per prime and no mixed p-q recurrent word by design. However, the recurrent part of the flow is a disjoint union of prime components; the reset and transient corridors are not recurrent and do not connect the periodic dynamics. Thus “connectedness” is only topological, not dynamical, and the prime-orbit bijection is obtained by explicitly imposing the gate.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The p^(-1) factors remain assigned as products of path weights. The reset gate has no derived finite-adic Jacobian, and the transient corridor provides no adelic transverse measure. The modular structure is not generated by a global arithmetic action.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The renewal roof gives discrete log p periods but no infinite-place distribution. The kernel (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole term are absent.

### SPECTRUM

The recurrent spectrum is the union of the prime cycle spectra. The reset corridor contributes transient or nilpotent spectrum. A single global operator therefore decomposes into a prime-sector recurrent part plus a transient coupling, and no canonical global spectral object beyond the imposed renewal rule is obtained.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Because the gate prevents recurrent concatenation, the trace contributions reduce to one block per prime. The trace norm lower bound for each p-cycle from Candidate 73 remains, so the ordinary trace norm diverges. Making the cycle weights trace summable changes p^(-1); making the reset coupling nonzero does not cancel singular values of the recurrent blocks. The operator can be nonnormal, but nonnormality does not remove the trace-norm lower bound.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime paths, roof lengths log p, assigned cycle products p^(-1), a reset gate, and transient corridors. No zeros are used. The gate is an explicit primitive-orbit projection encoded in the transition graph, not a derived arithmetic mechanism.

### P1: partial — the renewal rule separates formal prime returns, but the arithmetic-to-additive bridge is imposed by the gate and weights.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — prime cycles are explicit and mixed words are prevented, but only by a nonrecurrent reset projection rather than one natural connected flow.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). The reset gate removes mixed words only by dynamically decomposing the recurrent system into prime sectors. The trace norm still diverges from the cycle products, and the modular and archimedean structures are assigned.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A reset gate can prevent composite prime words only by making the recurrent periodic set dynamically disconnected from itself. Topological connectedness through transient states does not yield a connected arithmetic flow; the gate is an explicit primitive-cycle projection, and it leaves the trace-norm and modular obstructions unchanged.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 77

The next candidate must obtain anti-concatenation from an intrinsic invariant of one recurrent flow, not from a reset, absorbing state, forbidden transition, or explicit primitive projection. It must also lower the ordinary trace norm without changing positive p^(-1) cycle weights.

## Candidate 77: Character-filtered global prime flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let Y be a connected global return system containing a prime-labelled return operator U_p for every p, with roof log p and formal modular weight p^(-1). Enlarge the state space by the compact character torus T^P, one phase theta_p for each prime, and twist the p-return by e^(i theta_p). Define the global trace by Haar integration over the character torus:
\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{char}}(U)=\int_{T^P}\operatorname{Tr}(U(\theta))\,d\theta.
\]
Fourier orthogonality is intended to cancel mixed words while retaining selected primitive prime terms. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces reset gates and forbidden transitions by an intrinsic harmonic filter. The global system remains connected before taking the character trace, and cancellation is supposed to occur through an invariant Haar average rather than an explicit prime-sector projection.

### ORBITS

A word containing distinct prime returns carries the product of their phases. Haar integration kills nontrivial phase characters, but it also kills each individual prime word if the p-phase appears with exponent one. To retain the prime term one must insert a compensating character or differentiate in theta_p. A compensating character selects a prime sector; differentiating produces an unbounded distributional functional. No canonical primitive-orbit trace survives as an ordinary Haar trace.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The phase torus does not supply p^(-1) Jacobians. Those weights remain assigned to the return operators. The character average only changes signs or annihilates words and provides no finite-adic transverse scaling.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The character torus is purely finite-prime harmonic data. It supplies no real-place coordinate and does not derive (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2.

### SPECTRUM

The enlarged operator is a direct integral over character parameters. Its spectrum contains the spectra of all phase twists, and Haar integration is a trace functional rather than a single discrete spectral operator. Differentiation or character insertion can isolate a prime coefficient but is not a bounded trace on the Hilbert space.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

If U is trace class uniformly in theta, Haar integration preserves trace class but kills every word whose phase character is nontrivial, including the desired single-prime words. If the trace is modified by a character insertion to retain p, the insertion is not the positive Haar trace and cannot retain all primes simultaneously as one ordinary trace. Distributional phase differentiation is unbounded. The natural torus representation is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY; the nonnormal alternative does not cure the unbounded selector.

### INPUTS

The inputs are a connected prime-return system, a compact prime character torus, phase twists, Haar integration, assigned roof lengths log p, and assigned p^(-1) weights. No zeros are used. The selector needed to recover prime terms is not derived from the flow.

### P1: partial — Fourier orthogonality provides a global algebraic filter, but it cannot retain all primitive prime words under one ordinary Haar trace.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — Haar filtering removes the desired prime words or requires an external unbounded/sector selector.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Character averaging can remove mixed words only by also removing single-prime words. Recovering the prime terms requires an inserted character or distributional derivative, which is not the required ordinary trace. Modular and archimedean structures remain external.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A positive Haar character trace cannot simultaneously annihilate all mixed prime words and retain every single-prime word: the single-prime words are themselves nontrivial Fourier characters. Any selector that restores them is a nonpositive or unbounded functional, or an explicit prime-sector projection.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 78

The next candidate must separate mixed words by an intrinsic dynamical invariant that preserves all single-prime words under one bounded ordinary trace, not by Haar averaging, character insertion, differentiation, or sector projection. It must also derive modular and archimedean factors.

## Candidate 78: Prime-length Anosov geodesic flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let M be a compact negatively curved surface or a compact contact Anosov flow with geodesic generator G. Require its primitive closed geodesics to include one orbit gamma_p of length log p for every rational prime p, with no other primitive nonstationary closed orbits contributing to the arithmetic trace. Define a Ruelle transfer operator L_s on an anisotropic Banach or Hilbert space so that its dynamical determinant has the primitive-orbit expansion
\[
\det(I-L_s)^{-1}
 =\prod_{p}(1-p^{-s})^{-1}.
\]
Use the geodesic flow and its stable/unstable Jacobians as the proposed transverse structure. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This is the first candidate in the current run where primitive cycles are intrinsic to one connected flow rather than inserted as graph blocks, character sectors, or return gates. Anosov trace formulas naturally distinguish primitive orbits and do not require concatenable paths to be interpreted as new primitive orbits.

### ORBITS

Primitive geodesic flow handles the mixed-word issue: concatenating two closed geodesics is not generally a primitive geodesic. However, a compact Anosov flow has a much larger primitive length spectrum, with exponentially many primitive orbits. Requiring the contributing spectrum to be exactly the prime lengths log p is an additional spectral selection not supplied by the flow. No compact flow with this exact length spectrum and no extra trace contributions is constructed.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The stable and unstable Jacobians of an Anosov flow provide genuine transverse multiplicative factors, but there is no theorem identifying the Jacobian of gamma_p with p^(-1) for all prime-labelled orbits. Assigning that weight is a new normalization, not a consequence of the geodesic geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The smooth geodesic flow has an intrinsic real-time measure and a contact volume, but its Ruelle/Selberg trace formula does not automatically produce the specific distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or pole exponent -2. Those would require a separately identified representation or transfer kernel.

### SPECTRUM

For an Anosov flow, anisotropic transfer operators can have discrete Pollicott-Ruelle resonances and dynamical determinants. This supplies a plausible trace-class-like spectral framework. The resonances are determined by the full closed-orbit geometry, not just the prime subset, and no canonical arithmetic spectrum is identified.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Anisotropic transfer operators are often nuclear only after choosing anisotropic spaces and a smoothing/regularization framework; they are not ordinary trace-class Hilbert operators on the natural L2 space. If the candidate is restricted to a Hilbert trace-class operator, the smoothing changes the orbit weights or removes the exact geodesic trace. If it uses the standard anisotropic nuclear trace, it leaves the stated ordinary trace-class Gate 1 class. The natural contact/L2 norm is normal on the unitary flow branch and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are a compact Anosov flow, a prescribed prime-length subset of its primitive geodesics, stable/unstable Jacobians, and an anisotropic transfer operator. No zeros are used. The exact prime-length realization is not known.

### P1: partial — the dynamical zeta formalism gives a genuine orbit-to-trace bridge, but no arithmetic identification with Euler factors is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — no flow is constructed whose complete contributing primitive orbit set is exactly indexed by rational primes with lengths log p.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). Anosov dynamics solves the primitive-versus-composite word problem conceptually, but its primitive orbit spectrum is far richer than the primes and no exact prime-length realization is known. The p^(-1) weights and archimedean kernel are not derived, and anisotropic nuclear traces are not ordinary Hilbert trace-class traces.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A connected hyperbolic flow can intrinsically separate primitive orbits from their iterates, but its primitive length spectrum cannot simply be restricted to the prime set without an additional non-invariant spectral filter. Thus replacing combinatorial prime cycles by geodesic primitive cycles removes concatenation ambiguity but introduces a full-orbit-spectrum obstruction.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 79

The next candidate must explain why a global flow has exactly the prime-length primitive orbit contribution, not merely a selected prime subset. It must identify stable/unstable Jacobians with p^(-m), derive the archimedean factor, and provide an ordinary trace-class realization rather than an anisotropic regularized trace.

## Candidate 79: Bruhat-Tits arithmetic geodesic quotient

### CONSTRUCTION

For each prime p use the Bruhat-Tits tree T_p of PGL_2(Q_p), with its natural translation length and modular action. Form a proposed global quotient of the restricted product of the T_p by a rational arithmetic group, and let the diagonal Hecke flow act on the quotient. A translation of local length one at p is assigned global roof log p, and the quotient trace is intended to count primitive arithmetic geodesics. The local tree index supplies a candidate p^(-m) transverse factor. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces artificial finite graph weights by genuine local arithmetic geometry. It also has intrinsic geodesic primitive cycles and Hecke correspondences, while the global quotient is intended to couple all primes.

### ORBITS

Closed geodesics in an arithmetic tree quotient correspond to conjugacy classes of hyperbolic elements or closed paths, not solely to rational primes. Products and powers produce composite arithmetic classes, and many distinct classes can have the same or related translation lengths. Selecting the classes with local support at exactly one prime is an external Hecke-sector restriction, not an invariant complete orbit set of the global quotient.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local tree action has genuine index and modular data, but the global rational quotient satisfies a product formula coupling all places. The finite p^(-m) factor is canceled or balanced by other local contributions unless a relative boundary measure is chosen. That boundary choice is not canonical in the proposed quotient.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The restricted product contains no canonical real flow coordinate with the required density (1-e^(-2t))^(-1). An archimedean Bruhat-Tits or symmetric-space factor can be appended, but its contribution depends on a separate representation and does not follow from the finite tree quotient alone.

### SPECTRUM

The tree adjacency and Hecke operators have continuous spectrum on the universal trees and discrete or mixed spectrum on arithmetic quotients. The quotient spectrum is indexed by automorphic data, not simply by the prime translation lengths. No trace-class generator with exactly the desired prime orbit determinant is identified.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Tree adjacency and Hecke correspondences are not ordinary trace-class operators on the natural L2 spaces; their traces are obtained through distributional or von Neumann trace formulas. Finite quotient truncations are trace class but their orbit spectra depend on the quotient and do not stabilize to a single prime-only flow. Smoothing changes the Hecke coefficients. The natural invariant Hilbert norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are Bruhat-Tits trees, an arithmetic quotient group, local Hecke translations, a proposed global diagonal flow, and roofs log p. No zeros are used. The exact global quotient and transverse measure are not constructed.

### P1: partial — local arithmetic geometry supplies multiplicative Hecke data and translation lengths, but no proved global ordinary trace bridge.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — the quotient has many arithmetic closed geodesics beyond one primitive orbit per prime, and prime-only selection is external.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Bruhat-Tits geometry supplies genuine local arithmetic structure, but the global quotient has a larger conjugacy-class length spectrum, distributional Hecke traces, and product-formula cancellation of local modular factors. The archimedean factor remains un-derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A global arithmetic quotient can make local prime translations geometric, but its closed-orbit spectrum is indexed by global conjugacy classes rather than individual primes. Isolating single-prime classes is a non-invariant local-support projection, while retaining all classes introduces composite and archimedean data not matching Gate 1.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 80

The next pass is a consolidation. It must compare the geodesic/Hecke classes from Candidates 78–79 with the earlier trace/orbit no-go theorem and state whether they add a genuinely new obstruction or fall within existing classes.

## Consolidation 80: Geometric orbit-spectrum no-go

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers Candidates 78 and 79: connected Anosov/geodesic flows and arithmetic Bruhat-Tits or adelic tree quotients. It compares them with the earlier graph, groupoid, correspondence, and trace-class obstructions. The conclusion is restricted to the stated geometric classes and does not exclude every possible global arithmetic dynamical system.

### CUMULATIVE RESULT

Geometric primitive-orbit systems solve one part of the earlier problem: primitive closed orbits are intrinsically distinguished from their iterates, so a formal dynamical zeta function need not confuse a prime orbit with its repetitions. However, neither a general connected Anosov flow nor an arithmetic tree quotient has a primitive orbit spectrum consisting exactly of rational primes with lengths log p.

For a connected Anosov flow, the full primitive length spectrum is generated by the complete recurrent geometry and has many additional primitive orbits. Selecting only the lengths log p is a non-invariant spectral filter. For an arithmetic tree quotient, closed orbits are indexed by global conjugacy classes or arithmetic paths, and single-prime local support is likewise a non-invariant selection.

The geometric classes also do not automatically provide the Gate 1 modular and archimedean data. Stable and unstable Jacobians or local tree indices are not identified with the exact p^(-m) factor in one common transverse measure, and neither class derives the distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) with pole exponent -2.

Finally, the natural traces are not ordinary trace-class Hilbert traces: Anosov constructions use anisotropic nuclear or resonance traces, while tree and Hecke constructions use distributional, finite-quotient, or von Neumann traces. Imposing Hilbert trace class by smoothing or truncating changes the orbit weights or quotient spectrum.

### STATUS

PARTIAL NO-GO. Candidates 78 and 79 add a proved structural distinction between primitive-orbit separation and exact prime-spectrum realization. They strengthen the existing orbit-selection obstruction but do not produce a universal no-go theorem for all possible geometric models.

### REMAINING OPEN CLASS

A remaining candidate would need a global geometry whose complete primitive orbit spectrum is exactly prime-indexed, whose local transverse cocycle is exactly p^(-m), whose infinite-place trace density is derived, and whose trace is ordinary Hilbert trace class without a non-invariant prime filter or smoothing.

### RESULT

CONSOLIDATION 80 — PARTIAL NO-GO. Intrinsic primitive-orbit dynamics is not enough: the complete orbit spectrum, modular cocycle, archimedean term, and ordinary trace class must arise from the same geometry. The geometric classes tested do not satisfy that conjunction.

## Candidate 85: Von Mangoldt Jacobi moment operator

### CONSTRUCTION

Seek a single Jacobi operator J on l2(N) whose cyclic spectral measure nu at a distinguished vector e_0 has arithmetic moments
\[
\langle e_0,J^m e_0\rangle=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-s_m}
\]
for a prescribed additive sampling sequence s_m, or whose Laplace transform is the von Mangoldt Dirichlet series. The Jacobi coefficients are to be generated from the moment sequence by the Stieltjes procedure, so primes are not explicit operator sectors. The flow coordinate is the logarithm of the spectral variable. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces explicit prime channels and determinant poles by one global spectral measure and one cyclic operator. If successful, arithmetic prime data would emerge from moments of a single operator rather than being inserted as eigenvalue labels.

### ORBITS

A Jacobi operator has no canonical foliated flow or periodic orbit interpretation. Its moments are closed-walk counts on a half-line graph, and the graph has composite walks unrelated to primitive prime orbits. No geometric orbit bijection is obtained.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The moment sequence encodes Lambda coefficients analytically, but no p-adic transverse action or Radon-Nikodym derivative produces p^(-m). Modular factors would be recovered only after transforming the moments, not geometrically.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The Jacobi spectral measure has no infinite-place distribution. A Laplace transform of the measure does not derive (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2.

### SPECTRUM

If the moment functional is positive and determinate, the Jacobi matrix has a self-adjoint spectrum. But the required arithmetic moments are not given as an ordinary finite spectral measure at the Gate 1 boundary. The moment problem either has infinite mass, requires signed moments, or needs damping that changes Lambda.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

A Jacobi operator carrying an undamped von Mangoldt Laplace transform cannot be trace class: the total prime-power mass at the boundary diverges. If one makes the moments finite by exponential damping, the resulting operator represents a shifted half-plane rather than the exact boundary trace. If one uses signed or distributional moment functionals, it is no longer an ordinary positive spectral measure or ordinary Hilbert trace. The Jacobi matrix norm is self-adjoint/normal on the positive branch and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the von Mangoldt moment sequence, the Stieltjes/Jacobi reconstruction, and a logarithmic spectral coordinate. No zeros are used. The arithmetic sequence is input rather than derived from a flow.

### P1: partial — a moment transform can encode the prime-power Dirichlet series globally, but no geometric multiplicative-to-additive bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — spectral moments are not primitive closed-orbit data and the prime-power sequence is supplied as input.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE). A single Jacobi operator can package arithmetic moments only after choosing a moment functional and convergence region. The undamped boundary functional is not an ordinary trace-class spectral measure, and no flow or derived local/global geometry is obtained.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Replacing prime eigenvalue labels by a global moment problem does not remove arithmetic input: the von Mangoldt sequence must be supplied as the moment functional, while trace-class and finite-measure realization require damping or distributional continuation. A moment transform therefore repackages rather than geometrically derives the prime data.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 86

The next candidate must generate the von Mangoldt moments from a geometric flow or local action, not prescribe them as a moment sequence. It must retain ordinary trace class at the boundary and derive modular and archimedean contributions.
