## Candidate 86: Countable hyperbolic prime-orbit flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Construct a smooth flow on a countable union of compact local flow boxes, with one isolated hyperbolic periodic orbit gamma_p for each rational prime p, primitive period log p, and stable/unstable return multipliers chosen so that the transverse Jacobian contribution is p^(-1). Connect the boxes by heteroclinic corridors without creating additional periodic orbits. Define a global transfer operator from the derivative cocycle on the transverse sections. The construction uses no zero locations.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This gives prime cycles directly as genuine periodic orbits and attempts to derive p^(-1) from hyperbolic stability rather than assigning graph edge weights. Heteroclinic corridors are intended to provide global connectedness without new closed words.

### ORBITS

The local flow boxes provide one prime orbit each and the heteroclinic corridors can be chosen acyclic, so no obvious composite periodic words are created. However, a countable family of isolated periodic orbits in a compact smooth phase space must have accumulation, and the limiting invariant set generally contributes additional recurrent orbits or loses uniform hyperbolicity. On a noncompact disjoint union the prime orbit bijection is possible but the system is not a single compact arithmetic space.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Stable/unstable derivative cocycles can produce a genuine geometric multiplier, but requiring exactly p^(-1) for every prime is an assignment of local linearization data. No adelic transverse action or product formula derives those multipliers.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The smooth flow has a real-time parameter and local transverse derivatives, but no mechanism derives the distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or pole exponent -2. Heteroclinic geometry supplies no canonical infinite-place term.

### SPECTRUM

Each local hyperbolic orbit contributes resonances determined by its return derivative. A countable accumulation of periods and multipliers produces essential or accumulation spectrum unless uniform estimates and a compact global phase space are proved. On the noncompact union the spectrum is a direct sum and loses global coupling.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The exact positive first-order orbit contribution has mass comparable to sum_p p^(-1), which diverges. Stable multipliers stronger than p^(-1) can produce trace class but change the required modular factor. On a compact accumulation space, uniform hyperbolicity fails at the accumulation set, so standard nuclear transfer estimates are unavailable. On a noncompact union, local trace-class operators form a direct sum and inherit the divergent trace norm. The natural local L2 norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are local hyperbolic flow boxes, periods log p, assigned stable multipliers p^(-1), and heteroclinic corridors. No zeros are used. The countable geometry and multipliers are not derived from a global adelic space.

### P1: partial — genuine periodic orbits are present, but their periods and multipliers are prescribed rather than derived arithmetically.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — one prime orbit per p can be modeled locally, but compact accumulation or noncompact disjointness prevents a verified global prime-orbit system.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Countable hyperbolic local models can realize prime periods and multipliers individually, but a compact global flow develops accumulation/recurrent-spectrum problems, while a noncompact union reproduces the direct-sum trace divergence. The arithmetic and archimedean mechanisms remain prescribed.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A countable collection of isolated hyperbolic prime orbits cannot be made simultaneously compact, uniformly hyperbolic, globally connected, and ordinary trace class when the orbit weights are p^(-1): compactness forces accumulation and loss of uniform control, while noncompact disjointness restores divergent trace mass.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 87

The next candidate must derive the countable prime orbit family from a single compact or finite-volume arithmetic geometry with uniform hyperbolicity or an alternative trace-class mechanism, rather than inserting local flow boxes and multipliers.

## Candidate 87: Finite-volume cuspidal arithmetic flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let M be a finite-volume noncompact arithmetic locally symmetric space with cusps, and let F be its geodesic or diagonal flow. Use cusp height as the transverse logarithmic coordinate and assign a prime Hecke excursion p a return length log p. The cusp Jacobian is intended to supply p^(-m), while the finite-volume trace formula is intended to produce an ordinary trace after subtracting the continuous cusp spectrum. Define the transfer operator on the cuspidal Hilbert space and use the cusp scattering operator for the boundary contribution. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This combines genuine arithmetic quotient geometry, a real logarithmic cusp, and a trace formula in one object. It tests whether the continuous spectrum can be removed intrinsically by restricting to cusp forms rather than by an external cutoff.

### ORBITS

Closed geodesics or diagonal-flow periodic orbits correspond to global conjugacy classes and Hecke data, not one prime per primitive orbit. Prime Hecke excursions are correspondences, not necessarily closed trajectories of F. Restricting to one-prime excursions is a local-support projection and leaves many composite and non-prime closed orbits.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Cusp scaling gives genuine modular cocycles, but the p-adic factor is tied to the full Hecke correspondence and global determinant, not an isolated p^(-m) Jacobian for each prime orbit. Product-formula cancellation and cusp normalization leave the exact finite-place coefficient dependent on the chosen Haar and scattering normalization.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The cusp has a genuine archimedean coordinate and scattering measure, but no calculation identifies its density with (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole exponent -2. The continuous scattering term is a different archimedean contribution.

### SPECTRUM

The cuspidal spectrum is discrete, while the full finite-volume flow has continuous Eisenstein spectrum. Removing the continuous sector gives a discrete subspace but is a spectral projection, not the trace of the full geometric flow. The Hecke spectrum is automorphic and not simply the prime orbit length spectrum.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Finite-volume trace formulas use regularized, relative, or distributional traces because the noncompact cusp contributes continuous spectrum. The cuspidal restriction can yield compact resolvents in elliptic directions, but it is not preserved by the full flow/Hecke correspondence in the required primitive-orbit sense. Ordinary transfer operators remain non-trace-class without smoothing; smoothing alters the Hecke coefficients. The natural L2 norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are an arithmetic locally symmetric quotient, geodesic/diagonal flow, cusp height, Hecke correspondences, cusp scattering, and a cuspidal projection. No zeros are used. The exact one-prime orbit and trace identifications are not proved.

### P1: partial — arithmetic quotient and Hecke algebra give a real multiplicative/additive bridge, but no Gate 1 ordinary trace formula is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — prime excursions are not the complete primitive closed-orbit set, and the cuspidal projection is external.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Finite-volume cusp geometry supplies genuine arithmetic and archimedean structure, but its trace is regularized by the continuous spectrum, its orbits are global conjugacy classes rather than primes, and the exact p^(-m) and gamma kernel are not derived in the required normalization.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Finite volume does not interpolate between compact trace class and infinite-volume noncompact dynamics: the cusp replaces divergent trace mass by an intrinsic continuous spectrum, so removing it requires a spectral projection or regularized trace. Such a projection changes the global orbit trace and cannot simultaneously retain the exact prime coefficients.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 88

The next candidate must derive the continuous cusp contribution and prime orbit terms in one ordinary trace-class operator, without cuspidal projection, relative regularization, or prime-support selection. It must also fix the exact archimedean normalization.

## Candidate 88: Arithmetic spectral triple with logarithmic Dirac operator

### CONSTRUCTION

Let H be l2 of an arithmetic basis indexed by positive integers, let D e_n=(log n)e_n, and let the algebra be generated by prime multiplication and its adjoints on the basis. Define the modular scale through the commutators [D,a_p]=log(p)a_p and use the spectral triple zeta functional to extract prime coefficients. The proposed arithmetic trace is a Dixmier or residue trace of functions of |D|, while the ordinary flow is generated by D. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces explicit prime orbit blocks by one global noncommutative spectral geometry. Prime logarithms arise as commutators with a single Dirac operator, and residue traces are intended to recover the divergent arithmetic density intrinsically.

### ORBITS

The spectral triple has algebraic prime multiplication operators but no classical foliated flow with primitive closed orbits. Products of a_p and a_q give composite multiplication paths, and the algebra does not select primitive primes as geometric periodic returns.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The commutator [D,a_p] gives the exact additive log p, but p^(-m) is not a transverse Radon-Nikodym derivative. It must be inserted through a separate modular operator or KMS weight.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The logarithmic Dirac spectrum supplies a real scale but does not derive the distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2. A heat-kernel asymptotic can produce an archimedean term, but its coefficient is representation-dependent and not identified with the required kernel.

### SPECTRUM

D has discrete logarithmic spectrum but exponentially many integer states at logarithmic energy. Heat operators e^(-t|D|) are trace class only for t>1, while the arithmetic boundary requires t=1. The commutator spectrum records prime logarithms algebraically but does not produce a prime-only dynamical spectrum.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The natural zeta and Dixmier traces are singular or residue traces, not ordinary Hilbert traces of trace-class operators. Ordinary heat traces diverge at the boundary because sum_n n^(-t) diverges at t=1. Replacing the residue trace by an ordinary trace requires damping and changes the arithmetic normalization. The diagonal Dirac representation is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the integer Hilbert basis, logarithmic Dirac operator, prime multiplication algebra, and a Dixmier/residue trace. No zeros are used. The arithmetic basis and algebra are supplied rather than derived from a foliated adelic space.

### P1: partial — commutators provide a clean additive log-prime bridge, but multiplicative orbit and ordinary trace realization are not proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — prime multiplication operators are algebraic generators, not primitive closed-orbit spectral data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). The spectral triple produces log p as a commutator, but its natural arithmetic functional is a residue/Dixmier trace and its ordinary heat trace diverges at the boundary. No prime-orbit flow or exact finite-adic and archimedean geometry is obtained.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A logarithmic Dirac operator can encode additive prime lengths through commutators, but the trace functional that sees the corresponding arithmetic density is necessarily singular at the boundary; replacing it with an ordinary trace-class heat operator removes the exact normalization. Thus noncommutative spectral geometry does not by itself satisfy Gate 1 ordinary trace class.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 89

The next candidate must retain the clean commutator log-prime bridge while replacing the singular residue trace by an ordinary trace-class mechanism and deriving p^(-m) and the archimedean term geometrically.

## Candidate 89: KMS Gibbs modular flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let H be the arithmetic l2 space with logarithmic Hamiltonian D e_n=(log n)e_n and prime multiplication operators a_p. For beta>1 define the normalized Gibbs state
\[
\varphi_\beta(X)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta D}X)}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta D})}.
\]
Its modular automorphism group is sigma_t(X)=e^{itD}Xe^{-itD}, so sigma_t(a_p)=p^{it}a_p. Use the KMS state and modular flow as the global trace mechanism, with the intended beta to approach the arithmetic boundary. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This turns the singular spectral-triple trace into a finite state in its convergence region while retaining exact logarithmic prime commutators. It tests whether a KMS limit can supply ordinary trace class without damping away the arithmetic coefficients.

### ORBITS

The operators a_p are algebraic multiplication generators, not primitive closed orbits of a foliated flow. Products a_p a_q remain composite multiplication words. The modular automorphism group has no prime-periodic orbit interpretation.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The KMS modular group gives p^{it} and the Gibbs density gives n^(-beta), but the finite-adic factor p^(-m) is a thermal weight rather than a transverse Radon-Nikodym Jacobian. It is not derived from an adelic orbit geometry.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The Gibbs Hamiltonian provides a real inverse-temperature parameter, but no derivation of (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or pole exponent -2. Changing beta changes the thermal normalization rather than producing the archimedean explicit-formula term.

### SPECTRUM

D has discrete logarithmic spectrum with multiplicity indexed by integers. The modular flow is unitary and has continuous time spectrum, while the Gibbs density is trace class only for beta>1. No prime-only spectral determinant or geometric orbit spectrum results.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For beta>1, e^(-beta D) is trace class and the KMS state is well defined. As beta approaches 1, the partition function zeta(beta) diverges, so no normalized trace-class Gibbs state exists at the arithmetic boundary. Renormalizing the state gives a singular or semifinite functional, not an ordinary trace-class trace. The Gibbs Hamiltonian representation is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the integer logarithmic Hamiltonian, prime multiplication algebra, Gibbs density, and modular flow. No zeros are used. The arithmetic basis and thermal state are supplied rather than derived from a foliated adelic system.

### P1: partial — the KMS modular flow gives a clean multiplicative-to-additive logarithmic relation for beta>1, but no ordinary boundary trace bridge.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — modular algebra generators are not primitive closed-orbit data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, ORBITS, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). The KMS state is finite only in a damped half-plane; at the arithmetic boundary its partition function diverges and the normalized state becomes singular. Thermal weights are not geometric modular Jacobians, and no prime-orbit or archimedean trace mechanism is derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A finite KMS normalization is equivalent to moving into a convergence half-plane. At the boundary where the arithmetic trace is required, the partition function diverges; any finite replacement is a singular or semifinite functional. Thus thermal modular flow cannot convert the divergent arithmetic mass into an ordinary trace-class Gate 1 system.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 90

The next pass is a consolidation. It must compare Candidates 81–89 and state a cumulative no-go theorem for spectral-triple, moment, Fredholm, hyperbolic, cusp, and KMS mechanisms, distinguishing proved class results from conjectural or partial observations.

## Consolidation 90: Spectral and thermal boundary no-go

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers Candidates 81 through 89: inverse-spectral compactification, conditional operator series, commutator anomalies, Fredholm pole families, Jacobi moment operators, countable hyperbolic flows, finite-volume cusp flows, arithmetic spectral triples, and KMS Gibbs modular flows. It also compares them with the geometric and global-assembly no-go results already recorded. The theorem is restricted to the stated constructions and Gate 1 ordinary trace-class requirements.

### CUMULATIVE RESULT

The spectral and thermal mechanisms split into two regimes.

In the convergent regime, damping, Gibbs factors, heat kernels, compact eigenvalues, finite-volume cutoffs, or trace-class Fredholm families produce legitimate operators. But convergence requires moving to a half-plane or introducing a summable factor. The resulting trace coefficients are damped, and the exact boundary prime coefficient p^(-1) is not retained.

In the boundary regime, the mechanisms recover the desired arithmetic density only through one of four non-Gate-1 devices: an unbounded inverse calculus, a conditional operator series, a residue/Dixmier or anomaly trace, or a regularized/relative determinant. Each device changes the required ordinary Hilbert trace or its domain.

Moment and Jacobi realizations do not derive the von Mangoldt sequence; they take it as their moment functional. Hyperbolic and cusp realizations can supply genuine orbits and real geometry, but their full primitive spectrum is larger than the primes, their trace is anisotropic, continuous, or regularized, and their exact modular and archimedean factors are not derived.

### CONSOLIDATED NO-GO STATEMENT

Within the union of the classes tested in Candidates 81–89, no construction simultaneously has:

- ordinary trace-class operators at the exact arithmetic boundary;
- exact positive p^(-m) coefficients without damping;
- a zero-independent global flow with primitive prime closed orbits;
- a derived finite-adic modular cocycle;
- a derived archimedean distribution.

The proof is by the alternatives above: summable operators alter the coefficients; unsummable operators require singular, conditional, unbounded, or regularized traces; geometric systems have extra orbit spectra or continuous cusp/modulus sectors; and moment/determinant systems insert the arithmetic data instead of deriving them.

### STATUS

PARTIAL NO-GO. The result is proved only for the union of the explicitly stated classes and assumptions. It does not rule out a genuinely new object whose ordinary trace is finite for a nonlocal reason while retaining exact boundary coefficients and whose geometry derives both finite and infinite-place data.

### REMAINING OPEN CLASS

The next candidate must evade all four spectral alternatives simultaneously. It must not use damping, inverse unbounded calculus, conditional summation, residue/Dixmier traces, relative regularization, post-trace arithmetic input, prime-sector projection, or a selected subspace of a larger orbit spectrum.

### RESULT

CONSOLIDATION 90 — PARTIAL NO-GO. Candidates 81–89 close the tested spectral, thermal, moment, Fredholm, hyperbolic, and cuspidal mechanisms under Gate 1, while leaving one genuinely new nonlocal ordinary-trace mechanism open.

along the proposed prime periodic orbit x_p, while allowing J_p to vary elsewhere so finite-measure consistency is possible. This avoids the constant-Jacobian contradiction of Candidate 67. The modular factor is required only on periodic orbit products, while the global finite measure can remain normalized.

Separating the x_p orbits requires invariant components or a non-invariant periodic-orbit selection.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Variable cocycles can have average derivative one while having periodic products p^(-m), so the finite-measure integral contradiction is avoided. However, the cocycles are prescribed along the prime orbits; no adelic action derives them. The periodic product is arithmetic input.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The compact suspension supplies real roof time but no canonical infinite-place distribution. The factor (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole exponent -2 remain external.

Retaining the selected prime orbit weights gives at least sum_p p^(-1) unless additional cancellations or damping are introduced. Damping changes the periodic products; signed cancellation is not ordinary trace-norm cancellation. The natural compact finite-measure representation is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

## Candidate 92: Livsic-derived arithmetic modular cocycle

### CONSTRUCTION

Let F be a transitive Anosov flow with a Hölder real cocycle a over its transverse dynamics. Require its period integral over a primitive orbit gamma_p to equal -log p for one orbit assigned to each prime:
\[
\int_{\gamma_p}a=-\log p.
\]
Use the Livsic cohomology framework to seek one global cocycle a whose periodic integrals generate the finite-adic modular factors, rather than prescribing separate cocycles. Couple the flow roof to log p on the same selected periodic orbits. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This replaces independent variable cocycles by one global cohomology class. Periodic data are constrained by the flow and, if compatible, a Livsic theorem produces a single Hölder cocycle.

### ORBITS

A transitive Anosov flow has infinitely many primitive periodic orbits beyond the selected gamma_p. The cocycle assigns integrals to all of them, and no mechanism forces the unselected periods to vanish from the trace. Selecting one orbit per prime is still external. If the selected prime data are required to exhaust the periodic set, the full Anosov orbit spectrum obstruction returns.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The periodic integral gives a genuine cocycle interpretation of p^(-1) along the selected orbit. But Livsic theory does not generate the numerical data -log p; it only tests whether a prescribed collection of periodic integrals is compatible with a Hölder cocycle. Compatibility with all other periodic orbit relations is unproved.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The Anosov flow supplies a smooth time variable, but the cocycle cohomology does not derive the distribution (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or pole exponent -2. An extra potential or transfer weight is required.

### SPECTRUM

The transfer operator weighted by a Livsic cocycle has Ruelle resonances determined by the full periodic orbit set. The selected prime orbit factors are not a complete spectral determinant. Anisotropic spaces produce nuclear resonance traces, not ordinary Hilbert trace-class operators.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The orbit weights p^(-1) on the selected prime cycles already have divergent sum. If the full flow contains additional cycles, their weights must be controlled without altering the selected factors. Anisotropic nuclearity can provide a regularized trace, but ordinary Hilbert trace class is not automatic and generally fails on the natural L2 space. The natural flow norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are a transitive Anosov flow, selected prime periodic orbits, prescribed period integrals -log p, and Livsic cohomology. No zeros are used. The prime orbit selection and numerical periods remain external.

### P1: partial — one global cocycle can in principle relate additive period integrals to multiplicative weights, but the arithmetic values and orbit bridge are not derived.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — the complete periodic spectrum is larger than the prime subset and prime selection is external.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). Livsic cohomology can unify periodic cocycle data, but it cannot make a transitive flow have only prime periodic orbits or make the selected prime orbit weights trace summable. The archimedean term is not derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A global cocycle cohomology theorem can unify compatible periodic weights but cannot remove the ambient flow's other periodic orbits. Therefore deriving p^(-1) through one Livsic cocycle does not solve the prime-spectrum or ordinary-trace problems; it transfers the arithmetic input into periodic orbit constraints.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 93

The next candidate must provide a flow whose complete periodic orbit set is arithmetically prime-indexed, or prove an intrinsic trace identity that cancels all nonprime periodic orbits without a projection or regularized trace. It must also derive the archimedean distribution.

## Candidate 93: Infinite-memory prime renewal shift

### CONSTRUCTION

Let X be a compact or countable-state symbolic flow with infinite memory. A bi-infinite itinerary is admissible only if every complete recurrent word is one of a prescribed family of prime words w_p, with roof length log p and a cocycle product p^(-1). The admissibility rule is global and nonlocal: it checks the entire past and future, so composite concatenations are rejected without a reset state or explicit character projection. Define the transfer operator on the path space with the global constraint. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This attempts to obtain prime-only recurrence from an intrinsic nonlocal constraint rather than local forbidden transitions, reset gates, or disconnected prime blocks. It is a genuinely new symbolic class with no finite-memory graph assumption.

### ORBITS

By construction the recurrent periodic sequences are prime words, so the desired orbit set can be imposed. However, the prime words and their roof lengths are the defining data of the shift; the arithmetic orbit bijection is not derived from an underlying adelic action. If the shift is made topologically transitive, connecting words create additional periodic sequences; if all connecting words are forbidden, the recurrent components are dynamically disconnected.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The p^(-1) cocycle products are assigned to the prime words. The nonlocal admissibility rule has no finite-adic Radon-Nikodym origin and supplies no canonical transverse Jacobian.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The suspension roof gives real periods but no derivation of (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2. The infinite-memory constraint has no natural infinite-place measure.

### SPECTRUM

Infinite-memory transfer operators may fail to be compact or nuclear unless strong summable-variation conditions are imposed. Those conditions introduce damping of long words and alter the exact prime weights. A compact path-space shift with exactly the prescribed recurrent words is not a single connected mixing flow.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

If the transfer operator is nuclear, the nuclear norm must control all admissible word weights. With one positive p^(-1) contribution per prime, the prime harmonic mass remains divergent unless additional damping or cancellation is added. If the operator is not nuclear, the trace is unavailable as an ordinary trace-class trace. A nonlocal admissibility rule can remove composite words but cannot reduce the singular-value cost of the retained prime words.

### INPUTS

The inputs are prime words, roof lengths log p, global infinite-memory admissibility, and prescribed cocycle products p^(-1). No zeros are used. The defining recurrence set is arithmetic input rather than derived geometry.

### P1: partial — nonlocal symbolic recurrence can encode prime words and additive roofs, but no arithmetic-to-additive derivation is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: partial — prime periodic words can be enforced intrinsically within the shift, but only as prescribed recurrence data and without a derived adelic flow.

### VERDICT

FAIL(TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). Infinite-memory admissibility can avoid local mixed words, but it simply moves the prime selection into the definition of the recurrent set. Nuclearity retains the divergent prime mass unless damping changes the coefficients; the modular and archimedean structures remain external.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

A nonlocal recurrence rule can eliminate composite words without a reset or finite-memory projection, but then the exact prime orbit set is itself an input axiom. It provides no arithmetic derivation and does not change the ordinary trace-norm lower bound of the retained positive prime contributions.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 94

The next candidate must derive the nonlocal recurrence rule from an intrinsic adelic or arithmetic invariant, not prescribe the prime words. It must preserve ordinary trace class with exact p^(-1) weights and derive the archimedean factor.

## Candidate 94: Divisibility-poset incidence flow

### CONSTRUCTION

Let P be the directed divisibility poset of positive integers, with an edge n to np for every prime p. Equip the incidence algebra with the zeta operator Z and its Möbius inverse M. Give an edge n to np the length log p and formal modular factor p^(-1). Form a Hilbert representation of the incidence algebra on l2(P), and attempt to obtain the arithmetic trace from closed incidence paths or from the determinant of Z. Primes are intended to appear as irreducible edges rather than named eigenvalue channels. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This is a global arithmetic object whose prime structure is intrinsic to unique factorization and whose Möbius inverse is canonical. It avoids a prime-indexed direct sum and does not prescribe a separate periodic block for each p.

### ORBITS

The divisibility graph is acyclic: every edge strictly increases n. Therefore it has no nontrivial closed paths and no periodic orbits. Adding inverse edges creates cycles, but then every factorization path can return through many composite words and the prime edges are no longer primitive closed orbits.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The edge label p^(-1) is canonical as an arithmetic ratio between n and np, but it is an assigned incidence weight rather than a Radon-Nikodym derivative of a transverse flow. The acyclic poset has no invertible dynamics that could generate the cocycle.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The logarithmic edge length gives an additive coordinate, but the incidence algebra contains no real-place measure or kernel. The factor (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole exponent -2 are absent.

### SPECTRUM

The zeta operator on the infinite divisibility poset is triangular/quasinilpotent in finite truncations and has no periodic orbit spectrum. Infinite representations have unbounded multiplicities and noncompact spectrum. The Möbius inverse is an algebraic inverse, not a flow generator.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Finite truncations are nilpotent and have zero trace of every positive power, so they cannot produce the positive prime orbit trace. Infinite incidence operators are not trace class under the natural l2 norm; damping the edges gives nuclearity but changes the p^(-1) weights. Adding inverse edges to create cycles restores mixed composite paths and the previous trace-norm divergence.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the divisibility poset, zeta and Möbius incidence operators, edge lengths log p, and arithmetic edge weights p^(-1). No zeros are used. The construction is canonical as an arithmetic category but has no invertible flow.

### P1: partial — unique factorization gives an intrinsic multiplicative-to-additive edge labeling, but no closed-orbit trace bridge exists.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — the canonical incidence dynamics is acyclic and has no primitive closed orbits.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). The divisibility poset makes primes intrinsic but destroys invertibility and periodic orbits. Finite incidence truncations have zero trace, while infinite or damped versions are non-trace-class or alter the arithmetic weights. No archimedean factor is derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Canonical unique-factorization incidence is intrinsically acyclic. Making prime factors into closed orbits requires adding inverse dynamics, which introduces composite return words and the previously established trace and orbit obstructions. Thus arithmetic irreducibility alone does not supply a dynamical prime-orbit trace.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 95

The next candidate must add invertibility to a canonical arithmetic incidence structure without creating composite cycles or losing ordinary trace class, and must derive the archimedean distribution from the same object.

## Candidate 95: Grothendieck-completed divisibility groupoid

### CONSTRUCTION

Complete the divisibility monoid of positive integers to the free abelian group Q_+ generated by the prime symbols. Give p the length log p and the character p^(-s). Form the groupoid or crossed-product representation of Q_+ acting on the completed divisibility object, so every prime edge is invertible. Define the arithmetic trace through groupoid fixed points and the determinant of the length representation. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This adds invertibility canonically rather than by arbitrary inverse edges: the Grothendieck completion is forced by unique factorization. It directly tests whether the acyclic incidence obstruction disappears under canonical group completion.

### ORBITS

The completed group is abelian and has elements represented by all rational products of prime powers. Primitive group elements are not canonically the individual primes; p q and p/q are equally valid group elements. The action has no intrinsic periodic orbit corresponding to one prime unless a quotient or fixed-point condition is added. Any such condition selects prime support externally.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The group character p^(-s) gives a multiplicative length weight, but no transverse Radon-Nikodym derivative is derived. In a Haar representation of the completed group, the action is measure preserving and its modular factor is 1; in a nonunimodular representation the weighting is a chosen cocycle.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The length homomorphism Q_+ to R gives the logarithmic coordinate, but the group completion contains no infinite-place distribution. The factor (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) and pole exponent -2 are absent.

### SPECTRUM

The regular representation of the free abelian group completion has continuous character spectrum. A compact dual has pure character spectrum but no prime-specific periodic returns. Any discrete quotient has a chosen lattice or finite quotient, and its spectrum depends on that choice.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The regular groupoid representation has infinite multiplicity or continuous spectrum and is not trace class. Finite quotients have finite traces but identify many rational products and do not stabilize to a prime-only determinant. Damping or choosing a finite trace ideal changes the group character weights. The natural Haar representation is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are the canonical group completion Q_+, the length homomorphism log, a groupoid representation, and arithmetic characters. No zeros are used. The quotient or fixed-point selector needed for prime orbits is not canonical.

### P1: partial — group completion gives a canonical multiplicative-to-additive length map, but no prime-orbit trace bridge.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — group completion erases primitive-prime distinction and supplies continuous or quotient-dependent orbit data.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). Canonical group completion restores invertibility but enlarges the dynamics to all rational products and loses a distinguished prime orbit class. Natural representations are continuous/non-trace-class; finite quotients are arbitrary. No archimedean factor is derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Canonical invertible completion of unique-factorization incidence destroys prime primitiveness: once inverse prime edges are admitted, the natural orbit labels are all rational products, not individual primes. Recovering primes requires an external support projection, while the natural group representation has no ordinary trace-class spectrum.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 96

The next candidate must recover individual prime primitive orbits from an invertible arithmetic completion without a support projection or finite quotient, while retaining ordinary trace class and deriving the archimedean factor.

## Candidate 96: Valuation-cone flow on Spec Z

### CONSTRUCTION

Use the set of nonarchimedean valuations of Q, with one valuation ray for each prime p and the archimedean valuation at infinity. Let u_p be the valuation coordinate, assign the scaling action n to u_p by v_p(n), and give the prime transition p a length log p and local factor p^(-1). Form a global valuation groupoid over the prime spectrum with a proposed flow in the logarithmic valuation coordinates. The trace is intended to sum fixed valuation rays. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This uses the canonical arithmetic geometry of Spec Z directly. Prime labels are points of the scheme rather than artificially named Hilbert basis vectors, and the infinite place is included from the start.

### ORBITS

Valuation rays are stationary arithmetic labels, not periodic trajectories of a one-parameter invertible flow. The scaling action changes valuation coordinates by integers and is not periodic on the rays. Quotienting coordinates to make returns periodic is an external choice and creates composite valuation vectors.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The valuation of p gives a canonical discrete p-adic scaling, but no finite transverse measure on the valuation groupoid has been specified whose Jacobian is p^(-m). The product formula couples all valuations and prevents isolating a finite-place factor without a relative normalization.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The infinite valuation is present as a formal coordinate, but no measure on the collection of valuation rays derives (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or the pole exponent -2. The archimedean point is a label, not a trace-density mechanism.

### SPECTRUM

The valuation groupoid has a discrete prime-indexed label space together with an unbounded valuation lattice. Its natural translation representation is noncompact and has continuous or infinite-multiplicity spectrum. A finite truncation has finite spectrum but no cutoff-independent trace.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The fixed-ray trace contains one positive p^(-1) term for every prime, so its absolute mass diverges at the arithmetic boundary. Truncating the valuation set or adding decay changes the prime coefficients. The product formula may cancel signed global valuation sums, but such cancellation is not ordinary trace-norm cancellation. The natural counting/valuation norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are Spec Z prime points, valuation coordinates, the product formula, logarithmic prime lengths, and proposed valuation transitions. No zeros are used. The trace measure and flow periodicity are not canonically supplied by Spec Z.

### P1: partial — valuations give a canonical multiplicative-to-additive bridge, but no ordinary periodic-orbit trace is constructed.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — scheme points and valuation rays are not primitive closed flow orbits.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN). Spec Z supplies canonical prime and infinite-place labels but not a periodic flow or trace-class valuation groupoid. Product-formula cancellation does not solve ordinary trace norm, and the archimedean density is not derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Arithmetic scheme points are canonical labels but not dynamical returns: turning valuations into periodic flow orbits requires an additional quotient or compactification that introduces composite valuation vectors. The canonical arithmetic geometry alone therefore supplies neither the required orbit trace nor the archimedean measure.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 97

The next candidate must construct an invertible flow directly from valuation geometry, with prime points as complete primitive periodic orbits, a finite ordinary trace, and a derived infinite-place density.

## Candidate 97: Arakelov tropical valuation skeleton

### CONSTRUCTION

Form a proposed tropical/Arakelov skeleton S with one ray for every finite prime valuation and one distinguished infinite ray, glued at a global arithmetic vertex. Let the flow translate along the logarithmic length coordinate, with a finite ray step at p assigned length log p and modular factor p^(-1). Use the Arakelov metric and global product formula to define one measure on S, and define a transfer trace from the resulting metric graph flow. No zero locations are used.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

This attempts to unify the finite and infinite places geometrically. The global vertex and Arakelov metric are intended to derive the archimedean normalization rather than append it after a finite-prime construction.

### ORBITS

The skeleton is a tree-like metric graph with rays, so translations along rays are not periodic. Gluing rays at the global vertex creates paths that can return only if inverse edges or compact loops are added; those loops generate composite paths and are not canonically indexed by individual primes. Prime rays are labels, not primitive closed flow orbits.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The Arakelov metric can encode finite valuation lengths and a global product-formula relation, but a metric length is not automatically a transverse Radon-Nikodym derivative. The factor p^(-m) remains a chosen local weight unless a specific foliated measure and return map are constructed.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The infinite ray is present, but no calculation from the tropical metric produces (1-e^(-2t))^(-1) or pole exponent -2. The Arakelov metric fixes a normalization only after choosing a Green function and boundary measure.

### SPECTRUM

A metric-tree translation has continuous spectrum and no periodic orbit spectrum. Compact graph approximations have discrete spectra but depend on truncation and added boundary conditions. The global vertex does not create a trace-class flow generator.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The natural length-space representation is noncompact and has continuous spectrum. Truncating rays or adding confining weights makes transfer operators trace class only by changing the prime lengths or weights. The product formula can cancel global signed length sums, but not the singular values of a positive trace contribution. The natural metric norm is normal and triggers NORM-FORCES-NORMALITY.

### INPUTS

The inputs are finite and infinite valuation rays, an Arakelov metric, a tropical global vertex, logarithmic lengths log p, and local p^(-1) weights. No zeros are used. The boundary Green function and trace measure are not canonically fixed.

### P1: partial — Arakelov geometry unifies valuation lengths and the infinite place formally, but no exact ordinary trace bridge is proved.
### P2: unknown — positivity is outside Gate 1 and is not asserted.
### P3: unknown — no s to 1-s symmetry is defined.
### P4: outside scope — no Xi or zero identification is attempted.
### P5: fails — the skeleton has rays rather than primitive prime closed orbits.

### VERDICT

FAIL(ORBITS, TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN). The tropical skeleton unifies finite and infinite labels but has nonperiodic rays and continuous spectrum. Compactification or loop insertion introduces arbitrary boundary data and composite paths; the exact modular and archimedean terms remain un-derived.

### NEW OBSTRUCTION

Unifying all places in a tree-like Arakelov skeleton does not create periodic arithmetic dynamics: rays provide valuation labels and continuous translation, while loops require extra quotient data that generate composite paths. The global metric therefore cannot simultaneously be canonical, periodic at primes, and ordinary trace class in this class.

### CONSTRAINT FOR CANDIDATE 98

The next candidate must turn the unified Arakelov place space into a canonical invertible periodic flow without arbitrary loops or boundary conditions, while deriving p^(-m), the archimedean kernel, and ordinary trace class.

## Consolidation 100: Gate 1 no-go for the tested compact arithmetic-return class

### SCOPE

This consolidation covers the constructions tested in Candidates 91–99: compact or inverse-limit arithmetic transversals, prime-marked return sections, profinite or solenoid correspondences, and their direct or inverse-limit assemblies. It does not claim a no-go theorem for all foliated systems.

### CONSOLIDATED FACT 1: PRIME-ONLY INVERTIBLE ORBITS

In every tested construction, prime multiplication is either a noninvertible correspondence or an invertible completion. The noninvertible case has no ordinary flow orbit with a Lefschetz return map. The invertible completion admits words in multiple prime generators, hence composite periodic paths. Removing mixed words by sector projection or resetting disconnects the global recurrent system.

### CONSOLIDATED FACT 2: MODULAR COCYCLE

The assigned local factor (p^{-m}) is not automatically a transverse Jacobian. For compact Haar translations the Jacobian is one; for multiplication correspondences the map is not an invertible self-map of the compact transversal. Therefore the stated constructions do not derive the required modular factors from a single invertible foliated flow.

### CONSOLIDATED FACT 3: ORDINARY TRACE CLASS

Whenever the prime return channels contribute positively with the required (p^{-1}) mass, their total trace mass is bounded below by a divergent quantity comparable to (sum_p p^{-1}). Graded cancellation can change a formal supertrace but cannot make the underlying positive operator trace class. Finite truncation or damping changes the Gate 1 coefficients.

### CONSOLIDATED FACT 4: ARCHIMEDEAN TERM

Compact finite-place constructions do not force a stationary archimedean point with exponent (-2) or the kernel ((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}). Adding a real factor or boundary condition supplies data externally rather than deriving it from the same return dynamics.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

For the tested class of compact/inverse-limit arithmetic correspondences with prime multiplication as the generating return maps, no construction simultaneously has: (i) a connected invertible flow with primitive closed orbits exactly indexed by primes, (ii) derived Radon–Nikodym factors (p^{-m}), and (iii) an ordinary trace-class transfer carrying the unsmoothed prime sum. The obstruction is a trichotomy: noninvertibility, mixed composite returns after inversion, or loss of ordinary trace class.

### STATUS

This is a class-restricted Gate 1 no-go statement, not a theorem about arbitrary Deninger systems, not a positivity result, and not an RH result.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 101 must leave the compact arithmetic-correspondence class. It must use a genuinely different source of invertibility and trace-class regularization, while deriving rather than assigning the prime cocycle and archimedean contribution.

## Consolidation 110: Sector-versus-orbit no-go

### SCOPE

Candidates 101–110 tested connected geometric flows, adelic quotients, ideal moduli, noncommutative endomorphisms, smooth mapping tori, arithmetic geodesics, and categorical Frobenius systems.

### CONSOLIDATED RESULT

Every construction made prime information available in one of four forms: a Hecke correspondence, an endomorphism degree, a moduli label, or a sector/filter of a larger periodic system. None made primality an intrinsic invariant of every primitive closed orbit of one connected invertible flow.

If sectors are recombined to obtain one connected system, mixed composite returns appear. If they remain separated or are filtered out, the recurrent dynamics is disconnected or the trace functional is altered. This is independent of whether the carrier is a graph, manifold, adelic quotient, noncommutative algebra, moduli space, or arithmetic topos.

The same constructions assign rather than derive the (p^{-m}) factor, fail to force the archimedean stationary contribution, and lose ordinary trace class at the unsmoothed prime boundary.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

For the tested class of arithmetic constructions in which prime data enter only as correspondences, endomorphism degrees, labels, or decomposed sectors of a larger flow, Gate 1 cannot be satisfied simultaneously. The missing mechanism must make prime primitiveness a global dynamical invariant before any filtering, sector decomposition, or trace extraction.

### STATUS

This is a class-restricted consolidation, not a universal no-go theorem and not a result about positivity or RH.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 111 must introduce a genuinely new primitive notion—neither a label, sector, correspondence, degree, nor post hoc filter—and prove that it is preserved by one connected invertible flow.

## Consolidation 120: Arithmetic-bridge relocation no-go

### SCOPE

Candidates 111–119 tested increasingly abstract mechanisms intended to make prime primitiveness intrinsic: higher categories, nonlinear ideal boundaries, profinite cocycles, algebraic solenoids, global potentials, topological indices, self-similar flows, and universal irreducible spectra.

### CONSOLIDATED RESULT

The same arithmetic bridge cannot be eliminated by changing its representation. Prime information appears as one of:

- a label or coordinate;
- a sector or invariant stratum;
- a correspondence or endomorphism degree;
- a potential coefficient or return constraint;
- a topological index;
- an irreducible spectrum of a specially chosen object.

When the information is not inserted, no mechanism tested forces the primitive periods to be exactly (log p). When it is inserted indirectly, the construction is circular with respect to P1.

### GATE 1 CONSEQUENCE

Within the tested class, a zero-independent connected invertible flow with exact prime-only primitive orbits has not been constructed. The failures are not evidence that such a flow is impossible in all mathematics; they identify the missing theorem: a canonical arithmetic object whose intrinsic recurrence spectrum is provably the rational-prime spectrum and whose transverse geometry simultaneously derives (p^{-m}), the archimedean kernel, and ordinary trace class.

### REMAINING LIVE CLASS

Not ruled out is a construction in which the prime spectrum is a theorem of a genuinely new global object—neither a chosen label nor a representation of already supplied primes—and in which the same object supplies a canonical nonsingular measure, stationary infinite-place geometry, and trace-class regularization without damping the target coefficients.

### STATUS

This is a class-restricted consolidation of the archive. It is not a universal no-go theorem, not a positivity result, and not an RH result.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 121 must either instantiate the remaining live class concretely or produce a sharper theorem showing that its arithmetic recurrence requirement forces an equivalent prime encoding.

## Consolidation 130: Trace-class boundary for the tested global mechanisms

### SCOPE

Candidates 121–130 tested the remaining universal-object direction and the principal mechanisms for globalizing the one-prime model: absolute arithmetic curves, weighted completions, intrinsic Laplacians, harmonic kernels, symmetry quotients, compact resolvents, arithmetic compactification, and relative cohomology.

### CONSOLIDATED RESULT

The following alternatives have now been separated:

1. **Keep the natural uncompactified norm direction.** The trivial sector has continuous spectrum, so the unsmoothed transfer is not ordinary trace class.
2. **Compactify or confine the norm direction.** A common period lattice is incompatible with the incommensurable prime lengths, or the boundary data change the flow.
3. **Use heat, Sobolev, or conductor damping.** Trace class appears only after changing the transfer or its coefficients.
4. **Use harmonic or invariant quotients.** Either infinitely many modes remain, or arithmetic modes are removed.
5. **Use relative, b-, semifinite, or zeta traces.** These may formalize an explicit formula but are excluded by Gate 1.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

For the tested class of globalizations of the one-prime compact model, no ordinary trace-class operator has been obtained simultaneously with the uncompactified arithmetic scaling action and the exact unsmoothed prime coefficients. The missing possibility is a new theorem that makes the uncompactified global cohomology intrinsically discrete and trace class without compactification, damping, quotienting away arithmetic modes, or replacing the trace notion.

### STATUS

This is a class-restricted Gate 1 consolidation, not a universal no-go theorem and not a result about positivity or RH.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 131 must construct an intrinsically discrete uncompactified global cohomology, or prove a sharper impossibility theorem for that remaining class.

## Consolidation 140: Canonical global arithmetic operations do not supply Gate 1 orbit geometry

### MOST FREQUENT FAILURE CLASS

The dominant class since Consolidation 130 is **ORBITS**, usually together with **MODULAR**, **ARCHIMEDEAN**, and **TRACE** failures. Candidates 131--139 tested global harmonic/cohomological, incidence, Hecke, Dirac, and idèle-class mechanisms. Each supplied arithmetic operations or representations, but none supplied the required prime-indexed primitive closed-orbit geometry with the exact archimedean contribution and ordinary trace class.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

**Partial no-go theorem for the tested canonical global-operation class.** Consider a construction whose arithmetic core is one of the following canonical mechanisms on the global arithmetic object: a global harmonic/cohomological complex, an incidence/Möbius complex, a Hecke convolution algebra, an adelic Dirac or differential complex, or the regular translation action of the idèle class group. Suppose its flow and transverse action are generated directly by that operation, with no separately adjoined prime return map, no post hoc quotient selecting prime packets, and no independently assigned modular weights. Then the construction cannot satisfy all of the following simultaneously:

1. primitive nonstationary closed orbits in bijection with rational primes and primitive lengths \(\log p\);
2. intrinsic negative-time factors \(p^{-m}\) coming from the flow's Jacobian;
3. a stationary archimedean point with exponent \(-2\);
4. an ordinary trace-class global cohomological transfer for every compactly supported positive-time test.

The reason is structural. Incidence and divisibility geometries are acyclic, so they have no native invertible recurrence; adjoining inverses produces mixed valuation cycles. Hecke and convolution operations preserve the composite multiplicative algebra and its representation multiplicities rather than turning prime generators into isolated geometric orbits. Dirac, harmonic, and cohomological realizations alter the spectrum or compactness but do not create primitive orbit geometry. The idèle-class translation action is invertible but its norm direction is noncompact and its compact directions have continuous recurrence rather than isolated prime periods. In all cases, the arithmetic ratio \(n/(np)=p^{-1}\) or a Hecke coefficient is a scalar/correspondence weight, not automatically the Radon--Nikodym derivative of an invertible flow. Finally, none of these native mechanisms contains a distinguished boundary stationary point whose local fixed-point contribution is \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\).

This is a complete argument for the stated class and scope, but not a no-go theorem for arbitrary adelic foliated spaces. It does not rule out a new transverse geometry that combines a genuinely invertible recurrence with a canonical additive normal direction and a spectrally compact global cohomology.

### STATUS

**PARTIAL.** The obstruction is proved for the explicitly stated operation-generated subclasses and follows from their native geometry and measure action. The universal claim over every possible adelic transverse structure remains open.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The concentration on orbit failure is **forced by the Gate 1 specification**, not merely an artifact of candidate naming. Gate 1 requires both isolated prime closed orbits and an exact global trace formula. Candidates that supply only an arithmetic operator, correspondence, or representation cannot pass unless that object also supplies the geometric recurrence and trace mechanism. The repeated orbit failure is therefore a constraint imposed by the target, although the tested subclasses are not exhaustive.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The archive now rules out the following proposed replacements for the finite-field transversal \(\mathbb Z_p^m\):

- global incidence/Möbius geometry: acyclic, with mixed cycles after inversion;
- Hecke/convolution sectors: algebraically canonical but composite and multiplicity-preserving;
- harmonic/Dirac/cohomological completions: capable of changing spectral compactness but not of generating prime orbit geometry;
- idèle-class translations: invertible but continuously recurrent/noncompact, with trivial Haar Jacobian.

A viable all-prime replacement must therefore be a new quotient or suspension-like transverse geometry whose prime returns are native rather than assigned, whose additive finite-adelic normal direction supplies the \(p^{-m}\) Jacobian, whose boundary compactification supplies the archimedean point, and whose invariant transverse cohomology is spectrally compact without forcing a zero-dependent normality condition.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**SEARCH CONTINUES.** The tested canonical global-operation class is partially closed for Gate 1, but no universal no-go theorem has been established and no pass-candidate has appeared.

## Candidate 141: Global finite-adelic arithmetic suspension

Let \(\mathbb A_f\) be the finite adeles with additive Haar measure \(dx_f\), let \(R=\mathbb R\) be a logarithmic flow coordinate, and let \(\mathbb Q_{>0}^{\times}\) act diagonally by
\[
q\cdot(x,u)=(qx,u-\log q).
\]
Define
\[
X=(\mathbb A_f\times R)/\mathbb Q_{>0}^{\times}
\]
where the quotient is understood on the standard adelic quotient charts, with the flow \(\phi^t[x,u]=[x,u+t]\). The transverse structure is the finite-adelic additive direction, and the candidate leafwise complex is the de Rham complex along the \(u\)-flow together with the harmonic/locally constant finite-adelic sector selected by the quotient. No zero locations are used.

The finite-adelic additive direction replaces \(\mathbb Z_p^m\), but all primes are present simultaneously in \(\mathbb A_f\). The logarithmic quotient coordinate replaces the single finite-field scale \(q\). The proposed replacement for Assumption (iv) is the globally rational-invariant finite-adelic harmonic sector: functions invariant under the diagonal \(\mathbb Q_{>0}^{\times}\)-action and locally constant on compact adelic slices. Unlike literal local constancy, the selection is imposed by the global quotient and is intended to remove independent conductor multiplicities.

### ORBITS

For \(p=2\), the intended return has length \(\log 2\), and its first two iterates would have lengths \(\log 2\) and \(2\log 2\), each with multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). For \(p=3\), the intended lengths would be \(\log 3\) and \(2\log 3\), again with multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). However, these are not actually primitive closed orbits of the displayed quotient flow. The diagonal relation identifies a \(u\)-translation by \(\log q\) for every positive rational \(q\), and therefore does not isolate the prime translations. At the zero finite-adele point, all rational scalings fix the transverse coordinate, but the subgroup \(\{\log q:q\in\mathbb Q_{>0}^{\times}\}\) is dense in \(R\), so the quotient flow is non-Hausdorff or has collapsed recurrence rather than separate prime orbits.

On the finite adeles,
\[
d(qx_f)=|q|_f\,dx_f,
\qquad |p^m|_f=p^{-m}.
\]
Thus the finite-adelic normal direction does produce the local factor \(p^{-m}\) before quotienting. But the diagonal real coordinate contributes the reciprocal archimedean scaling by the product formula. In the global quotient the factor is not the Lefschetz multiplier of an isolated prime return; it is a measure-scaling identity on a coordinate chart. The required prime-by-prime modular factor in the final supertrace has therefore not been derived.

(1-e^{-2t})^{-1}

is available. Adding a boundary fixed point and assigning this exponent would be extra data, not a consequence of the quotient.

The quotient retains a continuous logarithmic/adelic harmonic spectrum. The rational-invariant sector is not shown to decompose into finite-dimensional conductor blocks with counting \(O(T\log T)\). If the full finite-adelic character spectrum is retained, independent conductor modes occur with infinite or non-summable multiplicity. If one passes to the invariant sector, the quotient removes prime-local labels together with the unwanted modes, and no theorem identifies the remaining spectrum as the required global arithmetic cohomology.

The finite-adelic quotient does not by itself provide a compact-resolvent generator or finite transverse multiplicity. Consequently ordinary trace class is not established; in the unreduced representation the trace is distributional/semifinite, while a conductor cutoff or heat damping changes the exact trace coefficients. The proposed invariant sector has no proved Hilbert norm or compactness estimate, so it cannot supply the missing Assumption (iv).

Before inversion, positive words correspond to integer products and have positive-word lengths \(\log n\). After adjoining inverses to obtain a genuine flow, the word \(T_2T_3^{-1}\) has length \(\log2-\log3\), and commutativity identifies many distinct word presentations. The boundary reduction does not remove these inverse and mixed words; it only changes representatives. Thus primitive isotropy is not in bijection with the individual prime generators.

## Candidate 148: Connected prime bouquet with nonconcatenating junction

### CONSTRUCTION

Define the flow to traverse each loop at unit speed but impose a reflecting, non-transmitting boundary condition at \(v_\infty\): a trajectory returning to the junction is reflected back into the same loop and cannot switch to another prime loop. Use the graph de Rham complex with the junction matching condition as the candidate leafwise cohomology. The graph is topologically connected, but the flow's prime loops are dynamically nonconcatenating.

The bouquet junction replaces the finite-field transversal and attempts to assemble all primes into one connected object. The loop lengths replace the scale \(q\). The reflecting junction is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv): it prevents cross-prime propagation while keeping one common geometric point and one common transverse fiber.

The \(p=2\) loop gives a primitive orbit of length \(\log2\), with first iterate \(2\log2\), multiplicity one and intended sign \(+1\). The \(p=3\) loop gives the analogous lengths \(\log3\) and \(2\log3\). Because the junction reflects within the incoming loop, mixed \(2\)-\(3\) concatenations are absent. Thus the prime orbit list is correct at the graph level.

But the reflecting boundary condition decomposes the flow operator into invariant loop sectors. Topological connectedness does not create dynamical connectedness: no flow orbit travels from \(C_2\) to \(C_3\). The prime sectors therefore remain direct-sum-like.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The proposed \(p\)-loop transverse normal map has local factor \(p^{-1}\) on each return. Since the junction does not transmit between loops, iterates preserve \(p^{-m}\). However, this is a loop-specific boundary assignment; no single global flow Jacobian derives all \(p^{-1}\) factors from one connected transverse map. The common junction does not remove that local choice.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The junction \(v_\infty\) is a natural candidate for the infinite place, but the reflecting condition gives a discrete graph vertex, not a transverse map with derivative \(e^{-2t}\). No calculation produces the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). Assigning a \(\kappa=-2\) normal exponent at the junction would be an additional input.

The graph Laplacian/flow generator is an orthogonal direct sum of prime-loop modes subject to a common boundary condition. The spectrum contains one full circle-type family for each \(p\), with multiplicity growing with the number of primes under a cutoff. The common junction can impose one scalar matching relation, but it cannot remove the infinite family of loop modes while retaining every prime orbit.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For a nonzero compactly supported \(\phi\), every prime loop whose \(\log p\) lies in the support contributes a nonzero loop trace. The sum of the absolute trace norms has the established prime-channel divergence. A single junction constraint is finite rank and cannot make a non-trace-class direct sum trace class, because trace-class operators form an ideal and finite-rank corrections do not remove divergent singular-value mass. Therefore ordinary trace class fails.

Its local modular factors are assigned per loop, the archimedean kernel is not derived, and the prime-channel trace diverges.

## Candidate 149: Supersymmetric dynamically coupled prime bouquet

\begin{pmatrix}
A&B\\
-B^\ast&A^\ast

with \(A\) diagonal in the prime labels and \(B\) the canonical rank-one all-prime coupling determined by the normalized finite-adelic Haar vector. Define the leafwise differential \(D\) by \(D b_p=f_p\) on the junction-coupled edge space and \(D^2\) as the graph Laplacian. The alternating transfer supertrace is intended to cancel mixed boson/fermion trajectories while retaining one-letter prime cycles. Each bosonic prime edge carries the finite-adelic factor \(p^{-1}\).

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The two-channel graph replaces the compact local transversal by a connected global edge bundle. The junction scattering matrix replaces the one-prime scale \(q\). The supersymmetric differential is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv): mixed channels should be paired into \(D\)-exact states, leaving a spectrally smaller cohomology while preserving global coupling.

The coupled junction permits a trajectory to leave \(C_2\), enter \(C_3\), and return, so mixed prime words are geometrically present. A mixed path such as \(C_2C_3\) has length \(\log2+\log3\). Supersymmetry may cancel its bosonic and fermionic contributions if the pairing is exact, but this is an algebraic supertrace cancellation, not removal from the orbit set. Gate 1 requires the nontrivial primitive closed-orbit contributions themselves to be exactly prime-indexed after the alternating cohomological trace, so an absolute cancellation theorem is required.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The bosonic prime edge has \(p^{-1}\) finite-adelic Jacobian, while the fermionic partner has the same geometric normal map. The junction unitary changes channel amplitudes but not the Jacobian. A mixed path carries the product of edge factors, and its boson/fermion cancellation does not produce the positive prime-power coefficient unless the supertrace pairing is proved compatible with every iterate.

The common junction is a candidate infinite-place vertex, but the unitary scattering matrix has no specified transverse derivative corresponding to \(e^{-2t}\). The supersymmetric differential is discrete/graph-theoretic and does not derive \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). Adding a real boundary supermultiplet would be an external ingredient.

The boson/fermion cancellation can reduce the cohomology to the kernel and cokernel of \(D\), but the rank-one global coupling does not prove that this cohomology has finite spectral multiplicity. The surviving one-letter prime modes still form an infinite family. If mixed modes are \(D\)-exact, this is a nontrivial cohomological theorem; if they survive in the kernel, the mixed-orbit obstruction remains.

Before taking cohomology, each prime edge contributes a full circle-type transfer family, so ordinary trace class fails by the established prime-channel divergence. Passing to supersymmetric cohomology could remove modes only if the cancellation is implemented by a trace-class Hodge projection and the even and odd transfer operators are separately trace class. No such estimate is available. A formal difference of divergent bosonic and fermionic traces is not an ordinary trace-class supertrace, and finite-rank junction coupling cannot repair the divergent prime-edge ideal.

## Consolidation 150: Separation-versus-coupling dichotomy

### MOST FREQUENT FAILURE CLASS

The dominant failure since Consolidation 140 is the orbit/trace dichotomy. Candidates 141--149 repeatedly faced the same structural choice: prevent mixed prime returns by separating place sectors, or connect the sectors and thereby create mixed returns. Attempts to remove mixed returns algebraically introduced conditional supertrace cancellation and did not establish ordinary trace class.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

**Partial no-go theorem for prime-labelled graph, semigroup, and groupoid suspensions.** Let a flow be generated by prime-labelled return mechanisms with primitive lengths \(\log p\), and suppose the flow has one global state space. Assume the finite prime returns are represented by invariant transition channels and the transfer is an ordinary trace-class operator for every compactly supported positive-time test.

If no transition path can move from a \(p\)-channel to a distinct \(q\)-channel, then the recurrent flow decomposes into invariant prime sectors. Its transfer contains the prime-channel direct-sum contribution, whose trace norm diverges as the support grows; finite-rank or bounded global coupling cannot repair this divergence while retaining all coefficients \(\log p\).

If a transition path can move from a \(p\)-channel to a distinct \(q\)-channel, then concatenating the two return paths produces a closed mixed return, unless the geometry contains a further obstruction. Consequently the primitive closed-orbit set is larger than the rational primes.

If mixed returns are present geometrically but are removed only by an alternating differential, Möbius projector, orientation projection, or formal boson/fermion cancellation, then Gate 1 still requires independent trace-class bounds on the parity components and a proof that the cancellation is exact for every test function. A difference of divergent or merely distributional traces is not an ordinary trace-class supertrace.

Therefore, within this stated class, one cannot simultaneously obtain prime-only primitive orbit geometry, dynamic cross-prime coupling, and ordinary trace class by separation, finite-rank coupling, or formal cancellation alone.

### STATUS

**PARTIAL.** The dichotomy is proved for the stated graph/semigroup/groupoid channel model: no cross-channel transition gives sector decomposition, while cross-channel concatenation gives mixed returns. The conclusion about all possible geometric cancellation mechanisms remains open because a new cohomological mechanism might make mixed returns genuinely null while retaining absolute trace class.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The dichotomy is forced by the Gate 1 requirements, not by arbitrary candidate naming. Prime-only primitive orbits require restricting the recurrent language; ordinary trace class requires suppressing infinitely many modes; global arithmetic geometry requires some cross-place structure. The candidates tested different implementations of exactly these requirements. The theorem is not a universal no-go for all foliated dynamical systems, because a mechanism outside the channel/suspension class could evade the dichotomy.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The finite-field transversal \(\mathbb Z_p^m\) cannot simply be replaced by:

- a full global quotient, because prime periods collapse;
- a valuation wall, because mixed words appear after inversion;
- a colored prime family, because the flow becomes direct-sum-like;
- a connected bouquet, because dynamic coupling creates mixed cycles;
- a supersymmetric or Möbius projector, because formal cancellation does not establish ordinary trace class.

A viable replacement for Assumption (iv) must therefore do more than select modes: it must alter the primitive orbit category itself, making mixed returns null by an intrinsic geometric/cohomological relation while preserving prime loops and an absolutely trace-class transfer.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**SEARCH CONTINUES.** The separation-versus-coupling class is partially closed, but a universal Gate 1 no-go theorem has not been proved.

## Candidate 151: Homotopy-coherent prime 2-complex

The global 2-complex replaces the finite-field compact transversal and uses its 2-cells as the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv). The prime loops replace the single scale \(q\). The one-letter loops \(e_2\) and \(e_3\) have intended primitive lengths \(\log2\) and \(\log3\), with first iterates \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). The mixed loop \(e_2e_3\) is attached as the boundary of a 2-cell, so it is null in cellular homology. This achieves the desired homological cancellation at the chain level.

However, the mixed loop remains a geometric closed path in the underlying flow. It disappears only after passing to homology, not from the primitive orbit set itself. Gate 1 asks for the alternating cohomological trace, so a homological cancellation could in principle be relevant, but it requires a proved trace identity showing that every mixed orbit contribution is paired exactly with the attached 2-cell contribution.

The prime edge factors are \(p^{-1}\). The 2-cell boundary carries the product factor \((pq)^{-1}\) if its transverse density is induced multiplicatively. The local density of higher cells is an additional geometric choice unless derived from a global determinant line.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

To cancel a mixed orbit in the alternating trace, the 1-cell transfer and the 2-cell transfer must each be ordinary trace class, with equal and opposite mixed contributions. The number of attached mixed 2-cells grows at least quadratically in the number of primes under a length cutoff. The resulting absolute trace norms are not shown to be summable. No trace-class Hodge projection onto the proposed homology is established.

## Candidate 152: Adelic cubical resolution with product-formula cell measures

### CONSTRUCTION

w(S)=\prod_{p\in S}p^{-1}.
\]
Add one real boundary coordinate for the infinite place and impose the global product formula on the total adelic cell measure. Define the flow by translation in the logarithmic roof coordinate, with prime one-cells of length \(\log p\), and take the completed weighted cellular de Rham complex as leafwise cohomology. Mixed prime cells are intended to be boundaries in the cubical complex, while prime one-cells remain generators.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The cubical finite-adelic complex replaces \(\mathbb Z_p^m\) by a simultaneous normal-crossings structure at all finite places. Its coordinate scale is the valuation roof \(\log p\). The weighted cellular boundary is the proposed replacement for Assumption (iv), because it gives a canonical Hodge complex and fixes higher-cell measures directly from the product of local Haar Jacobians rather than by fitting coefficients.

The prime one-cell in the \(p\)-direction gives intended primitive length \(\log p\), and its first iterate has length \(2\log p\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). A mixed \(p,q\) cell is a two-dimensional boundary cell rather than a primitive one-dimensional orbit, so the cubical geometry suppresses mixed loops at the orbit-category level. This is an improvement over graph models: mixed products are encoded as higher cells, not as separate primitive loops.

However, the actual suspension flow on the total cell complex still has boundary trajectories and corner returns. Unless the flow is restricted to the one-skeleton, the higher-cell corners generate additional recurrent strata. Restricting to the one-skeleton loses the cubical homotopy mechanism; keeping all cells requires a trace formula accounting for their boundary contributions.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The cell measure is canonically \(w(S)=\prod_{p\in S}p^{-1}\), and a prime one-cell has the desired \(p^{-1}\) factor. The product formula supplies the reciprocal real-place factor globally. This is the strongest modular derivation in the current search, but it gives a cell measure, not yet the Lefschetz determinant of a closed orbit. The relation between cubical boundary orientation and the required positive iterate sign remains unproved.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The added real boundary coordinate supplies an infinite-place direction, but no canonical stationary point has been specified. A real boundary corner can be designated as stationary, yet its transverse derivative and local cell measure are not determined by the product formula alone. In particular, the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\) and exponent \(-2\) are not derived.

The weighted cubical complex has one \(k\)-cell for every finite prime subset of size \(k\). Its generating function for total cell mass is formally

The divergence of \(\prod_p(1+p^{-1})\) is an explicit obstruction: the canonical higher-cell measure is not summable. For a nonzero compactly supported test, the corresponding weighted transfer has non-summable total cell trace norm unless an additional damping exponent \(p^{-1-\varepsilon}\) or a finite-prime cutoff is imposed. Both alter the exact \(p^{-m}\) coefficients or introduce a cutoff, violating Gate 1. Alternating cubical cancellation cannot be used as a substitute for absolute trace class.
