The finite-adelic valuation directions, cubical finite-subset complex, product-formula measure, local Haar factors, logarithmic prime roofs, real boundary direction, cubical differential, and weighted Hodge complex. No zero locations are used.

The real boundary does not derive the \(\kappa=-2\) kernel, and the full cell flow has unresolved corner/boundary orbit contributions.

\[
d=\sum_p (1-T_p)\,\iota_{e_p},
\]
where \(T_p\) is the prime valuation return and \(\iota_{e_p}\) is contraction by the \(p\)-generator. The alternating cohomological transfer is the Euler-characteristic combination of exterior degrees. The determinant line and exterior grading are defined from the product formula, and the intended effect is that higher-prime subsets cancel in the Euler characteristic while the one-prime sectors retain the prime returns.

The prime generator \(e_p\) replaces the local finite-field transverse direction, and the exterior degree replaces the single scale \(q\). The one-generator sector retains intended primitive lengths \(\log2\) and \(\log3\), with iterates \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). However, the exterior algebra still contains one \(k\)-mode for every finite prime subset. The Euler characteristic can cancel alternating subset counts, but it does not remove those modes from the chain-level flow. Gate 1 requires ordinary trace-class operators on the actual cohomology/chain realization, not only cancellation of a formal Euler product.

\[
w(S)=\prod_{p\in S}p^{-1}.
\]
The exterior sign \((-1)^{|S|}\) supplies the Euler-characteristic sign, while the local Jacobians remain exact. Formally, the total signed mass is

\]
but this product tends to zero and is not an absolutely convergent trace expansion because \(\sum_p p^{-1}=\infty\). The Euler-characteristic cancellation is therefore conditional rather than an ordinary trace identity.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The compact solenoid has no distinguished archimedean boundary. A stable/unstable real factor could be appended, but its fixed point and exponent \(-2\) would be extra data, and the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\) is not forced.

### SPECTRUM

The Koopman operators of compact solenoid automorphisms have character spectra indexed by the dual discrete module. The joint spectrum contains infinitely many characters and composition sectors. Stable/unstable Hodge projection may remove some modes but does not prove a one-dimensional prime-periodic sector or compact resolvent for the global generator.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Compactness of \(Y\) does not imply trace class for Koopman transfers. The natural-extension automorphisms preserve Haar measure and have unitary Koopman operators with infinite multiplicity. Smearing in a suspension roof does not remove the character multiplicity. A finite-dimensional cohomological quotient would have to be imposed or proved via a new Hodge theorem; without it ordinary trace class fails.

## Consolidation 160: Compact-correspondence versus invertible-automorphism dichotomy

### MOST FREQUENT FAILURE CLASS

The dominant failure since Consolidation 150 is the compactness/orbit dichotomy. Candidates 151--159 tried to alter the primitive orbit category through higher cells, exterior complexes, canonical Dirichlet forms, compact suspensions, solenoids, and compact automorphisms. The common issue is that compactness and exact Haar factors are available, but prime correspondences are not invertible flows; making them invertible produces composite/inverse periodic data and infinite character multiplicity.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

**Partial no-go theorem for compact inverse-limit arithmetic mechanisms.** Consider a compact global arithmetic object \(Y\) equipped with prime-labelled maps \(T_p\), Haar-type local factors \(p^{-1}\), and a flow or transfer obtained directly from these maps.

If some \(T_p\) is a noninvertible covering or correspondence, then it is not itself a primitive closed orbit of an invertible flow. Its natural extension makes it invertible, but the generated semigroup/group contains compositions \(T_pT_q\) and inverse words \(T_pT_q^{-1}\). Unless the geometry supplies an additional intrinsic relation eliminating every such composition, the primitive periodic data are not indexed only by primes.

If the maps are instead native invertible automorphisms on one compact object, then the joint action contains the subgroup generated by all \(T_p^{\pm1}\). Periodic points and character modes are indexed by that joint arithmetic action, not by the individual generators. In particular, the Koopman representation contains the dual character spectrum of the compact object; without a proved finite-dimensional invariant quotient, compactness of \(Y\) does not imply ordinary trace class.

If the construction removes the composite modes by selecting a prime-only projection, exterior/Koszul quotient, or harmonic rank-one sector, then Gate 1 requires a geometric Hodge theorem proving that projection is the actual reduced leafwise cohomology and that the resulting transfer has the exact Lefschetz coefficients. An imposed projection or formal Euler cancellation is insufficient.

Therefore, within this compact inverse-limit/correspondence/automorphism class, one cannot obtain prime-only primitive closed-orbit data, exact local Haar factors, and ordinary trace-class global cohomology merely from compactness and invertible completion.

### STATUS

**PARTIAL.** The argument is complete for direct-limit solenoids, compact covering correspondences, and compact commuting automorphism systems of the tested type. It does not rule out a new compact object with an intrinsic cohomological quotient that is not a prime-only projection in the above sense.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

The dichotomy is forced by the Gate 1 requirement that prime data arise from a flow, not merely from correspondences, and that trace operators be ordinary trace class. The candidates varied the compact geometry and cohomological mechanism, but all retained the basic choice between noninvertible prime maps and invertible joint arithmetic dynamics. The result is therefore a structural constraint on this class, not a universal no-go theorem.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

A viable replacement for the finite-field transversal must avoid both failure branches:

- It cannot be only a compact prime correspondence, because correspondence degree is not a closed-flow period.
- It cannot be completed to a generic compact automorphism family, because joint compositions and character multiplicities appear.
- It cannot simply project onto selected prime modes, because the projection must be a geometrically derived reduced cohomology.
- It must supply an intrinsic relation that changes the primitive orbit category while preserving exact local Jacobians and finite smeared multiplicity.

The unresolved target is therefore a compact or locally compact arithmetic object whose cohomology is defined by a canonical differential relation that is part of the flow geometry itself, not an after-the-fact spectral filter.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**SEARCH CONTINUES.** The compact correspondence/automorphism class is partially closed. No universal no-go theorem has been proved.

## Candidate 161: Derived prime-place category with vanishing cross-prime tensor products

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \(\mathcal C\) be the derived category generated by one arithmetic place object \(E_p\) for each rational prime and one archimedean object \(E_\infty\). Impose the canonical arithmetic tensor rule
\[
E_p\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_q\simeq0\quad(p\neq q),
\]
mirroring the vanishing of distinct finite-place tensor products, while \(E_p\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_p\) carries the \(p\)-adic normal scaling with Jacobian \(p^{-1}\). Define a dg flow category by assigning \(E_p\) roof degree \(\log p\), with morphism complexes generated by the derived endomorphisms of each \(E_p\). Use the total derived Hochschild/de Rham complex as leafwise cohomology, and take the categorical Euler trace of the flow. The cross-prime tensor vanishing is intended to make mixed prime returns zero intrinsically.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The derived endomorphism category of \(E_p\) replaces \(\mathbb Z_p^m\); its self-tensor scale replaces \(q\). The vanishing cross-prime tensor rule replaces Assumption (iv) as an intrinsic differential relation: it removes mixed tensor paths before forming the trace, rather than by a numerical projection.

### ORBITS

Each \(E_p\) has intended primitive length \(\log p\), with first iterate \(2\log p\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). Cross-prime composites vanish categorically, so no \(pq\) mixed orbit survives in the derived tensor category. This is a genuine categorical elimination of mixed products.

However, the resulting category is a disjoint collection of prime-place blocks: there are no nonzero morphism complexes between \(E_p\) and \(E_q\). The flow is therefore not one connected global dynamical system; it is a categorical direct sum indexed by primes.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The self-tensor \(E_p\) can carry the local \(p^{-1}\) Jacobian, but the vanishing cross-prime tensor rule does not derive a common global Radon--Nikodym structure. The factors are local block data. The categorical Euler trace sees them only after choosing a trace on each block and summing over \(p\).

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The object \(E_\infty\) can be included as a separate generator, but no canonical derived endomorphism complex has been specified whose trace gives exponent \(-2\) and kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). Cross-prime tensor vanishing does not construct the infinite-place local term.

### SPECTRUM

The Hochschild/de Rham spectrum is a direct sum of prime-place spectra because all cross morphisms vanish. Even if each \(E_p\) contributes only one harmonic class, the global category retains one independent block per prime. Any attempt to couple the blocks reintroduces nonzero cross-prime tensors and therefore mixed categorical paths.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The categorical trace decomposes as a sum of prime-block traces. For compactly supported \(\phi\), only finitely many prime lengths occur, but each block's trace-class property and the global cohomological realization are not established. In the full unsmeared categorical completion, the sum of block trace norms has the same prime-channel issue as a direct sum. A finite-rank global coupling cannot repair this without changing the vanishing tensor rule or the exact trace.

### INPUTS

The derived prime-place objects, derived tensor product, cross-prime vanishing rule, local self-tensor Jacobians, roof degrees \(\log p\), dg flow category, Hochschild/de Rham complex, and categorical Euler trace. No zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, ARCHIMEDEAN, CONNECTED-GEOMETRY).** Cross-prime tensor vanishing intrinsically removes mixed categorical paths, but it does so by making the prime-place category disconnected. The resulting trace is a prime-indexed direct sum, the global ordinary trace-class realization is not proved, and the archimedean term remains unconstructed.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Categorical orthogonality/direct-sum obstruction:** making mixed prime products vanish intrinsically removes cross-prime geometry and leaves independent prime blocks; categorical orthogonality does not supply a connected global trace mechanism.

## Consolidation 170: Composition-law trilemma for prime returns

### MOST FREQUENT FAILURE CLASS

The dominant failure since Consolidation 160 is the composition-law problem. Candidates 161--169 tried categorical vanishing, derived exactness, unified groupoids, prime-only subgroupoids, and nonmultiplicative hub resets. They expose three exhaustive behaviors for a prime-labelled return mechanism.

### NO-GO STATEMENT

**Partial no-go theorem for prime-labelled composition systems.** Suppose a Gate 1 candidate has one return mechanism for each rational prime \(p\), with primitive intended length \(\log p\), and the returns are represented by arrows, correspondences, or morphisms in a category/groupoid that supports a trace.

1. If the composition law is rational multiplication, then \(p\)- and \(q\)-returns compose to a \(pq\)-return, and inverse closure produces \(p/q\)-returns. The primitive orbit category is not prime-only.

2. If the composition law makes distinct prime returns orthogonal or noncomposable, then the system decomposes into prime sectors. The resulting trace is direct-sum-like; coupling only through an external linear relation does not make the geometric returns connected. If all prime sectors are retained with full local dynamics, the established trace-class obstruction remains.

3. If a reset or nonmultiplicative composition law is used to prevent cross-prime composition, then a single prime arrow is not itself a closed orbit unless the endpoint is identified with the starting point. That identification makes different prime arrows composable again. If the actual closed path includes the inverse reset, its Radon--Nikodym factors multiply to \(1\), so the required \(p^{-m}\) factor is lost.

4. If mixed compositions are retained geometrically but declared exact, null, or canceled in a derived/supersymmetric complex, then ordinary Gate 1 trace class additionally requires separately trace-class chain operators and a canonical trace-compatible contraction. Formal homological cancellation does not suffice.

Thus, within the tested class of compositional arithmetic systems, prime-only primitive closed orbits, nontrivial cross-prime global geometry, exact local modular factors, and ordinary trace class cannot be obtained merely by choosing a composition law.

### STATUS

**PARTIAL.** The trilemma is complete for the explicitly listed composition behaviors and their direct categorical/graph/groupoid realizations. It does not exclude a new primitive-orbit notion in which composition is not represented by ordinary arrows but still has a canonical Lefschetz trace.

### SELECTION-BIAS AUDIT

This result is forced by the Gate 1 requirements: an orbit trace needs composition or iteration, prime labels must remain primitive, and the global object must be connected enough to have one trace system. The candidates varied how composition was implemented, not merely the notation. The theorem is nevertheless scoped, because an as-yet-unknown foliated geometry may have a more subtle orbit category than these arrow systems.

### CENTRAL QUESTION

The next viable mechanism cannot be a standard prime-labelled semigroup, groupoid, orthogonal categorical sum, or reset graph. It must define primitive closed orbits through a different geometric invariant—perhaps a foliation holonomy or an index class—such that mixed arithmetic compositions are not additional primitive orbits, yet the local Haar cocycle remains a genuine Lefschetz multiplier.

### CONSOLIDATION VERDICT

**SEARCH CONTINUES.** The standard composition-law class is partially closed; no universal Gate 1 no-go theorem has been established.

## Candidate 171: Prime holonomy index on an adelic foliation

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \(X\) be a connected adelic foliated space with a flat line bundle \(L\) whose holonomy around a closed leaf \(\gamma\) is a positive real number. Define the prime index class of a closed leaf by
\[
\operatorname{ind}(\gamma)=\log\operatorname{Hol}_L(\gamma).
\]
Construct the flat connection from the finite-adelic valuation one-form, so a local \(p\)-normal loop has holonomy \(p\), index \(\log p\), and Haar transverse Jacobian \(p^{-1}\). Define the flow and its reduced leafwise cohomology on the connected holonomy groupoid. Primitive orbit contributions are to be selected by the index spectrum rather than by prime-labelled arrows; a separate index-\(\log p\) class is intended to represent each prime.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The flat holonomy bundle replaces the local \(\mathbb Z_p^m\) transversal, and its connection holonomy replaces the single scale \(q\). The proposed Assumption (iv) analogue is the kernel of the flat connection on the unit-invariant harmonic sector. The key change is that primes are detected by holonomy indices, not by an explicitly named composition generator.

### ORBITS

The construction can assign a closed leaf with holonomy \(2\) and length \(\log2\), and one with holonomy \(3\) and length \(\log3\); their first iterates have lengths \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and intended sign \(+1\). But holonomy is multiplicative under concatenation:
\[
\operatorname{Hol}(\gamma_2\gamma_3)=6,
\qquad
\operatorname{ind}(\gamma_2\gamma_3)=\log2+\log3.
\]
Therefore the index spectrum detects products, not individual primes. Selecting only holonomy values that are prime is an arithmetic spectral filter, not a geometric primitive-orbit theorem. Conversely, if mixed concatenations are disallowed, the holonomy classes are disconnected or direct-sum-like.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The connection can derive \(p^{-1}\) as the inverse of the finite-adelic holonomy \(p\), giving a genuine cocycle. But the holonomy of a mixed path is the product \(pq\), and inverse paths have reciprocal holonomy. The index invariant therefore preserves the multiplicative-composition obstruction rather than removing it.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

A flat line bundle holonomy class has no stationary archimedean point. An archimedean connection may be added, but its local holonomy derivative is not forced to be \(-2\), and the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\) is not derived.

### SPECTRUM

The holonomy operator is diagonalized by characters of the flat line bundle and produces a continuous or character-valued spectrum. A prime-index subspace is not generally invariant under the holonomy algebra because products of prime holonomies are present. Restricting to the prime index spectrum is not a closed spectral calculus.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The holonomy trace can be distributionally organized by index values, but ordinary trace class requires a discrete invariant spectral sector. The prime-index filter is not an orthogonal invariant projection under multiplication of holonomies. If one uses the full holonomy spectrum, composite sectors and continuous multiplicity remain; if one filters to primes, the trace mechanism is imposed rather than geometrically derived.

### INPUTS

The connected adelic foliation, flat holonomy line bundle, finite-adelic valuation connection, holonomy index, unit-invariant harmonic sector, flow, and proposed archimedean connection. No zero locations are used.

## Candidate 172: Additive rotation index for prime-place returns

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \(X\) be a connected adelic suspension with a compact rotation coordinate \(\theta\in\mathbb T^{(\mathcal P)}\), one circle factor for each prime, and a finite-adelic normal coordinate. Define the prime return \(R_p\) to translate only the \(p\)-coordinate by one unit, with roof length \(\log p\), while the geometric index of a closed trajectory is its primitive rotation support
\[
\operatorname{supp}_{\mathrm{rot}}(\gamma)=\{p:\Delta\theta_p\neq0\}.
\]
This is nonmultiplicative as a label: a single-place trajectory has support \(\{p\}\), whereas a mixed trajectory has support of cardinality at least two. The finite-adelic normal map supplies \(p^{-1}\), and the flow cohomology is the support-filtered de Rham complex of the compact rotation suspension.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The prime rotation torus replaces the compact local transversal, while the support index replaces Assumption (iv). The finite-adelic normal coordinate keeps the local Haar factors. The key change is that the invariant distinguishes prime support combinatorially rather than through multiplicative holonomy.

### ORBITS

The \(p=2\) and \(p=3\) one-coordinate rotations have intended primitive lengths \(\log2\) and \(\log3\), with first iterates \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). A trajectory using both coordinates has support \(\{2,3\}\) and is declared non-prime by the index. However, the support index is not an invariant of the primitive orbit under iteration in the required sense: iterating a one-coordinate trajectory preserves support, but concatenating trajectories produces a legitimate mixed closed orbit in the connected torus. Removing mixed support classes is a spectral/chain projection, not a geometric elimination.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The \(p\)-normal finite-adelic direction supplies \(p^{-1}\). The rotation coordinate is Haar-preserving and contributes no Jacobian. The support filter changes which trajectories enter the trace but does not alter their Lefschetz multipliers. Thus the local factor exists, but the prime-only trace requires an additional support projection.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The compact rotation torus has no distinguished real boundary point. A real suspension coordinate can be added, but no stationary transverse map with derivative \(-2\) is forced. The kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\) is absent.

### SPECTRUM

The compact rotation torus has character spectrum indexed by finitely supported integer vectors. Single-coordinate characters are not invariant under the full transfer algebra: products of rotations generate all finitely supported vectors. A support-one projection is not an algebraic spectral subspace for the full connected action. The full character spectrum is infinite and has the same compact-automorphism multiplicity problem.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

Compact support in time does not make the full torus Koopman spectrum trace class; infinitely many character modes remain. Restricting to support-one modes gives a prime-indexed diagonal model with finite smeared trace, but that restriction is exactly the external prime filter the candidate was designed to avoid. No canonical Hodge projection from the rotation geometry produces it.

### INPUTS

The compact prime rotation torus, finite-adelic normal directions, prime return translations, support index, Haar measures, logarithmic roof lengths, and support-filtered de Rham complex. No zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(ORBIT-FILTER, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE).** The nonmultiplicative support index distinguishes single-place labels from mixed labels, but mixed trajectories remain in the connected flow and the support-one restriction is not flow invariant. The full rotation spectrum is non-trace-class, and the archimedean term is absent.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Nonmultiplicative-index/filter obstruction:** a support or winding index can label single-place trajectories without multiplicative collapse, but it cannot remove mixed geometric orbits or define an invariant prime-only spectral subspace.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 173 must make the single-place index part of the geometry's primitive-orbit definition, not a post hoc spectral filter. It must preserve the exact local Haar factor, obtain finite trace multiplicity, and derive the archimedean stationary sector.

## Candidate 173: Stratified single-place foliation

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \(X\) be a connected stratified space with strata
\[
X_p=Y_p\times\mathbb R
\]
for each prime \(p\), together with a common singular stratum \(X_\infty\). Each \(X_p\) carries a flow of period \(\log p\) and a finite-adelic normal coordinate with Haar factor \(p^{-1}\). The foliation is defined so that the support stratum \(X_p\) is an invariant leaf type: a trajectory entering \(X_p\) cannot move to \(X_q\) for \(q\neq p\). The strata meet only at \(X_\infty\), where the foliation has a prescribed singular tangency. Leafwise cohomology is the intersection/stratified de Rham cohomology with matching conditions at \(X_\infty\).

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

Each \(Y_p\) replaces the finite-field transversal, while the common singular stratum replaces the global arithmetic junction and the infinite place. The invariant stratum type replaces Assumption (iv): single-place support is built into the foliation itself, not a post hoc projector.

### ORBITS

The \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) strata carry primitive orbits of lengths \(\log2\) and \(\log3\), with first iterates \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). Because the strata are foliation-invariant, mixed prime trajectories do not exist. This achieves intrinsic single-place primitive geometry at the cost of making the prime strata dynamically disconnected. The singular stratum \(X_\infty\) does not provide a flow path that couples \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) without violating the invariant-stratum rule.

### MODULAR FACTORS

Each stratum has its own finite-adelic normal Jacobian \(p^{-1}\). These factors are intrinsic within \(X_p\), but there is no single global normal map whose restriction simultaneously produces all prime factors. The matching condition at \(X_\infty\) does not determine the individual stratum Jacobians.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The singular stratum \(X_\infty\) is intended to be the archimedean point, but its transverse cone and tangency have not been specified by an explicit local model. No derivation gives exponent \(-2\) or the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). Treating the singular stratum as such is a declaration, not a proof.

### SPECTRUM

The stratified cohomology contains one invariant prime sector per \(p\), coupled only by finite matching conditions at \(X_\infty\). The matching space is finite rank relative to the direct sum and cannot remove the independent prime modes. If the matching conditions eliminate them, the prime trace is lost; if they retain them, the spectrum remains direct-sum-like.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

For each fixed compactly supported \(\phi\), the direct sum of prime strata still has the established prime-channel trace behavior. The singular matching condition is finite rank and cannot repair a divergent/non-trace-class direct sum. Heat regularization of the strata returns to the heat-removal obstruction. Consequently ordinary trace class for the full stratified cohomology is not proved.

### INPUTS

The connected stratified space, prime invariant strata, finite-adelic normal measures, singular infinite-place stratum, stratified foliation, matching conditions, and leafwise cohomology. No zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN).** The candidate makes single-place primitivity intrinsic to the foliation, but this is exactly dynamic sector separation in stratified form. The common singular stratum does not provide global coupling, canonical common Jacobian, the archimedean kernel, or ordinary trace class.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Stratified-separation obstruction:** encoding prime support as an invariant foliation stratum removes mixed orbits intrinsically but leaves a direct-sum prime spectrum; a finite singular junction cannot supply the missing global trace mechanism.

## Candidate 174: Hilbert--Schmidt singular junction for prime strata

### CONSTRUCTION

Take the invariant prime strata \(X_p\) of Candidate 173 and add one infinite-dimensional singular stratum
\[
X_\infty=\ell^2(\mathcal P)\times\mathbb R
\]
at the common boundary. Couple the prime boundary value \(h_p|_{\partial X_p}\) to the \(p\)-th coordinate of \(X_\infty\) through the operator
\[
(Jh)_p=\frac{1}{1+\log p}\,h_p|_{\partial X_p}.
\]
The coupling \(J\) is Hilbert--Schmidt by the square-summability of \((1+\log p)^{-1}\) after the prescribed conductor normalization. The singular stratum carries a real flow and a boundary potential chosen from the product-formula normal coordinate. The prime strata remain invariant in the interior; cross-stratum interaction occurs only through \(X_\infty\). Leafwise cohomology is the domain of the coupled self-adjoint boundary problem.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The infinite-dimensional singular stratum replaces the finite-field compact transversal and the common finite matching junction. The Hilbert--Schmidt boundary operator replaces Assumption (iv), intended to couple infinitely many prime sectors while preserving compact trace interaction. The exact local prime normal factors remain on \(X_p\).

### ORBITS

The interior prime strata retain intended primitive lengths \(\log2,\log3\), with first iterates \(2\log2,2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). Since cross-stratum coupling occurs only through the singular boundary, a trajectory can travel from \(X_2\) into \(X_\infty\), then into \(X_3\), and return. Thus mixed prime paths are present unless the boundary condition is reflecting. If reflecting, the Hilbert--Schmidt coupling does not dynamically connect the prime strata and the direct-sum obstruction remains. If transmitting, mixed orbits return.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The local \(p^{-1}\) factors remain on the prime interiors. The boundary coupling \(J\) rescales amplitudes by \((1+\log p)^{-1}\), which is not a Haar Jacobian and changes the exact prime trace coefficients. Choosing a coupling with unit amplitude would destroy Hilbert--Schmidt summability. Thus the trace-class coupling scale conflicts with exact modular coefficients.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The singular stratum contains a real boundary flow, but its potential and endpoint condition are not canonically determined by the product formula. No proof gives derivative \(-2\) or the kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). The infinite-dimensional junction adds a boundary space, not the required stationary local model.

### SPECTRUM

The coupled boundary problem can have compact resolvent if the singular stratum has a confining generator, and the Hilbert--Schmidt boundary map is compact. But the prime trace modes are modified by the boundary coupling; with transmission, mixed eigenmodes appear, and with reflection, the prime sectors remain effectively independent. No spectral theorem gives both exact prime eigenvalues and dynamic global coupling.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The Hilbert--Schmidt boundary coupling is compact, but compact coupling does not make a non-trace-class direct sum trace class; trace-class ideals are stable under compact/trace-class perturbations only when the base operator already has the required class. If the boundary problem is independently trace class, its coupling coefficients alter the prime trace. Therefore one cannot simultaneously retain exact \(\log p\) prime coefficients, obtain genuine cross-prime dynamics, and use the Hilbert--Schmidt junction to repair trace class.

### INPUTS

The invariant prime strata, infinite-dimensional singular boundary stratum, Hilbert--Schmidt coupling \(J\), finite-adelic local normal maps, boundary flow, product-formula potential, and coupled leafwise boundary complex. No zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(TRACE, MODULAR, ORBITS, ARCHIMEDEAN).** An infinite-dimensional junction can be compactly coupled, but transmitting coupling creates mixed prime paths, reflecting coupling preserves the direct-sum obstruction, and Hilbert--Schmidt weights change the exact local trace factors. The archimedean stationary term remains un-derived.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Compact-coupling/exact-coefficient obstruction:** a compact infinite-dimensional junction can connect prime strata only by altering amplitudes; exact Haar/Lefschetz coefficients and genuine cross-prime dynamics cannot both be retained.

## Candidate 175: Derived quotient by the mixed-path ideal

### CONSTRUCTION

Let \(\mathcal A\) be the path algebra of the connected prime-return groupoid, with one degree-zero generator \(a_p\) for each prime return and cross-prime morphisms \(a_{pq}\). Let \(I_{\mathrm{mix}}\) be the two-sided ideal generated by every composable path containing two distinct prime labels. Define the derived quotient
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prime}}=\mathcal A/\!^{\mathbf L} I_{\mathrm{mix}},
\]
using the canonical bar resolution of \(I_{\mathrm{mix}}\). Single-prime powers \(a_p^m\) survive, while every mixed word is zero in the quotient. Equip \(a_p\) with roof length \(\log p\), finite-adelic factor \(p^{-1}\), and form the quotient's Hochschild/de Rham cohomology as the leafwise complex. The quotient is intended to preserve nonzero cross-prime morphisms at degree one while making all mixed composites null intrinsically.

### COMPARISON TO THE WORKING MODEL

The connected path algebra replaces the finite-field transversal; the derived mixed ideal replaces Assumption (iv). Unlike Candidate 161, cross-prime morphisms are retained, and only their composites are killed. The quotient is intended to change the primitive orbit category without decomposing the object into prime blocks.

### ORBITS

The surviving \(a_2\) and \(a_3\) loops have intended primitive lengths \(\log2\) and \(\log3\), with first iterates \(2\log2\) and \(2\log3\), multiplicity one and sign \(+1\). Mixed words such as \(a_2a_3\) vanish in the quotient, so the quotient orbit algebra has prime-only primitive words.

However, a two-sided ideal quotient is algebraic rather than geometric: the mixed path remains a path in the original groupoid and is removed only after passing to the quotient. The derived bar resolution reintroduces the killed paths as higher homological generators. To establish a geometric Lefschetz trace, one must prove that the entire derived ideal contribution cancels in an absolutely trace-class way.

### MODULAR FACTORS

The prime generators retain local factors \(p^{-1}\). The mixed ideal generators and their bar-resolution homotopies have no canonically specified Haar densities. If they are assigned zero weight because the ideal is killed, the quotient is a non-geometric algebraic deletion. If they receive induced product weights, the higher derived complex reproduces the mixed-cell divergence of Candidates 151--153.

### ARCHIMEDEAN POINT

The quotient has no intrinsic infinite-place object. An \(E_\infty\) generator can be added, but no relation produces the stationary exponent \(-2\) or kernel \((1-e^{-2t})^{-1}\). The mixed ideal does not determine the archimedean term.

### SPECTRUM

The quotient algebra has one-prime word spectrum formally, but the derived quotient carries higher Tor/bar groups generated by the mixed ideal. If these higher groups are retained, mixed multiplicities return; if they are collapsed, the collapse is a non-derived algebraic projection. No canonical compact-resolvent/Hodge theorem identifies the desired reduced spectrum.

### TRACE CLASS AND NORM

The quotient's formal prime transfer has finite compact-test trace, but an ordinary trace on the original foliated/groupoid object must account for the ideal resolution. The bar terms have infinitely many mixed generators, and no absolute trace-class estimate is available. Declaring the ideal invisible is equivalent to dropping non-trace-class terms by hand. Thus the algebraic quotient does not supply a valid Gate 1 trace.

### INPUTS

The connected prime path algebra, mixed-path two-sided ideal, derived quotient, bar resolution, prime roof lengths, finite-adelic local factors, and Hochschild/de Rham trace complex. No zero locations are used.

### VERDICT

**FAIL(GEOMETRIC-REALIZATION, MODULAR, ARCHIMEDEAN, TRACE).** The derived quotient gives a clean algebraic prime-only orbit algebra while retaining degree-one cross-prime morphisms. But mixed paths are removed algebraically rather than geometrically, and the derived resolution recreates their trace-class problem. The archimedean sector is absent.

### FAILURE CLASS

**Ideal-quotient deletion obstruction:** killing mixed paths by a two-sided ideal preserves a formal prime-only algebra but does not remove the paths from the geometric trace; the derived resolution carries the missing terms back.

### NEXT CONSTRAINT

Candidate 176 must realize the mixed-path ideal as an actual geometric null foliation or contractible leaf family with a separately trace-class quotient map. It must derive all ideal measures and the archimedean stationary sector from the same object, without declaring mixed paths zero algebraically.
